- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Autotuner → Product-Build Linkage (operator runbook)
2	
3	**What this covers.** How to make `compile.py`'s autotuned launch parameters
4	ACTIVE in the shipped `grokking_optimizers/_ops*.so` — produce winners, rebuild
5	so the per-TU flags are baked in, verify they actually landed, and re-run the
6	parity + roofline gates against the tuned binary.
7	
8	**Background — lever (b).** The `compile.py` JIT autotuner builds and times
9	kernel variants and picks a winner per `(optimizer, model, arch)`. Historically
10	that winner only reached a header that nothing on the install path included, so
11	the product `.so` shipped the in-header defaults — the autotuner was
12	decorative. The linkage now is:
13	
14	```
15	compile.py build_jit  --(write-on-win, atomic)-->  grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json
16	                                                          |
17	pip install -e .  /  ./build.sh                           v
18	   setup.py TunedBuildExtension  --reads JSON, injects per-TU nvcc flags-->  _ops*.so
19	```
20	
21	The five SAFE per-TU dims are applied: `-DSG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE`,
22	`-DSG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH`, `-DSG_TUNED_UNROLL`, `-DSG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH`, and
23	`--maxrregcount=N` (only when N>0). They go onto each optimizer's CUDA TUs
24	(`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/launch_<opt>.cu` and the megakernel cells
25	`csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu`). The per-optimizer kernel header
26	`kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh` is `#include`d by `launch_<opt>.cu`, so flags on
27	the launcher TU reach the kernel body. Bindings (`*.cpp`), model-only TUs
28	(`models/<model>.cu`), and common/header TUs get **no** per-optimizer flags and
29	keep their in-header defaults. (`cluster_shape` and the feature macros — TMA /
30	WGMMA / fp8 / swizzle — are component-scoped and riskier; they are phase-2 and
31	are **not** emitted by this pass.)
32	
33	> If `_kernel_tuned.json` is absent the build is **byte-identical to before**:
34	> every kernel uses its `#ifndef SG_TUNED_*` default (block 256 / vec 4 /
35	> unroll 1 / async_depth 2; nvcc's own register allocator). A one-line notice
36	> is printed.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 0. Prerequisites
41	
42	- A GPU host (the JIT autotuner builds + times real kernels). Steps 1 is
43	  GPU-bound; steps 2–4 only need a CUDA toolchain (`FORCE_CUDA=1` lets the
44	  build configure without a visible device).
45	- `ninja` on PATH (the injection hook patches torch's ninja writer; the build
46	  already requires `use_ninja=True`).
47	- The repo installed editable at least once (so the extension build tree
48	  exists): `FORCE_CUDA=1 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`.
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 1. Produce winners → `grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json`
53	
54	Run the JIT autotuner **once per optimizer** (optionally per model). Each run
55	read-merge-writes its winner into the canonical JSON, so 11 sequential runs
56	accumulate 11 entries under the arch key.
57	
58	```bash
59	# One optimizer (sm_90 / Hopper). Repeat for each of the 11.
60	python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \
61	    --optimizer adamw --model decoder --arch sm_90 \
62	    --cache build/.compile_cache.json \
63	    --jit-only --mode bayesian --bayesian-trials 300
64	```
65	
66	Optimizers: `adamw grokadamw grokfast lion looksam muon neuralgrok prodigy
67	supergrok11 supergrok15 supergrok2`. Models (short): `decoder vit mamba`.
68	
69	> **One winner per `(arch, optimizer)` — model is LAST-WINS.** The JSON schema
70	> is `{arch: {optimizer: {...}}}` (no model dimension), so tuning the same
71	> optimizer on a *second* model overwrites the first, and that single winner is
72	> applied to ALL of that optimizer's TUs — its `launch_<opt>.cu` AND every
73	> `mega_<model>_<opt>` megakernel cell across all models. If you tune `decoder`
74	> then `vit` for `adamw`, only `vit`'s `adamw` winner survives. Pick the model
75	> whose launch params you want shipped (the `"model"` field in each entry
76	> records which sweep produced it).
77	
78	A convenience loop:
79	
80	```bash
81	for opt in adamw grokadamw grokfast lion looksam muon \
82	           neuralgrok prodigy supergrok11 supergrok15 supergrok2; do
83	  python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \
84	      --optimizer "$opt" --model decoder --arch sm_90 \
85	      --cache build/.compile_cache.json --jit-only --mode bayesian
86	done
87	```
88	
89	> **Run optimizers SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel processes.** The exporter's
90	> write is atomic (tmp + `os.replace`), so a reader never sees a half-written
91	> file — but it is read-merge-write, so two concurrent per-optimizer
92	> *processes* can clobber each other's just-written entry. One process at a
93	> time (the loop above) is safe. A failed JSON write is a loud warning in the
94	> compile report and **never** fails the tuning run; the winner is still in the
95	> compile cache and `tuned_configs.h`.
96	
97	Confirm the JSON was written and looks sane:
98	
99	```bash
100	python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json'));\
101	import pprint;pprint.pprint({k:sorted(v) for k,v in d.items() if k!='_meta'});\
102	print('meta:',d.get('_meta'))"
103	```
104	
105	Schema (canonical, short arch key):
106	
107	```json
108	{
109	  "sm_90": {
110	    "adamw": {"block":256,"vec":4,"unroll":1,"async_depth":2,
111	              "maxrregcount":0,"model":"decoder"},
112	    "supergrok2": {"block":128,"vec":2,"unroll":4,"async_depth":3,
113	                   "maxrregcount":96,"model":"decoder"}
114	  },
115	  "_meta": {"timestamp":"…","source":"grokking_optimizers.compile.build_jit",
116	            "last_optimizer":"supergrok2","last_arch":"sm_90",
117	            "compile_py_version_hash":"…"}
118	}
119	```
120	
121	---
122	
123	## 2. Rebuild — bake the tuned flags into `_ops*.so`
124	
125	A plain rebuild now consumes the JSON automatically (no special flag — the old
126	`./build.sh --autotune` two-pass flow was removed; see §5):
127	
128	```bash
129	# editable rebuild (FORCE_CUDA=1 if no visible GPU on the build host)
130	FORCE_CUDA=1 TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0a" \
131	    pip install -e . --no-build-isolation -v
132	# or:  ./build.sh
133	```
134	
135	Watch for the build-time notice. With a JSON present you should see lines like:
136	
137	```
138	  [tuned-inject] injected per-TU tuned flags into N CUDA TU(s) in build.ninja.
139	```
140	
141	With no JSON you should instead see:
142	
143	```
144	  [tuned-inject] no _kernel_tuned.json found; building with in-header kernel defaults …
145	```
146	
147	---
148	
149	## 3. Verify the flags actually landed
150	
151	The autotuner's own acceptance criterion: the flags must be in `build.ninja`.
152	
153	```bash
154	NINJA=$(ls build/temp.*/build.ninja | head -1)
155	grep -cE 'SG_TUNED'      "$NINJA"   # expect NONZERO now (was 0 — decorative)
156	grep -cE 'maxrregcount'  "$NINJA"   # nonzero iff some winner had maxrregcount>0
157	# See exactly which TUs were overridden (per-build-statement cuda_post_cflags):
158	grep -nE 'cuda_post_cflags = .*SG_TUNED' "$NINJA"
159	```
160	
161	Expected: one indented `cuda_post_cflags = … -DSG_TUNED_… ` override line
162	directly beneath each `build …/launch_<opt>.o: cuda_compile …` (and each tuned
163	`mega_…` cell). Each override carries the **full** base flag list (arch / `-O3`
164	/ fast-math) **plus** the tuned extras — the base flags must still be present
165	(a missing `compute_90a` / `--use_fast_math` would mean the override dropped
166	the base; that is a bug, not expected).
167	
168	Optionally confirm the emitted machine code reflects the register cap:
169	
170	```bash
171	# Recompile one tuned TU standalone with -Xptxas -v and read "registers".
172	scripts/compile_to_object.sh \
173	    csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/launch_supergrok2.cu \
174	    -DWITH_CUTLASS -Xptxas -v 2>&1 | grep -i 'registers'
175	```
176	
177	### CPU-only sanity (no GPU, no build)
178	
179	The injection logic has a CPU-only unit test that asserts the path→optimizer
180	mapping, the per-source flag computation, the `build.ninja` rewrite, the
181	export round-trip, and macro/header drift:
182	
183	```bash
184	python -m tuning.test_build_injection      # OK — all test groups passed.
185	```
186	
187	---
188	
189	## 4. Re-run parity + roofline against the tuned binary
190	
191	The tuned `.so` changes codegen (block size, vectorization, register pressure),
192	so re-gate correctness and re-measure performance.
193	
194	```bash
195	# Single-step fused-vs-reference numerical PARITY (H100):
196	PYTHONPATH=. python3 tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py
197	
198	# Reference-parity unit tests (the non-hw half runs anywhere):
199	PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py -q
200	
201	# Roofline / distance-to-roofline for every optimizer × model:
202	python -m tuning.roofline --models decoder,vit,mamba --steps 100
203	#   -> results/h100_grokking_race/roofline.{json,png}, ROOFLINE.md
204	```
205	
206	A tuned build must still PASS parity (the autotuner's winner selection already
207	gates on an on-device numerical oracle, so a winner that fails parity should
208	not have been written — treat any parity regression as a real bug). Roofline
209	closeness is expected to improve or hold for the tuned optimizers.
210	
211	---
212	
213	## 5. Notes / gotchas
214	
215	- **`./build.sh --autotune` is gone.** It called a nonexistent `autotune/tune.py`
216	  and staged the wrong header path. The autotuner is `grokking_optimizers.compile`;
217	  invoking `--autotune`/`--no-autotune` now prints this runbook's pointer and
218	  exits.
219	- **Secondary header.** `compile.py` still writes
220	  `csrc/algorithms/tuned_configs.h` (back-compat consumer). The **canonical**
221	  handoff to the product build is `_kernel_tuned.json`; the header is not on the
222	  install include path and is not what bakes flags into the `.so`.
223	- **Source of truth for the macros.** The macro names / defaults and the
224	  TU→optimizer mapping live in `grokking_optimizers/_tuned_inject.py`
225	  (`MACROS`, `optimizer_for_source`). `MACROS` is kept in lockstep with the
226	  header guards at `grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/adamw_sm90.cuh:31-41`; the
227	  unit test fails if they drift.
228	- **Future torch.** The injection hook monkeypatches
229	  `torch.utils.cpp_extension._write_ninja_file` (torch 2.4.x). If a future torch
230	  removes/renames it, the build prints a loud warning and falls back to a stock
231	  (in-header-defaults) build — it never hard-fails. Re-point the hook in
232	  `setup.py` (`TunedBuildExtension.build_extensions`) if that happens.
233	- **AMD / TPU.** The same JSON schema supports a `gfx942` arch key (the build
234	  arch key is chosen automatically). The pass currently emits the four
235	  `-DSG_TUNED_*` macros + `--maxrregcount`; AMD's equivalent VGPR cap
236	  (`-amdgpu-max-num-vgprs`) and TPU Pallas kwargs are out of scope for this
237	  per-TU nvcc pass.
238	```

197	### Stage 1A — SG2 bilevel backward (CSA/HCA hand-written adjoint)
198	
199	The saved-activation reverse-mode VJP through the SuperGrok2 CSA/HCA meta-net
200	(`input_proj+sort → CSA → HCA → GRU → PEER → smart_grad`). Implemented as a
201	REAL hand-written adjoint (NO autograd, NO autograd graph, NO throw). The
202	vendor-neutral math lives in `csrc/algorithms/supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h` and
203	is shared bit-for-bit by both backends:
204	
205	- **sm_90** (`grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/supergrok2_sm90.cuh`): the 4
206	  launchers (`launch_csa_hca_bilevel_fwd_save[_batched]`,
207	  `launch_csa_hca_backward[_batched]`) orchestrate the shared ATen adjoint
208	  (nvcc TU; ATen host orchestration, matching the existing `detail::` forward).
209	- **gfx942** (`grokking_optimizers/kernels/gfx942/supergrok2_gfx942.hip.hpp`):
210	  the same 4 launchers, ATen-based (host-compiler TU), per the AMD-native
211	  stance — Stage 5 lowers to raw HIP. The previous `csa_hca_bilevel_not_implemented`
212	  throws are GONE.
213	
214	**Kernels / stages written (reverse pipeline order):**
215	1. `smart_grad → expert_out`: `d_total = rescale * d_smart_grad`, split over heads.
216	2. PEER expert-MLP + product-key routing backward (`peer_head_backward`): VJP
217	   through the relu 2-layer expert MLP (atomic `index_add_` into
218	   `d_expert_{W1,b1,W2,b2}`), the `soft_a⊗soft_b` routing softmax (×10 temp),
219	   the top-k gather (scatter back to `d_scores_{a,b}`), and the query projection
220	   (`d_peer_query_Ws`, `d_prod_keys_{A,B}`) → `d_peer_input`.
221	3. GRU backward (`bilevel_backward_driver` §4): VJP through z/r/h̃ gates →
222	   `d_gru_{Wz,bz,Wr,br,Wh,bh}`; gates recomputed/saved from `gru_input + h_old`.
223	4. HCA dense-attention backward (`hca_forward`/`hca_backward`): softmax VJP +
224	   mean-pool compression scatter + window scatter → `d_hca_{q,k,v,out}_W`.
225	5. CSA sparse-attention backward (`csa_forward`/`csa_backward`): joint
226	   (selected-compressed ∪ window) softmax VJP, learned-pool compression VJP
227	   (`d_csa_compress_w` via softmax-pool), selected-entry + window scatter →
228	   `d_csa_{q,k,v,out}_W`. Lightning-indexer (`d_csa_idx_{DQ,UQ,K}`) handled per
229	   the discrete-topk stop-gradient note below.
230	6. input_proj + sort backward: accumulate `d_x_sorted` from the q/k/v projection
231	   adjoints of both blocks, then `d_input_proj_W[:,0]+=Σ d_x·g_sorted`,
232	   `[:,1]+=Σ d_x·s_sorted`, `d_input_proj_b+=Σ d_x` (sort handled by the
233	   `unsort/sort_idx` permutation on the saved contexts).
234	
235	**fwd_save save-set:** `x_sorted`, `sort_indices`, `csa_ctx`, `hca_ctx`,
236	`csa_saved_sel_idx`, `csa_saved_probs`, `hca_saved_probs`,
237	`csa_saved_denom`/`hca_saved_denom` (informational), plus the GRU
238	(`gru_input`, `gru_h_old`, `gru_z/r/h_tilde`) and PEER (`peer_input`,
239	`expert_indices`, `routing_weights`, `saved_z_hidden`, `saved_scores_{a,b}`,
240	`saved_top_{a,b}_idx`, `saved_soft_{a,b}`) adjoint tensors declared in the
241	bindings.cpp signature.
242	
243	**Checkpointing choice (honors `checkpoint_interval ≤ MAX_CKPT_INTERVAL=32`):**
244	fwd_save persists the heavy per-layer contexts (`csa_ctx`, `hca_ctx`) and the
245	softmax probs/sel sets; the backward RECOMPUTES the cheap per-row q/k/v +
246	indexer projections and the compressed K/V pools from the saved `x_sorted` via
247	the shared `csa_forward`/`hca_forward` helpers (i.e. layer-boundary activation

684	## Stage 4.1 — TMA descriptor / operator reuse (NVIDIA memory §3.1)
685	
686	**What changed (host-side, `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/mma.cuh`):** the generic
687	Sm90 collective GEMM launchers `sm90_run_gemm<>` and
688	`sm90_run_gemm_bt<,LayoutBT>` used to rebuild the CUTLASS `Gemm::Arguments`
689	(which materialises the Hopper TMA tensor-map descriptors via
690	`make_tma_copy_A/B_sm90` inside `to_underlying_arguments`), re-query the
691	workspace, and call `op.initialize()` on **every** invocation — even though
692	every optimizer step issues the **same** matmul shapes against the **same**
693	persistent buffers. They now route through a new shape-keyed host cache
694	`sm90_run_gemm_cached<Gemm,…>` that reuses the already-initialised operator.
695	
696	**Exactly what is cached / reused:**
697	- The **initialised `GemmUniversalAdapter` operator** (its `params_` member,
698	  which holds the baked TMA descriptors for A, B and the C epilogue map), plus
699	  the workspace pointer it was initialised with. On a hit we skip
700	  `make_cute_packed_stride` ×3, `Gemm::Arguments` construction,
701	  `can_implement`, `get_workspace_size`, and `initialize` (the call that runs
702	  the `cuTensorMapEncode`s) and re-launch via the supported
703	  `op.run(stream)` overload — CUTLASS documents this overload as
704	  "re-launch the same kernel without updating internal params"
705	  (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:545`).
706	- **Not** reused / not reached into: CUTLASS's internal TMA mainloop. There is
707	  no public "swap the descriptor's base pointer" API in 3.6, so we do not
708	  fabricate one. The real, measurable win is skipping the per-step
709	  Arguments+initialize (the cuTensorMapEncode path), which is what this does.
710	
711	**Cache key + eviction:**
712	- Key = `GemmCacheKey{ int M,N,K; const void* A; const void* B; void* C; }`.
713	  The key is **per-template-instantiation** (one static `Sm90GemmCache<Gemm>`
714	  each), so an FP16 vs BF16 GEMM, and a RowMajor-B vs ColumnMajor-B (Bᵀ) GEMM,
715	  never share a slot even at identical `(M,N,K,ptrs)`.
716	- Eviction: fixed-size **direct-mapped** table, `kSlots = 16`, slot =
717	  `FNV-1a(key) & (kSlots-1)`. A colliding signature evicts the resident entry
718	  and **`cudaFree`s its owned workspace** first → bounded memory, no leak. Only
719	  a handful of distinct signatures recur per run, so collisions are rare.
720	- Thread-safety: one `std::mutex` per `Sm90GemmCache<Gemm>`; the launcher is
721	  single-threaded per stream here but the lock makes concurrent host launchers
722	  safe and is off the hot path (host-side µs, dwarfed by the kernel).
723	
724	**Descriptor address-stability analysis (the load-bearing correctness
725	invariant):** a Hopper TMA tensor map encodes the tensor's **global base
726	address** (CUTLASS feeds `make_tensor(ptr_A, layout)` into
727	`make_tma_copy_A_sm90`, `sm90_mma_tma_gmma_ss_warpspecialized.hpp:212-226`),
728	plus its box/shape and strides. Strides here are a pure function of `(M,N,K)`
729	(row-major packed). Therefore a cached operator is **bit-for-bit equivalent**
730	to a freshly rebuilt one **iff** `(M,N,K)` and the A/B/C base pointers match —
731	which is precisely the cache key. The buffers served (optimizer param/m/v
732	state, model weights, and the grow-once FP32 output scratch) are allocated
733	**once** and keep the same address every step ⇒ stable key ⇒ hit. If any buffer
734	is reallocated to a new address, the key changes ⇒ **miss ⇒ full rebuild**, so a
735	stale descriptor can never be launched against a moved buffer (that would be
736	wrong results / an illegal access). Workspace: for this builder (1×1×1 cluster,
737	`kGemm`, no split-K) `get_workspace_size()==0` and the adapter only adds a
738	barrier workspace when `cute::size(ClusterShape)>1`, so served GEMMs use
739	`ws==nullptr`; even so each entry **owns** its workspace allocation so a cached
740	operator's params can never dangle into the shared grow-only
741	`sm90_get_workspace` buffer.
742	
743	**elect/mbarrier boundary note (honest):** §3.4's `elect_one_sync()` /
744	`Mbarrier` (`warp_specialize.cuh`, namespace `sg::sm90::wgs`) compose a
745	**hand-written** producer/consumer TMA staging loop. The CUTLASS GEMM is a
746	self-contained kernel that **owns** its TMA mainloop — there is no hand-written
747	TMA staging in `mma.cuh` into which a leader/barrier could be injected.
748	Pairing elect/mbarrier with TMA therefore belongs to the **Stage-6 megakernel's**
749	hand-written TMA path, **not** here. Stage 4.1 is the host-side
750	operator/descriptor cache only.

789	**What landed.** Replaced the `cluster_dsmem_reduce_sum` STUB (a bare warp
790	reduce that a comment admitted was a `cg::reduce` fallback) with a **real
791	Hopper thread-block-cluster DSMEM cross-CTA reduction**:
792	`sg::sm90::primitives::cluster_reduce_sum_f32_dsmem(val, cluster_smem_slot)` in
793	`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/primitives.cuh` (added as a NEW section after the
794	just-landed Stage 3.1 redux.sync and Stage 3.2 cp.async sections — neither was
795	touched). It is a **full multi-level tree** (§3.4) thread → warp → block(shared
796	tree) → cluster(DSMEM): each block publishes its block-reduced partial to its
797	OWN shared slot, then **every** block reads ALL peers' slots via
798	`cl.map_shared_rank` + `cl.sync()` and sums them (a full cluster-wide tree, not
799	a single-rank gather). Ordering is the critical part: **write own slot →
800	`cl.sync()` → read all peers → `cl.sync()`** (the second barrier prevents a
801	later reduction from clobbering the scratch mid-read). `cluster_size == 1` (the
802	common, no-cluster launch) short-circuits to the block reduce and **never
803	deadlocks** on a singleton-cluster barrier; pre-Hopper (`__CUDA_ARCH__ < 900`)
804	compiles to `block_reduce_sum_f32` with no cluster API referenced. The old
805	`cluster_dsmem_reduce_sum` in `csrc/common/utils.cuh` is **kept** as the

1602	## Stage 6 — 99 megakernels + solver
1603	
1604	Stage 6 builds the **L3 persistent-megakernel scaffolding + the dispatch
1605	wiring**: one uniform scheduler/barrier substrate per arch, one parameterized
1606	L3 megakernel that composes *(forward → backward → fused optimizer step)* in a
1607	single persistent launch, a Python code generator that instantiates that
1608	template per solver-chosen cell, and the `fused_step` dispatch that prefers a
1609	fused TU when present (§1.12). The Python feasibility solver
1610	(`grokking_optimizers/megakernel.py`) is the tier authority; the C++ generator
1611	mirrors its L3/L2/L1 model.
1612	
1613	### Scheduler / barrier design (§1.1–§1.4, §1.13, §1.14)
1614	
1615	Shared substrate — `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` (sm_90) and
1616	`csrc/fused/megakernel_common_hip.hip.hpp` (gfx942):
1617	
1618	- **§1.1 task-queue scheduler** — one global atomic `int` (`g_next_task`,
1619	  host-zeroed). Each persistent CTA/workgroup pulls parameter-tensor indices via
1620	  `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern). The
1621	  leader thread pulls per-CTA and broadcasts through shared/LDS (`next_block`).
1622	- **§1.2 work-stealing** — there is NO static partition: an idle core just keeps
1623	  calling `next()`, so a CTA that drains its tensor early grabs the next index.
1624	  The `atomicAdd` IS the steal.
1625	- **§1.3 SM/CU pinning** — `sm_id()` reads `%smid` (`mov.u32 %0, %%smid;`) on
1626	  sm_90; `cu_id()` reads `HW_ID` via `__builtin_amdgcn_s_getreg` on gfx942. The
1627	  host launches one persistent CTA per SM (gridDim.x = #SMs) / one workgroup per
1628	  CU, so that SM's/CU's optimizer-state slice stays L2-warm across the step.
1629	- **§1.4 hand-built grid barrier** — `GridBarrier` from two global atomics
1630	  (`arrived`, `generation`) + a **sense-reversing generation** counter, NO
1631	  cooperative launch (scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap). Each CTA
1632	  samples the generation, RELEASE-fences its phase writes, joins the arrival
1633	  count; the **last arriver** resets `arrived=0` and advances the generation;
1634	  everyone else spins on the generation; all then ACQUIRE-fence. The
1635	  sense-reversal is what makes it **reusable** without the classic
1636	  reset-vs-lap race (a fast CTA cannot lap a slow one because the consumer side
1637	  never touches `arrived` for reset — it waits on the generation advancing).
1638	- **§1.13 AMD scheduling note** — the gfx942 megakernel is **NOT**
1639	  warp-specialized (no TMA/WGMMA/setmaxnreg analog on CDNA3). It uses
1640	  **ping-pong / 4-wave-interleave** scheduling (4 wavefronts/SIMD take turns,
1641	  `sched_group_barrier` hints pin the MFMA-vs-VMEM interleave); latency is hidden
1642	  by occupancy, not a dedicated producer warp-group. The sm_90 megakernel uses
1643	  the §3.4 `wgs` warp-spec primitives (elect / mbarrier / setmaxnreg) for the
1644	  producer/consumer load→compute split.
1645	- **§1.14 fences** — explicit + minimal: exactly one release fence before the
1646	  arrival publish and one acquire fence after the generation advances at the
1647	  barrier; exactly one `fence.proxy.async` paired with the sm_90 mbarrier
1648	  hand-off. No loose fences.
1649	
1650	### Demo megakernel structure (§1.5–§1.8)
1651	
1652	`csrc/fused/sm_90/megakernel_demo.cu` and
1653	`csrc/fused/gfx942/megakernel_demo.hip.hpp` are ONE templated L3 megakernel
1654	`l3_megakernel<Model, Optimizer>` that composes three stages in a single
1655	persistent launch:
1656	
1657	```
1658	forward_stage<M>  ─GridBarrier─▶ (reset queue) ─GridBarrier─▶
1659	backward_stage<M> ─GridBarrier─▶ (reset queue) ─GridBarrier─▶ optimizer_stage<Opt>
1660	```
1661	
1662	The forward/backward stages are lightweight **representative** bodies
1663	(grid-stride compute over the param tensor with the correct barrier/hand-off
1664	structure); the optimizer stage is the fused L3 tail (`opt_update<Opt>`,
1665	specialized per optimizer). The sm_90 forward stage exercises the §3.4
1666	producer/consumer split: warp 0 is the producer (`elect_one_sync`,
1667	`arrive_expect_tx`, `warpgroup_reg_dealloc<32>`, one `fence_async_proxy`), warps
1668	1–3 are the consumer (`warpgroup_reg_alloc<240>`, `mbarrier.wait`). The task
1669	queue counter is reset **inside** the kernel at the grid barrier (last arriver),
1670	where all CTAs are quiesced — race-free. **§1.7**: SG2's SAM/bilevel outer loop
1671	stays OUTSIDE this per-step megakernel (a separate host launch); the demo
1672	instantiates the elementwise-tail optimizers and the generator emits the SG2
1673	meta-net tail as its own cell.
1674	
1675	A generated cell `.cu` defines `SG_MEGAKERNEL_DEMO_TEMPLATE_ONLY` before
1676	including the demo, so it pulls in JUST the template machinery (comdat-folded)
1677	and adds its own unique launcher — no duplicate-symbol clash.
1678	
1679	### Cells instantiated + wired into `fused_step`
1680	
1681	Three representative **L3-fitting** (model, optimizer) cells are instantiated in
1682	the sm_90 demo TU and routed by `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp::fused_step`
1683	(§1.12), with the gfx942 twins instantiated in the header (gate-verified):
1684	
1685	| cell | tier (solver) | wired in dispatch | launcher |
1686	|------|---------------|-------------------|----------|
1687	| (mamba3, adamw) | L3_FWD_BWD_OPT | yes (sm_90) | `mega_mamba3_adamw` |
1688	| (transformer_decoder, lion) | L3_FWD_BWD_OPT | yes (sm_90) | `mega_decoder_lion` |
1689	| (vit, supergrok15) | L1_OPT_ONLY* | yes (sm_90) | `mega_vit_supergrok15` |
1690	
1691	`fused_step` detects the arch, looks up `wired_fused_cell(model, optimizer,
1692	arch)`, and dispatches to the demo launcher for these cells; **every other cell

29	## 0. What "make it REAL" means here (the re-spec)
30	
31	The owner's correction reframed the task twice, and both reframings are load-bearing:
32	
33	1. **NOT "re-derive wgmma from scratch."** The in-kernel ss-wgmma engine
34	   (`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh`, consumed via `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:717+`) is
35	   hand-tuned and, per the scoping survey, unlikely to be beaten by any autoscheduler *on the
36	   isolated GEMM*. Re-synthesizing the GEMM is low-value.
37	2. **"Max the shared primitive FIRST, then synthesize the FUSION."** The owner explicitly rejected
38	   naive engine-reuse because *"the engine itself may not be maximal"* — reuse on a sub-maximal base
39	   propagates the deficit to every fused structure. So Level-2's value is **automatic synthesis +
40	   correctness-gated selection of the transport/fusion structural rewrites**, composed over a GEMM
41	   primitive that has *already* been driven to maximality by the #22 structural track.

43	So the deliverable is: **turn the hand-identified structural levers (dW staging redirect, the P1
44	fp32-epilogue fusion class, M0 projection-wgmma, the ViT B1 reshape) from manual one-offs into a
45	searchable + (where tractable) *synthesizable* space that compile.py's generative layer drives and
46	the fp64 + A/A/A gate certifies.** Level-2 = Level-1's flag/macro search (already real) **plus** a
47	*generative* structural-rewrite layer that emits new sources, not just new `-DSG_TUNED_*` values.

49	## 1. The constraints that bind regardless of GO (do not relitigate)
50	
51	These came out of the scoping survey and are architectural facts. The plan is built *around* them.
52	
53	- **C1 — Transport-only legality.** Bit-exact A/A/A determinism requires preserving the **ascending-k
54	  fp32 reduction order** (`SUPEROPTIMIZER_SCOPING.md:232`). fp32 add is non-associative; *any* rewrite
55	  that reassociates the accumulation (faster reduction tree, stream-K, reordered split-K) changes bits
56	  and fails the determinism gate. ⟹ the legal generative space is **transport-only**: move the *same*
57	  operands to the *same* smem in the *same* k-order, faster. Synthesis is constrained to this class.
58	- **C2 — No IR expresses the persistent fused megakernel.** CuTe / Triton / MLIR-Linalg / polyhedral
59	  are all collective- or single-op-shaped; none can host "a persistent grid that runs fwd+bwd+dW+the
60	  optimizer step between hand-built grid barriers" (`:111-201`). ⟹ generative back-ends produce
61	  **device-side-embeddable tile/epilogue fragments** spliced into the existing megakernel, OR
62	  **host-launchable GEMM families** — never a replacement kernel. A host-launched collective cannot
63	  run device-side inside the persistent grid (`wgmma.cuh:14-18`).
64	- **C3 — fp64 must move into the search loop.** Today the in-loop oracle is strict-AOT-fp32
65	  self-consistency; fp64 ground truth lives only in `tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py` and does **not**
66	  call the autotuner (`:223-230`). Self-consistency proves a variant matches the strict build of the
67	  *same* source — it does **not** prove a *newly synthesized* source is fp64-correct. ⟹ wiring the
68	  fp64 oracle into the search loop is the **hard prerequisite** for trusting any generative winner.
69	- **C4 — The pattern library must actually contain the bottleneck's fix.** The scoping gap (`:89-94`):
70	  the generative layer is a *fixed pattern library* + polyhedral reschedule, not search over semantics.
71	  If the library can't express the dW staging redirect / the P1 fusion, turning it "on" yields nothing.
72	  ⟹ Phase C's first job is to *extend the pattern library to the transport/fusion rewrites we know we
73	  want* — synthesis fills the search **within** that class, it does not invent the class.

78	primitive. Status:

80	  - decoder dW contiguous K-major staging — **KEPT** (+2.05×).

82	    worktree). Its KEEP/REVERT verdict fixes whether the maximal decoder primitive is PIPE=1/STAGES=4

85	  - Mamba M0 projection-wgmma — scaffold authored + gated OFF (byte-identical), **stashed/deferred**

91	enabling piece and is *independent of which back-end we turn on*. Concretely: give `BuildSpec` /
92	`pick_winner` a correctness hook that, for any candidate whose origin is in
93	`_SOURCE_GENERATING_ORIGINS` (i.e. a *generated/transformed* source, not a flag-only variant), runs
94	the fp64 parity + A/A/A determinism check (the `run_cell_gate` path already seamed in `af9b720`) and
95	makes the candidate **ineligible to win** unless it records a fp64 PASS — generalizing the existing
96	`_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS` / strict-fp32 gate to true fp64. Flag-only variants keep the cheap
97	in-loop strict-fp32 oracle (they can't change semantics by construction). *Exit:* a deliberately-wrong
98	synthesized variant is rejected in-loop by the fp64 hook (negative self-test), and a known-good one

103	Reframed from the scoping doc's go/no-go probe into a **calibration** under the GO decision: re-express
104	**one isolated decoder fwd in_proj GEMM** (clean shape M=token-tile, N=3d, K=d — *not* the dW, whose

111	- CuTe meaningfully **faster** than the *maxed* hand engine ⟹ a real GEMM-scheduling gap exists →

118	## 4. Phase C — the real generative Level-2 (sharpened by the status map)
119	
120	The map reframes Phase C decisively: **the synth GEMM is a bogus stub, but the elementwise/reduce
121	lowerers are REAL and emit compilable CUDA.** That is exactly the owner's re-spec — *do not synthesize
122	the GEMM* (reuse the maxed hand primitive, §0), *synthesize the FUSION* (the fp32 epilogue passes,
123	which are elementwise/reduce). So Phase C deliberately **sidesteps `_MMA_NATIVE_LOADS_WIRED`/the GEMM
124	synth entirely** and rides the working lowerers + the already-real source-swap/#16 gate. The generative
125	layer must (a) emit **transport-only** rewrites (C1) that are (b) **device-embeddable** into the
126	persistent megakernel (C2), (c) composed over the **maxed** primitive (§0/A1), (d) **fp64-gated
127	in-loop** (C3/A2), and (e) drawn from a library **extended to contain our levers** (C4).
128	
129	**C0 — foundational unblock (prerequisite for any generated source on the real path).** The map found
130	three hard blockers, in order: (i) the **`grokking_optimizers.codegen` emitter module is missing** — the
131	production build never reaches the emitter (`_resolve_sources` L10492 globs hand-written TUs;
132	`_variant_macros` L14646 fails-open to macros-only). Either restore that module to render the *real
133	megakernel TU*, or — cleaner given C2 — **re-target the emitter to emit a device-inlinable fragment**
134	(a `__device__` tile/epilogue function spliced between grid barriers), NOT a standalone `__global__`
135	(today's synth emits launchable kernels with their own grid — useless for the persistent megakernel).
136	(ii) install + verify the **soft deps** actually needed (islpy for sound polyhedral deps; libclang for
137	the body-lift) — skip cutlass (host-launch, C2). (iii) the synth's elementwise/reduce path emits a
138	standalone kernel too; the C0 re-target fixes both. **Until C0 lands, the generative layer cannot touch
139	the production build at all** — this is the real cost the scoping no-go was pricing.

141	Candidate targets once C0 + A2 are green, in increasing risk:
142	
143	- **C-fusion-1 (P1 fp32-epilogue fusion):** synthesize fusions of the ~10 `__syncthreads`-separated
144	  fp32 passes/layer (bias/round/residual/LN-first-read) into the GEMM epilogue lambda
145	  (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:1046-1188` + ViT twin) — order-preserving fold, A/A/A-safe iff the fp32
146	  fold order is preserved (`:1071-1075`). This is the most tractable *and* highest-value synthesis
147	  target: affine, non-GEMM, no reduction reorder. Polyhedral (Phase D) and OpGraph synth both plausibly
148	  reach it.
149	- **C-transport-1 (dW staging variants):** parameterize + synthesize the contiguous K-major

155	Each lands one at a time on the ratchet. **Do not** attempt persistent-megakernel-internal

157	composition story exists — the scoping doc flags this as the hardest, least-proven part (`:340-346`).

159	## 5. Phase D — polyhedral on the non-GEMM fp32 epilogues
160	
161	The libclang+islpy scaffold is order-sensitive, so confine it to the **affine fp32 epilogue passes**
162	(the P1 fusion candidates) where order-preserving tiling/fusion/interchange is legal (C1). It cannot
163	reach the GEMM substrate (no model of wgmma/TMA, `:188`). Treat as an *experiment* that either
164	compounds the C-fusion-1 win or is recorded as a measured dry-well.
165	
166	## 6. Gating + ledger discipline (the spine, non-negotiable)
167	
168	Every generated/transformed candidate, at every phase: **(1)** fp64 parity (rel-tol 1e-4; SAM
169	surfaces 2.5e-2/3e-2) **(2)** A/A/A bit-identical determinism via `torch.equal` **(3)** 3-seed timing
170	at d=2048 — KEEP iff faster on 3+ seeds AND parity-clean, else REVERT, root-caused into the ledger.
171	The fp64 gate (A2) runs *in-loop* for generating origins; the hardware gate
172	(`test_l3tc_tail_gate.py`) remains the final authority on the production step. Microbench screens
173	(fast_triage) may PRUNE but never PICK (the representativeness invariant).
174	
175	## 7. Honest risk register
176	
177	| risk | severity | mitigation |
178	|---|---|---|
179	| Pattern library doesn't contain our levers (C4) | high | Phase C step 0 = extend the library to the named transport/fusion rewrites *before* turning search on; the status map tells us how far the existing emitters already get. |
180	| No e-graph / equality-saturation / semantic search exists here (`:90-92`) | med | We are NOT building one — transport-only legality (C1) collapses the useful space to a small, enumerable set; TPE + the extended pattern library covers it. |
181	| Persistent-launch composition of any generated GEMM is unproven (`:346`) | high | Gate behind a demonstrated host-launched win first; never block the megakernel path on it. |
182	| fp64-in-loop adds ~60s/candidate (the gate cost) | low-med | Only generating-origin candidates pay it; flag-only variants keep the cheap oracle; the cost-model prunes before the gate. |
183	| Synthesis effort exceeds the value vs #24 (the scoping no-go's core point) | med | Phase B calibration + one-lever-at-a-time ratchet means we *measure* the marginal value continuously and can stop at any phase with the ledger as the record. |
184	
185	## 8. Sequencing vs. the in-flight work (status map RESOLVED)
186	
187	The concrete near-term path is now fixed:
188	1. **A2 (fp64-oracle-in-loop) — ALREADY LANDED (af9b720), verified by code read.** The selection side
189	   is complete: `_default_correctness_hook` (L7213) builds the fp64-parity + A/A/A gate via
190	   `run_cell_gate`, `_jit_autotune` installs it on the GPU path (L7236), and `pick_winner`'s P0-1 path
191	   (L6926-6959) re-checks the top-K candidates against it — demote-and-fall-through, fail-closed — so a
192	   winner that merely shares an fp32 rounding error with the strict oracle (the IL=4 trap) can't be
193	   finalized. The #16 gate (L6882) already makes generated origins ineligible without a strict-oracle
194	   PASS. **Remaining A2 gap is Phase-C-coupled, not standalone:** the hook runs `run_cell_gate(cell_key)`
195	   against the *currently-built* `_ops` (L7269 comment), so for a truly *synthesized* candidate the
196	   candidate's generated source must be rebuilt+published *before* the hook fires (today only the final
197	   winner is rebuilt in the verify phase). That per-candidate rebuild-before-fp64-gate is wired in C0,
198	   when generated candidates first exist — there are none today, so A2 is correct as-is for the
199	   flag/macro path that actually ships.
200	2. **A1 (max the primitive)** completes as the #22 tournaments resolve — the PIPE=2-vs-PIPE=1/S=4 gate
201	   (in flight) fixes the maximal decoder primitive; ViT B1 (#29) is the bigger lever next.
202	3. **Phase B (CuTe calibration probe)** — authorable any time; informs whether synthesis aims at the
203	   GEMM (unlikely) or stays on the fusion (likely).
204	4. **C0 (foundational emitter unblock)** then **Phase C (fusion synthesis on the working lowerers)** —
205	   the large build; gated behind A2 green + C0 + the maxed primitive.
206	
207	So #27 advances *in parallel* with the structural ratchet: A2 + Phase B are CPU-authorable now while the
208	GPU runs the perf gates; C0/C is the post-A2 build. Honest framing for the owner: the scoping no-go was
209	pricing exactly the C0 cost (a missing emitter module + absent deps + a re-target from launchable
210	kernels to device fragments). The owner's GO is taken — we start with the genuinely-tractable, already-
211	half-built pieces (A2 + the real source-swap/validation gate) and let the ratchet decide each step.

1	# BUILD_AND_VALIDATE — lever (a): L1 fused megakernel in the grokking race
2	
3	This document is the operator runbook for the change that wires the L3-substrate
4	fused model×optimizer megakernels into the grokking race **as the optimizer
5	step**, with the FULL optimizer scalar set (no placeholder scalars). Run the
6	sequence below on a real **sm_90 (H100/H200)** device after the concurrent GPU
7	job releases the device and the live `_ops.so`.
8	
9	> Source-complete only. The implementing agent did NOT build, did NOT run any GPU
10	> validation, and did NOT touch `setup.py` / `compile.py` / `build.sh` / `README`
11	> (a sibling agent owns those). Everything below is for the operator to run.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 0. The one deviation you must know (read first)
16	
17	The directive's items 4–5 assume the L3 fused megakernel computes the **real**
18	model forward/backward (so a "megakernel-vs-eager loss-trajectory" test is
19	meaningful). **It does not.** The L3 model stages are an element-local
20	**surrogate** over the flat parameter blob:
21	
22	* `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages.cuh`:
23	  `acts[gi] = GELU(params[gi] + input[gi])`, `grad[gi] = acts[gi]·GELU'(params[gi])`
24	  — no token embedding, no attention, no matmul, no cross-entropy.
25	* The race's model `input` is **int token indices** `[B, seq]`; the kernel wants
26	  `float[numel(params)]`. They are not even shape-compatible.
27	* On the L3 path the kernel does `(void)grad;` and recomputes its own surrogate
28	  grad, ignoring any real gradient handed in.
29	
30	Therefore an L3 cell's loss **cannot** match an eager PyTorch run, and "skip the
31	race's fwd/bwd and let the megakernel own fwd+bwd+opt" would train on gradients
32	unrelated to the task. (Three independent confirmations; see the cited file.)
33	
34	**What was built instead — the faithful unit.** The **L1 optimizer tail**
35	(`fused_optimizer_stage<Opt>`) reads the **real** gradient from global memory
36	(computed by the framework's own `loss.backward()`) and applies the canonical
37	per-element `apply_optimizer<Opt>` update. That is exactly the eager optimizer
38	step. So lever (a) is wired as: **keep the real PyTorch forward + backward, and
39	replace `optimizer.step()` with the L1 fused megakernel** (`opt_only=True`). This
40	is validated by **optimizer-equivalence** + a **grok smoke**, not by an (ill-
41	posed) L3-vs-eager loss test. The L3 path stays compiled (perf-placement
42	coverage) and reachable via `opt_only=False`, but is **not** the race path.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 1. What changed (files)
47	
48	ABI / C++ (the C2-gap fix — carry the FULL scalar set, not just `lr`):
49	* `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` — new `FusedScalars` POD (lr, beta1,
50	  beta2, eps, wd, bc1, bc2, alpha, beta, lamb, alpha_max, gate, d_factor,
51	  neg_lr_scale, decay_factor) + `apply_scalars()` (folds it into `FusedOptState`,
52	  which `apply_optimizer<>` already reads — this is what un-freezes bc1/bc2/gate/
53	  d_factor from their inert `1.0` defaults). HIP twin in
54	  `csrc/fused/gfx942/opt_components.hip.hpp`.
55	* `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` — `fused_step` widened to carry the scalar set +
56	  an `int64 step` + `opt_only` (tier selector); builds `FusedScalars` and passes
57	  it through `dispatch_{sm90,gfx942}_cell`. Layout-identical `FusedScalars`
58	  mirrors added (sm90 / gfx942_mega namespaces) so the call-site mangling matches
59	  the cell `.cu`/`.hip` definitions (same pattern the existing `PersistentContext`
60	  mirror uses).
61	* `csrc/bindings/helpers.h` — `fused_step` declaration widened (default values
62	  live HERE only — the definition in dispatch.cpp omits them, per C++ rules).
63	* `csrc/bindings/bindings.cpp` — `m.def("fused_step", …)` gains `py::arg`
64	  defaults so the short 7-arg call still works.

97	decoder:lion, vit:lion, mamba:lion`** (6 cells). L1 is model-agnostic (the tail
98	never touches the model stages), so all 3 models × {adamw, lion} are equivalent

159	```bash
160	PYTHONPATH=. python3 tests/hw/parity_gate_h100.py     # expect 11/0
161	```

165	## 5. NEW validation: L1 megakernel vs eager reference
166	
167	The lever-(a) gate. (A) optimizer-equivalence per whitelisted cell (the L1 tail
168	vs a pure-PyTorch reference transcribed from `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h`, at
169	~1e-4 rel over K=200 steps — tight enough to catch a frozen `bc1/bc2`); (B) a
170	3-seed `(decoder, adamw)` grok smoke (real decoder + real fwd/bwd + the L1 fused

172	
173	```bash
174	# The two example cells from the directive:
175	PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_megakernel_vs_eager --cells decoder:adamw,decoder:lion
176	# All 6 whitelisted cells:

201	```bash

203	PYTHONPATH=. python grokking_race_v2.py --tasks decoder --num-seeds 3 \
204	    --eval-every 50 --output results/fused_l1_check

214	threshold in step-counts consistent with the eager baseline (the L1 tail is the

217	---
218	
219	## 7. Known risks / caveats
220	
221	* **fp32 only.** The L1 tail indexes raw `float` memory; `fused_optimizer_step`
222	  raises on non-fp32 params and `.contiguous()`-es param/grad. The race runs AMP
223	  off by default, so this holds. With AMP on, the fused path raises and the run
224	  degrades to eager (no silent corruption).
225	* **`fused_step` does NOT run `check_param_grad`** (that guard is on the per-op
226	  path). The Python driver enforces dtype/contiguity instead; do not call the raw
227	  `ops.fused_step` with a non-contiguous/half tensor.
228	* **Single `(bc1, bc2)` per call** is correct only because every race parameter
229	  steps together (one shared step counter). A caller that steps tensors at
230	  different counts must call `fused_step` per-tensor with that tensor's bc. This
231	  is asserted-by-construction in the race and documented loudly in
232	  `opt_components.cuh` / `dispatch.cpp`.
233	* **Persistent optimizer state is owned by the driver**, keyed by `id(param)` on
234	  the optimizer instance (`_fused_state_cache`). It is allocated once per param
235	  and never reallocated (reallocating would reset momentum and the run would not
236	  grok). It is NOT checkpointed by `optimizer.state_dict()` — a mid-run
237	  save/restore would lose the fused momentum. For a from-scratch race this is a
238	  non-issue; flagged for any resume-from-checkpoint use.
239	* **L3 remains compiled but unused by the race.** If a future change wants real
240	  fused fwd+bwd+opt, the model stages must be replaced with the real model graph
241	  (out of scope here) — `opt_only=False` currently runs the surrogate.
242	* **gfx942 host launch is 🟡** (no hipcc/MI300X in the implementing environment);
243	  the AMD cells were regenerated for ABI consistency but only the sm_90 path is
244	  exercised by this runbook.
245	* **Per-parameter launch cost (perf, not correctness).** The `fused_step` ABI is
246	  one parameter tensor per call (`n=numel`, `n_tasks=1`, `state≥3n`), so
247	  `fused_optimizer_step` launches ONE persistent megakernel per parameter (each a
248	  `#SMs`-CTA grid where a single CTA does the one-task work). For a model with
249	  dozens of small params this is many tiny launches — expected to be SLOWER per
250	  step than a multi-tensor fused optimizer, and the roofline number for the fused
251	  AdamW/Lion path should be read with that in mind (it is a correctness/wiring
252	  deliverable at this ABI, not a throughput win). A batched multi-tensor ABI
253	  (pack all params into one call with real per-tensor `sizes`/`offsets`) is the
254	  natural follow-up but is out of scope for lever (a).
255	
256	---
257	
258	## PHASE 1 — the TRUE L3 fused megakernel for `decoder × adamw` (real fwd+bwd+opt)
259	
260	> Supersedes §0's "L3 cannot match eager" **for the one cell
261	> `(transformer_decoder, adamw)` on sm_90 only**. Every OTHER cell's L3 path is
262	> still the element-local surrogate (§0 holds for them); they remain compiled and
263	> unused by the race. This section is what changed in PHASE 1 and how to validate
264	> it. Source-complete only — the implementing agent did NOT build and did NOT run
265	> any GPU work (tuning owns the GPU).
266	
267	### What PHASE 1 does
268	
269	Replaces the SURROGATE model stage with the **REAL transformer-decoder
270	forward+backward** inside the existing persistent megakernel, so that for the
271	`decoder × adamw` cell **`(decoder × adamw)` runs as ONE persistent kernel per
272	training step** — real model math, real optimizer math, **zero intermediate
273	kernel launches** (the owner rejected CUDA graphs; this is the chosen path).
274	Weights/state stay resident; the stages are separated only by in-kernel grid
275	barriers.
276	
277	The race's `train_adamw` loop now, for the decoder cell, calls
278	`_try_fused_train_step(...)` FIRST: if the L3-REAL kernel is available it runs the
279	whole step (fwd+bwd+adamw) and returns the loss, and the loop **skips its own
280	eager forward/backward/`optimizer.step()`**. Otherwise it falls back to the eager
281	fwd+bwd + the L1 fused optimizer tail (the pre-PHASE-1 path). `eval_every`
282	evaluation stays eager/unchanged.
283	
284	### Exact architecture transcribed (cites grokking_race_v2.py)
285	
286	`_raw_model` → `Transformer(nl=2, d=128, h=4, ntok=99, seq=4)` (seq hardcoded 4):
287	
288	| component | def | shape |
289	|---|---|---|
290	| `tok` | `nn.Embedding(99,128)` (:360) | [99,128] |
291	| `pos` | `nn.Embedding(4,128)` (:360) | [4,128] |
292	| 2× `DecoderBlock` | (:346) | |
293	| `attn` | `nn.MultiheadAttention(128,4,batch_first)` (:349), **causal** `triu(diag=1)` (:352) | in_proj [384,128]+[384], out_proj [128,128]+[128] |
294	| `n1,n2` | `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (:350), eps **1e-5** | [128]×2 each |
295	| `ff` | `Linear(128,512)→GELU→Linear(512,128)` (:351) | [512,128]+[512], [128,512]+[128] |
296	| post-LN | `x=n1(x+attn(x)); h=n2(x+ff(x))` (:354-355) | |
297	| `norm` | `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (:362) | [128]×2 |
298	| `out` | `nn.Linear(128,99)` (:362) | [99,128]+[99] |
299	| forward | `h=tok+pos; for l: h=l(h); return out(norm(h)[:,-1,:])` (:366-368) | **LAST token** |
300	| loss | `F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)` (:745) | mean over B |
301	
302	**30 parameter tensors, 422,755 total params.** Numerics pinned (each verified
303	against autograd in `tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py`): **GELU = exact erf** (the
304	surrogate's tanh approx is ~4e-4 off — wrong here); LayerNorm **eps=1e-5**;
305	attention scale **1/√32**, softmax with row-max subtraction; CE **mean over B** →
306	`dlogits=(softmax−onehot)/B`. `nn.MultiheadAttention` is transcribed bit-identical
307	(in_proj packs `[Wq;Wk;Wv]` row-blocks; verified `max|diff|==0`).
308	
309	### Stage / barrier layout (one persistent kernel)
310	
311	`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`, gridDim = #SMs (one CTA/SM),
312	256 threads/CTA. **Batch-parallel** (NOT the param-tensor work-steal queue — that
313	would vary the batch→CTA grouping and fp32 sums aren't associative):
314	
315	```
316	P0  each CTA zeroes its OWN grad-partial slice + loss slot
317	--- grid barrier B0 ---
318	P1  each CTA owns a FIXED contiguous batch slice (blockIdx.x); processes its
319	    samples ONE AT A TIME (CTA-cooperative), accumulating each sample's weight-
320	    grad into the CTA's partial with a SINGLE-OWNER-THREAD-PER-ELEMENT rule
321	    (no atomics → deterministic), and sums its slice's NLL (fp32)
322	--- grid barrier B1 ---
323	P2  deterministic cross-CTA reduce: sum partial[0..nCTA) in ASCENDING CTA index
324	    into the global grad (no float atomics; order fixed → reuses the work-steal
325	    queue to pick WHO reduces which tensor). Loss: fp64 ordered sum → loss/B → a
326	    device float the host reads back.
327	--- grid barrier B2 (sync_reset: also resets the queue for P3) ---
328	P3  the REAL apply_optimizer<AdamW> tail consumes the reduced grad in place
329	```
330	
331	Determinism: fixed batch→CTA grouping + fixed ascending-CTA reduction order; **no
332	float atomics** in the weight-grad reduce. The embedding `tok.weight` scatter maps
333	**thread→embedding column** and loops `(sample,position)` sequentially, so
334	colliding token ids (vocab 99) accumulate deterministically.
335	
336	### SMEM budget per CTA
337	
338	One sample, one layer live (the backward **recomputes** each layer's forward from
339	the cached layer input rather than caching every intermediate, so only one layer's
340	activations are live): `DecSampleSmem` ≈ **41.96 KB** — UNDER the 48 KB static-smem
341	cliff, so NO dynamic-smem opt-in and the occupancy≥1 launch guard
342	(`dynamicSMemBytes=0`) is unchanged.
343	
344	### Weight layout (ONE source of truth)
345	
346	`tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py::decoder_param_layout()` (asserted == the eager
347	`named_parameters()` order in the parity test) is the single source. The C++
348	device header `csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh` is **GENERATED** from the same
349	table by `megakernel_codegen.py --decoder-layout` and **static-asserts the count
350	(30) and total (422755)** + an offset/size consistency fold — a mismatch fails the
351	**build**, never corrupts at dispatch. The Python wrapper
352	(`dispatch.py::_DECODER_TOTAL_ELEMS`) and dispatch.cpp (`kDecoderTotalElems`)
353	mirror the literal and cross-check `params.numel()` at the call site.
354	
355	### ABI (no `bindings.cpp` / `setup.py` edit; the owned-seam extension)
356	
357	The pybind `m.def("fused_step", ...)` arity is pinned in `bindings.cpp` (NOT
358	owned), so `fused_step`'s arity is unchanged. The token path is carried through the
359	EXISTING tensors, and the **behavior** is extended in `dispatch.cpp` (owned):
360	
361	* `input` = **int32** `[B*(kSeq+1)]` — tokens `[B*kSeq]` then targets `[B]`
362	  (`B = numel/(kSeq+1)`; S/vocab/d are compile-time).
363	* `params` = flat `[422755]` fp32; `state` = `[m|v|extra]` (`3*total`) **+ a
364	  trailing loss slot** the kernel writes the mean CE into (read back in Python).
365	* the **workspace** (`nCTA*total` grad partials + `nCTA` loss) is device scratch
366	  allocated in `dispatch.cpp` (keyed by device) — it never crosses the ABI.
367	* routing: `dispatch.cpp::fused_step` branches on
368	  `(model=="transformer_decoder" && optimizer=="adamw" && !opt_only)` →
369	  `mega_decoder_real_adamw` (an `extern` nvcc launcher; **the 33 generated
370	  surrogate cells are untouched, so no cell/table regeneration is forced and git
371	  stays generator-consistent**). dispatch.cpp is HOST-compiled, so all
372	  `<<<>>>`/device code lives in the new nvcc TU
373	  `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw.cu` (picked up by setup.py's
374	  `csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu` glob), reached via an `extern` decl using the existing
375	  mirror structs (same FQN/layout → mangling matches).
376	
377	Python: `dispatch.py::fused_train_step(model, opt, module, optimizer, tokens,
378	targets, ...)` packs the int32 input, owns the persistent flat-param + state
379	buffers, calls `ops.fused_step(..., opt_only=False)`, scatters the updated params
380	back, and returns the loss. The L3-REAL tier marker is `_FUSED_L3_REAL` +
381	`has_l3_real()` (sm_90-only).
382	
383	### What is validated by which test (`tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py`)
384	
385	**No-GPU (run anywhere, the rigor substitute for an un-runnable .cu):**
386	* `test_decoder_oracle_matches_autograd` — the manual fwd+bwd oracle == autograd
387	  (loss + every grad, ~1e-12 fp64). This is the math the CUDA transcribes.
388	* `test_decoder_kernel_mirror_matches_oracle` — a single-threaded **structural
389	  mirror** of the kernel (same buffer aliasing, recompute, head-split index math,
390	  owner-thread accumulation, the 3-pass attention backward, a token collision) ==
391	  the oracle (~1e-12). Catches the missing-term/index/alias bug class the
392	  un-runnable .cu hides. (It does NOT cover `__syncthreads`/grid-barrier races —
393	  those are verified by reading each barrier against the buffer it guards.)
394	* `test_decoder_layout_matches_named_parameters` — flat layout == `named_parameters`
395	  order (30 tensors, 422755), and `_DECODER_TOTAL_ELEMS` agrees.
396	
397	**GPU-gated (sm_90 + built extension; skip cleanly otherwise):**
398	* `test_decoder_l3_real_single_step_parity` — (a) kernel loss within **1e-5 rel**
399	  of eager; **the kernel's reduced weight grad** (routed out through the ABI
400	  `grad` tensor, returned by `fused_train_step(return_grad=True)`) compared
401	  **PER-TENSOR against the oracle** within **1e-4 rel** (dumps max-rel per tensor)
402	  — the keystone check that actually exercises the hand-written backward's grad
403	  magnitudes (loss is fwd-only; params-after-step is sign-dominated at step 1);
404	  params after 1 step within **1e-5 rel**.
405	* `test_decoder_l3_real_trajectory` — (b) 200-step loss curve tracks eager AdamW
406	  (**1e-3 rel**); final params within **1e-3 rel** (fp32 accumulation drift).
407	* `test_decoder_l3_real_groks` — (c) 3-seed grok smoke through `train_adamw` (now
408	  routing the decoder cell through the L3-REAL megakernel).
409	
410	### Run (operator, on a real sm_90 device after the GPU job releases)
411	
412	```bash
413	# clean rebuild (the dispatch.cpp behavior changed + the new .cu must compile):
414	PYTHONPATH=. pip install -e . --no-build-isolation   # or rm -rf build/ first
415	
416	# no-GPU correctness gates (also run in CI):
417	PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py \
418	    -k "oracle or mirror or layout" -q
419	
420	# generator-consistency of the layout header (EXPECT: no diff):
421	PYTHONPATH=. python -m grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen --decoder-layout \
422	    > csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh && git diff --stat
423	
424	# GPU parity + grok (sm_90):
425	PYTHONPATH=. python -m pytest tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py -m hw -q
426	
427	# end-to-end: the decoder race now takes the L3-REAL fused train step:
428	PYTHONPATH=. python grokking_race_v2.py --tasks decoder --num-seeds 3 \
429	    --eval-every 50 --output results/l3_real_decoder
430	```
431	
432	### Known scope / caveats (PHASE 1)
433	
434	* **fp32 compute is the correctness baseline.** bf16 compute is a deliberate
435	  follow-up: it would be a flag defaulting to THIS fp32 path (the L3-REAL path
436	  raises/falls back to eager under AMP today — a loud None, never a silent stub).
437	  The race's bf16-autocast default applies to the EAGER fallback path, not the
438	  fused kernel.
439	* **decoder × adamw on sm_90 only.** Other optimizers / models / gfx942 keep the
440	  eager (+ L1) path; only this one cell has the real fwd+bwd+opt kernel.
441	* **The surrogate L3 cells are now unreachable dead code on the race path** (the
442	  decoder real path is routed before them in `fused_step`; the other cells'
443	  `opt_only=False` still runs the surrogate but the race never sets it). Documented,
444	  not hidden.
445	* **Persistent flat-param + optimizer state are driver-owned** (keyed by model on
446	  the optimizer instance), allocated once and never reallocated (reallocating
447	  resets momentum → never groks). NOT checkpointed by `optimizer.state_dict()`.
448	* **The model must be eager** (not `torch.compile`-wrapped) on the fused path — the
449	  flat layout assumes the eager `named_parameters()` order. The race builds the
450	  decoder eager by default (`compile_model=False`).
451	* **Per-step cost:** the workspace is `nCTA × 422755` fp32 (~223 MB at 132 SMs),
452	  allocated once. This is a correctness/wiring deliverable; a warp-per-sample
453	  concurrent variant + bf16 tensor-core matmuls are the perf follow-ups.

11	inside a component layer (substrate / model-stage header / optimizer header /
12	`opt_components.cuh`) so all 33 cells inherit it through recomposition by
13	`megakernel_codegen.py`. No cell-specific hacks. The architecture in
14	`csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md` is inviolate.

(The file's own docstring at `:18` says "5 phases / 4 barriers" but enumerates only P0–P3 and B0–B2 — the docstring is stale; the **call sites** are the ground truth.) | `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:124,148,178` |

The only WGMMA path is **host-launched CUTLASS** in `mma.cuh` (not device-callable). `wgs::` has mbarrier / setmaxnreg / elect only — no MMA. cp.async + DSMEM-reduce + L2-persist exist in `primitives.cuh`; **TMA tensor-map / `cp.async.bulk.tensor` do NOT exist** | grep: only hit for `wgmma` outside `mma.cuh` is `compile.py` (a feature-detect string); `model_stage_*` scalar loops at `dec_linear` `model_stages_decoder.cuh:289`, `vit_linear:299`, `mb_linear:307` |

37	
38	## 1. The regime, and the two architectural forks (read this first)
39	
40	### 1.1 The regime split: current = memory-bound; post-R2 decoder/vit = compute-bound; mamba = memory-bound. Verified.
41	
42	The current scalar cells are memory-bound (on the 223 MB partial workspace, §1.2).
43	After Fork B removes the partials (§3), the **decoder and vit move COMPUTE-bound**
44	(decoder AI ≈ 900 FLOP/B ≫ the 295 FLOP/B bf16 ridge — §10.4), so their roof is
45	GEMM-limited and the §3 short-K/occupancy=1 achievable-roof honesty is what governs.
46	**Mamba stays memory-bound** intrinsically (the selective scan, AI ≈ 0.86 FLOP/B —
47	§8). The compute floors below set the prize; the per-GEMM roofs (§3) set what is
48	actually reachable.
49	
50	Decoder fwd+bwd FLOPs/step (computed — `python3`, shown):
51	- per-layer MACs = in_proj(S·3d·d) + scores(H·S·S·dh) + ctx(H·S·dh·S) + out_proj(S·d·d) + ff0(S·dff·d) + ff2(S·d·dff); head(1·V·d).
52	- fwd = L·per_layer + head = **1,593,728 MAC/sample**; bwd ≈ 2× fwd (dX + dW) ⇒ fwd+bwd = 3× fwd = **9,562,368 FLOP/sample** (MAC=2 FLOP).
53	- × B=4704 ⇒ **44.98 GFLOP/step** (matches the briefing "tens of GFLOP").
54	
55	| precision | peak (TF/s) | decoder compute floor / step |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| bf16 TC | 989.4 | **45.5 µs** |
58	| tf32 TC | 494.7 | 90.9 µs |
59	| fp32 CUDA | 66.9 | **672 µs** |
60	
61	Source peaks: `tuning/roofline.py:44-54`.
62	
63	**The current scalar fp32 design is pinned near the 672 µs CUDA-core floor and in
64	practice far below it** (one sample per CTA, no ILP, no vectorization, no TC).
65	The bf16-TC floor is **14.8× below** the fp32-CUDA floor — that gap is the prize.
66	
67	### 1.2 But the dW partial workspace already costs 3× the bf16 floor
68	
69	The current cells use a `[nCTA × total]` per-CTA grad-partial buffer
70	(`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:112` `tok.workspace + cta*total`), reduced in P2:
71	- nCTA=132 (H100 SMs), total=422,755, fp32 ⇒ **223 MB**.
72	- P1 writes it, P2 reads it ⇒ **446 MB / step → 133 µs** at HBM3 3.35 TB/s.
73	
74	**133 µs is ~3× the 45 µs bf16 compute floor.** So even a perfect TC GEMM leaves
75	the decoder cell memory-bound on the partials alone. **Q2 (eliminate the partials)
76	is co-primary with Q1 (the TC restructure), not a follow-up.** The same holds for
77	vit (132×418,017×4 = 221 MB) and is the dominant cost for mamba (132×259,425×4 =
78	137 MB; mamba's GEMMs are already memory-bound — §8).
79	
80	### 1.3 The Q1/Q2 duality — you cannot eliminate both global acts AND partials
81	
82	This is the load-bearing constraint the whole doc is organized around.
83	
84	- The full token tensor does **not** fit smem: T·d·2B = 18,816·128·2 = **4.8 MB ≫
85	  227 KB**. So "activations smem-resident" is only ever achievable **per-CTA on a
86	  token-tile**, never globally.
87	- The weight-grad contraction dW = Xᵀ@dY sums over the **token dimension T**,
88	  which is **spread across CTAs** (each CTA owns a token slice). Therefore:
89	  - **Either** acts stay CTA-local in smem (a token-tile) **and** dW needs a
90	    **cross-CTA reduction** (→ the partials, 223 MB),
91	  - **or** dW is **output-stationary** — each CTA owns dW tiles and contracts the
92	    **full T itself** (Q2, no partials) — **but then acts must live in HBM** so the
93	    dW-owning CTA can read every token's activation.
94	
95	You get one or the other per GEMM, chosen by traffic. Naming this duality is the
96	honest answer to Q1+Q2; "both at once" is impossible.
97	
98	**Fork A — CTA-local token-tile (M_tile≈128), wgmma on the local tile, keep the
99	current recompute-in-bwd discipline.** No global acts; no new inter-layer grid
100	barriers (a CTA stays local through all layers, exactly as today). **But dW still
101	needs the cross-CTA reduction → keeps the 223 MB partials (133 µs).**
102	
103	**Fork B — dW-output-stationary (Q2).** Eliminates the 223 MB partials. fwd writes
104	acts to HBM; bwd dW-tile CTAs stream the full T. Acts traffic (decoder, bf16,
105	rough): ~2 `[T,d]` tensors/layer × L = 9.6M elems × 2B × (write+read) = **39 MB →
106	11.5 µs** (computed). vit/mamba scale with d_inner but stay tens of MB in bf16.
107	
108	**Recommendation: Fork B for all three models.** 39 MB (11.5 µs) of acts traffic
109	replaces 446 MB (133 µs) of partials traffic — an **11× traffic reduction on the
110	dominant term**, and it deletes one whole grid-barrier phase (P2 reduce, B1). The
111	acts round-trip is the documented cost; it is an order of magnitude smaller than
112	the partials it replaces. Fork A is retained only as the fallback for any GEMM
113	whose dW output tile is so small that output-stationary under-occupies (none in the
114	race — see §3).
115	
116	> **Note on the briefing's Q1 phrasing.** The briefing's "layer-by-layer batched
117	> GEMMs across T with a grid barrier between each layer GEMM, acts in HBM" is one
118	> realization of Fork B, but **a global per-layer barrier is NOT mandatory** and is
119	> rejected: it would serialize the grid L×(#GEMMs) times per step. The chosen
120	> structure (§2) keeps each CTA's fwd→bwd **local and barrier-free within the
121	> token-tile**, with grid barriers only at the genuine cross-CTA couplings
122	> (embedding scatter, optimizer). Code/analysis wins over the context note.
123	
124	---
125	
126	## 2. The persistent-kernel phase structure (Fork B), per step
127	
128	One launch, gridDim = #SMs, 256 threads/CTA (two Hopper warpgroups). Barriers are
129	the existing `GridBarrier::sync` / `sync_reset` (`megakernel_common.cuh:144,209`).
130	
131	```
132	P0  zero embedding-grad accumulators (tok/pos only — the ONLY tensors needing a
133	    cross-CTA scatter; all weight dW are output-stationary so need no pre-zero).
134	--- B0 (sync_reset) ---
135	P1  FWD+BWD, token-tile-parallel. Each CTA owns a contiguous token-tile of M_tile
136	    rows (M_tile=SG_TUNED_TILE_M, default 128). For its tile it runs the full
137	    fwd then bwd through all layers, wgmma on bf16 smem tiles, fp32 accumulators.
138	      - forward activations needed by bwd are written to HBM acts[T, ...] (bf16)
139	        OR recomputed (the current recompute discipline still applies per tile).
140	      - dW: each CTA accumulates its tile's contribution into its OWNED dW output
141	        tiles by contracting its M_tile rows; see §3 for the split-K ownership that
142	        makes this a full-T contraction without partials.
143	      - embedding grads (tok/pos): index-scatter into the P0 accumulators by the
144	        deterministic owner map of §3.4.
145	      - loss: per-CTA fp32 NLL slot (kept — `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:147`).
146	--- B1 (sync_reset) ---
147	P2  OPTIMIZER tail. apply_optimizer<Opt> over the (now-complete, in-place) grad.
148	    For epilogue-fusable optimizers (§4) this phase is FUSED INTO P1's dW epilogue
149	    and B1+P2 collapse — 3 phases / 2 barriers for adamw/lion/grokfast/grokadamw/
150	    neuralgrok. Non-fusable optimizers keep P2 (and their own precompute phases).
151	```
152	
153	**Barrier count per step, decoder, before vs after:**
154	
155	| design | phases | grid barriers |
156	|---|---|---|
157	| current (scalar, partials) | 4 (P0,P1,P2-reduce,P3-opt) | **3** (B0,B1,B2; the fwd→bwd sync inside P1 is `__syncthreads`, not a grid barrier) |
158	| Fork B, non-fusable opt | 3 | **2** |
159	| Fork B, **epilogue-fused opt** (5 of 11) | 2 | **1 or 2** (see caveat) |
160	
161	The dW-reduce phase (P2) + its barrier (B2) are **deleted** (no partials → nothing
162	to reduce): the baseline **3 → 2** barriers, a net saving of **one** grid barrier.
163	This is the second win of Fork B beyond traffic.
164	
165	> **Embedding caveat on the "1 barrier" fused case.** Weight dW fuses to its
166	> optimizer in the P1 epilogue (0 extra barriers). But the **tok/pos** grads are a
167	> cross-CTA scatter (§3.4) that every CTA contributes to — their optimizer apply
168	> must wait for **all** CTAs to finish scattering, which needs **B1 before the
169	> tok/pos apply**. So a fully-epilogue-fused cell is **2 phases / 1 barrier for the
170	> ~28 weight tensors, but the 2 embedding tensors still require that one barrier** —
171	> i.e. the realistic fused floor is **1 barrier (B0 for the embedding-accumulator
172	> zero + the post-scatter rendezvous folded into it)**, not zero. The 5-fusable
173	> cells land at **1 barrier**; do not claim 0. 🟡
174	
175	> 🟡 **Recompute vs acts-in-HBM is itself a per-model choice.** Decoder's bwd
176	> currently recomputes each layer from `layer_in` (`model_stages_decoder.cuh:498`
177	> `dec_recompute_layer`) to stay under 48 KB static smem. Under Fork B the dW CTA
178	> needs *other* CTAs' tile activations, so the cross-tile activations MUST be in
179	> HBM regardless; the within-tile recompute can stay. The build agent picks
180	> recompute-vs-store per GEMM by the smem budget table (§6/§9); both are
181	> bit-identical in the produced grad (same expression, different storage class).
182	
183	---
184	
185	## 3. Per-GEMM TC plan (M/N/K, wgmma tiling, ownership, achievable roof)
186	
187	Conventions: wgmma atom `m64nNk16` for bf16 (Hopper ss-wgmma; N ∈ {8..256}). A
188	"CTA tile" is the M×N output block one CTA owns; the K loop iterates k-steps of 16.
189	Activations are bf16 in smem staged from HBM via cp.async (TMA in phase-2, §4).
190	**Achievable roof per GEMM is bounded by the mainloop k-step count** (short-K = few
191	MMA issues to amortize prologue/epilogue + occupancy=1 has no inter-CTA latency
192	hiding — the in-CTA producer/consumer pipeline must hide it). I give the roof class
193	honestly; I do **not** claim peak.

195	### 3.1 Decoder (d=128, dff=512, S=4, V=99, H=4, dh=32; B=4704, T=18,816)
196	
197	The forward GEMMs are tall-skinny in T: **M = number of (sample×position) rows the
198	GEMM touches.** in_proj/out_proj/ff act on all S positions ⇒ M-rows = T = 18,816.
199	The head acts on the last position only ⇒ M-rows = B = 4704.
200	
201	| GEMM | M (rows) | N | K | wgmma tiling | CTA tile (M×N) | acts location | roof class |
202	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
203	| **in_proj** (fwd) qkv = X·Wᵀ | 18,816 | 3d=384 | d=128 | m64n128k16, 3 N-tiles, **8 k-steps** | 128×128, ~147 M-tiles over 132 SMs | X in smem tile (bf16) | K=128 → mid. M huge → TC-saturated on issue; **~55–70%** 🟡 |
204	| **scores** q·kᵀ (per head) | S=4 | S=4 | dh=32 | **too small for wgmma** — 4×4×32. Keep **scalar fp32** per (head,qrow) exactly as now (`model_stages_decoder.cuh:364`) | — | smem | N/A (special-cased; <0.1% of FLOPs) |
205	| **ctx** attn·v (per head) | S=4 | dh=32 | S=4 | too small — scalar fp32, kept | — | smem | N/A |
206	| **out_proj** a = ctx·Wᵀ | 18,816 | d=128 | d=128 | m64n128k16, **8 k-steps** | 128×128 | smem tile | as in_proj, **~55–70%** 🟡 |
207	| **ff0** g = x1·Wᵀ | 18,816 | dff=512 | d=128 | m64n128k16, 4 N-tiles, **8 k-steps** | 128×128 | smem tile | M·N large; **~60–72%** 🟡 |
208	| **ff2** ff = g·Wᵀ | 18,816 | d=128 | dff=512 | m64n128k16, **32 k-steps** | 128×128 | smem tile | **best — K=512 amortizes prologue; ~72–82%** 🟡 |
209	| **head** logits = hn·Wᵀ | 4704 | V=99 | d=128 | m64n96k16 (pad N→128), 8 k-steps | 64×96 | smem | N=99 odd, padded; M=B large; **~45–60%** 🟡 |
210	| **bwd dX** (per linear) dX = dY·W | 18,816 | K_in | N_out | mirror of fwd, swap N↔K | 128×128 | acts HBM | same class as the fwd it mirrors |
211	| **bwd dW** (per linear) dW = dYᵀ·X | N_out | K_in | **T=18,816** | **m64nNk16 contracting full T**, T/16=**1176 k-steps** | dW output tile (e.g. 64×128 for ff0_w[512,128]) | **dY,X stream from HBM acts** | **K=T huge → the most TC-efficient GEMMs; ~80–88%** 🟡 |
212	
213	**Why dW is the TC-friendliest and how Q2 lands here.** dW = Σ_{t∈[0,T)} dY[t,:]ᵀ
214	X[t,:]. In GEMM terms (M_g=N_out, N_g=K_in, **K_g=T**) the contraction is the full
215	token dimension. **Each CTA owns a fixed (M_g×N_g) output tile of dW and contracts
216	ALL T tokens itself** by streaming dY[*, n_out_tile] and X[*, k_in_tile] from the
217	HBM acts buffer in **fixed ascending-t k-step order**. No `[nCTA×total]` partial,
218	no cross-CTA reduce — the dW tile is written **once**, complete. This is the literal
219	Q2 deliverable.
220	
221	- **Tile ownership map.** dW tensors are small (largest decoder weight = ff0_w/ff2_w
222	  = 512×128 = 65,536 elems = 8 output-tiles of 64×128). The 30 weight tensors yield
223	  ~**O(60) dW output tiles** total. Assign tiles to CTAs round-robin by a fixed
224	  `tile_id = atomic-free static partition` (tile_id → CTA = tile_id % nCTA), so
225	  every step the same CTA owns the same tile (determinism + L2 warmth). With ~60
226	  tiles and 132 SMs, ~half the SMs own a dW tile; **the rest are NOT idle** — they
227	  own dX tiles and the fwd GEMMs in P1 (the phases overlap within P1; dW and dX of
228	  a layer are independent given dY).
229	- **Determinism.** k-order is **ascending t**, fixed and identical on every run;
230	  one CTA owns each tile end-to-end (no work-steal split of a tile's K-loop). No
231	  float atomics. ✔ matches the owner's determinism rule.
232	- **Eliminated traffic (quantified).** Removes the 223 MB partial buffer and its
233	  446 MB/step round-trip (**133 µs**); adds ~39 MB/step acts (**11.5 µs**). Net
234	  **−122 µs/step** of HBM time on the decoder.
235	
236	**What remains of P2 (the embedding scatter).** tok/pos grads are index-scatter,
237	not a GEMM: `g.tok[token_id·d + j] += dh` and `g.pos[s·d + j] += dh`
238	(`model_stages_decoder.cuh:981-988`). These collide across tokens/CTAs and **cannot
239	be output-stationary** (the output row depends on data-dependent `token_id`).
240	**Deterministic owner map (Q2 tail):**
241	  - **tok** (99 rows × 128): owner = `row j of tok-tensor → CTA (row % nCTA)`. Each
242	    owner CTA, after B0, loops **all T tokens in ascending t**, and for each token
243	    whose id maps to a row it owns, accumulates `dh[t,:]`. Fixed t-order + single
244	    owner per row ⇒ deterministic, atomic-free. Cost: each CTA scans T token-ids
245	    (cheap, T=18,816 int reads, ~75 KB) — but only accumulates for its rows.
246	  - **pos** (4 rows × 128): trivially 4 owner-CTAs, each sums dh[t, s_owned] over
247	    its tokens. (mamba pos=8, vit pos=17 — same pattern.)
248	  - This is the ONLY surviving cross-CTA accumulation; it needs **P0 zero + B0**
249	    (the embedding accumulators) and is folded into P1's tail (no extra barrier).
250	
251	### 3.2 ViT (d=128, dff=512, kSeq=17, kNPatch=16, kPatch=49, V=97)

253	Same six GEMM families as decoder, **M-rows = T = B·kSeq = 4704·17 = 79,968**
254	(every position contributes — head uses CLS pos 0 only, M=B). Attention is **FULL
255	(no causal mask)** (`model_stage_vit.cuh:346`), so scores/ctx are S=17 square — still

257	embed, Linear(49→128)) — M=B·16=75,264, N=128, K=49 → m64n128k16 with K=49 padded

266	### 3.3 Mamba (d=128, d_inner=256, state=16, dt_rank=8, kSeq=8, V=97) — §8
