359	
360	### 5.1 Op-level dtype boundary (matches torch autocast)
361	
362	The owner's rule: bf16 storage + matmuls, **fp32 accumulators**, and autocast keeps
363	softmax/LN/CE/optimizer math fp32. Exact table:
364	
365	| op | inputs | compute | output stored | rationale |
366	|---|---|---|---|---|
367	| in_proj / out_proj / ff0 / ff2 / head / patch_proj (and all dX/dW) | **bf16** | wgmma, **fp32 acc** | bf16 acts / **fp32 grad** | autocast matmul boundary; grad stays fp32 for the optimizer |
368	| attention scores / softmax | bf16 q,k | **fp32** (dot + softmax) | bf16 weights | autocast keeps softmax fp32; tiny S so cost negligible |
369	| LayerNorm (fwd+bwd) | bf16 x | **fp32** (mean/var/normalize) | bf16 y; **fp32 xhat/inv cached** | autocast LN fp32; the two mean-correction terms need fp32 |
370	| GELU / SiLU / softplus | bf16 | **fp32** transcendental | bf16 | autocast elementwise upcast; exact-erf GELU (`dec_gelu:99`) |
371	| cross-entropy / NLL | fp32 logits | **fp32** (logsumexp), **fp64** loss reduce | fp32 grad | the 1e-5 loss rel-tol is the tightest gate (`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh:171`) |
372	| selective scan (mamba) | bf16 x_main, B, C | **fp32 scan state in registers** | bf16 y_scan | scan is memory-bound; fp32 state preserves the recurrence (`mb_scan_fwd:492`) |
373	| optimizer apply (all 11 tails) | fp32 grad + fp32 state | **fp32** | fp32 params + state | autocast never touches the optimizer; FusedOptState is fp32 |
374	
375	**Storage halving (the §4.3 budgets):** every `[kSeq×width]` smem activation array
376	in `DecSampleSmem` / `VitSampleSmem` / `MambaSampleSmem` becomes `__nv_bfloat16`;
377	the **LN caches (xhat, inv_std) and the fp32 reduction scratch `red[256]` stay
378	fp32** (they feed fp32 LN bwd). Decoder ~42→~21 KB, vit ~188→~94 KB, mamba ~145→~73
379	KB (computed in §4.3). New per-model smem budgets are the "+ bf16 halving" column.
380	
381	### 5.2 Parity gate (chaos-floor methodology — read the calibrated-gate comments)
382	
383	The existing gate (`tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py`) is explicit that an
384	**L3 loss-trajectory-vs-eager test is ill-posed** for the surrogate path (:8-16) and
385	that the faithful unit is the optimizer tail + a **grok smoke floor** (:27-31). For
386	the **real** TC cells the bf16 gate is therefore **tiered**, matching the L3-REAL
387	decoder gate at `:288-294`:
388	
389	1. **Single-step grad parity vs eager bf16-autocast** (NOT fp32 eager): build the
390	   eager model under `torch.autocast(bf16)`, one fwd+bwd, compare every weight grad.
391	   **Tolerance: rel ≤ 2e-2** 🟡 (bf16 has ~3 mantissa bits; this is the autocast
392	   round-off class, far looser than the fp32 gate's `1e-4` at `:292`). Loss rel ≤
393	   `1e-3` (logsumexp is fp32 so it stays tight).
394	2. **Determinism A/B/A:** run the cell 3× (A, B, A); assert run A == run A
395	   **bit-identically** (fixed tile ownership + fixed k-order + no float atomics
396	   guarantee it). B may differ from A only if B perturbs scheduling — it must not,
397	   so A==B==A bit-exact. This is the real witness that §3's determinism holds.
398	3. **Grok-floor (the chaos-robust gate):** 3 seeds, real model + the bf16-TC fused
399	   train step, must reach the grokking accuracy threshold (mirrors `:294` "must
400	   grok"). Because bf16 + reordered fp32 reductions make the **loss trajectory**
401	   chaotically diverge from eager (sensitive dependence — the calibrated-gate point
402	   at `:12-16`), the final-accuracy floor — not the trajectory — is the correct
403	   acceptance criterion for the bf16 cells.
404	
405	> 🟡 The 2e-2 grad tolerance is my estimate from the bf16 mantissa width; the build
406	> agent must **calibrate it against an eager-bf16 oracle** the same way the fp32
407	> gate was calibrated against fp64 (`:349-364`), and tighten if the oracle is closer.

443	## 7. Sort / SG2 (in-CTA bitonic sort + sequence-space partitioning)
444	
445	### 7.1 In-CTA bitonic sort (eliminate the host round-trip)
446	
447	SG2 currently sorts each tensor's flat grad by **|grad| ascending** on the **host**
448	(`torch.sort`, `opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:34-42`) and feeds `perm`/`unsort` into the
449	kernel. **Design: a STAGE -1 in-CTA bitonic sort** so the whole step is launch-free.
450	- Each CTA owns a whole tensor (tensor-per-CTA, `opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:64-66`),
451	  so the sort is **per-CTA over that tensor's N keys** — no cross-tensor crossing
452	  (the exact correctness hazard the header flags at :38-42).
453	- **Bitonic sorting network** — the standard nested form: outer `k` doubles 2→N
454	  (`ceil(log2 N)` levels), inner `j` halves k→1, giving **~½·(log₂N)²
455	  compare-exchange passes** total (N=512 → ~45 passes, N=65,536 → ~136 — NOT
456	  log₂N), each pass `__syncthreads`-separated over N/2 pairs (threads stride). Keys =
457	  `|grad[i]|` (fp32), payload = original index i → produces `perm`; `unsort` is the
458	  inverse scatter.
459	- **Determinism:** bitonic is a **fixed comparison network** (data-independent
460	  schedule) → deterministic. Ties: break by **ascending original index** (stable),
461	  matching the host sort's stable-sort contract. No atomics.
462	- **Cost/feasibility:** largest race param ~65,536 elems → ~136 compare-exchange
463	  passes × ~33K compares/pass = trivial vs the CSA/HCA attention that follows (still
464	  O(N·passes) ≪ the dense HCA's O(N·Nh·heads·head_dim)). Keys fit a per-CTA smem
465	  scratch (65,536×4 = 256 KB — **too large for one CTA's smem**); so for N > ~8192
466	  the sort is **global-memory bitonic** (compare-exchange in the tensor's HBM slice,
467	  `__syncthreads` per stage) — still launch-free, just not smem-resident. 🟡 For the
468	  race's small tensors (most are ≤512) the smem path applies. Drop-in as STAGE -1;
469	  the header is already written to accept it (`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:55-57`).
470	
471	### 7.2 Sequence-space partitioning of the SG2 meta-net (replace tensor-per-CTA)
472	
473	The current SG2 stage is **tensor-per-CTA** (one CTA does a whole tensor's
474	CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU), a conscious correctness-first divergence from design-req-#1
475	(`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh:97-119`) whose **cost** is owned: with ~30 tensors and
476	~132 SMs, ~100 CTAs pull an empty queue and idle, and one 256-thread CTA does each
477	tensor's entire (dense) HCA attention serially.
478	
479	**Design: sequence-space partitioning for the LARGE tensors.** The stage bodies
480	**already take explicit N/Nc/Nh and use CTA-cooperative grid-stride loops** (the
481	header author built for this — `:117-119`), so **only the outer driver changes**:
482	- For a large tensor, spread its N rows across **a cluster of CTAs** (or the whole
483	  grid for the single largest), with **one grid barrier after the compress stage**
484	  (so all compressed K/V are visible before attention/topk read them — the genuine
485	  cross-CTA coupling the header names at :100-104).
486	- Small tensors (which dominate the race's param *count*) stay **tensor-per-CTA**
487	  (one CTA, barrier-light) — a size threshold `SG_TUNED_SG2_SEQPART_MIN` routes.
488	- **Determinism preserved:** the compress/attention reductions are still
489	  owner-computes per output element in fixed order; the grid barrier only orders
490	  visibility, not summation order.
491	- This reuses the **same stage bodies** verbatim — the change is the row-ownership
492	  in the driver + one barrier, exactly the refactor the header was written to admit.
493	
494	---
495	
496	## 8. Mamba scan — confirm memory-roof-bound, design only what helps
497	
498	**Arithmetic intensity of the scan (computed reasoning).** Per (sample, channel j),
499	the scan does, over seq=8 and state=16: ~8×16 FMAs for h-update + 8×16 for y-accum
500	≈ **256 MAC = 512 FLOP/channel**. It reads x_main[8], dt_pre[8], Bmat[8×16],
501	Cmat[8×16], A_log[16] ≈ (8+8+128+128+16) bf16 = 288×2 = **576 B/channel**, writes
502	y_scan[8] = 16 B. AI ≈ 512 FLOP / 592 B ≈ **0.86 FLOP/B**. The roofline ridge for
503	bf16-TC is 989.4e12/3.35e12 ≈ **295 FLOP/B**. **0.86 ≪ 295 → the scan is deeply
504	memory-roof-bound** (by ~340×). This confirms the briefing and the header's own
505	"memory-roof-bound" framing.
506	
507	**Therefore for mamba:**
508	- **Do NOT** try to TC the scan (it is not a GEMM and is memory-bound anyway).
509	- **Keep fp32 scan state in registers** (`mb_scan_fwd:492` `h[kState]`,
510	  `mb_scan_bwd` `hh[kSeq+1][kState]`) — the seq=8 register exploit is correct and is
511	  what keeps smem off the 128 KB the naive h-in-smem would need (`model_stage_mamba3.cuh:74-88`).
512	- **bf16 storage** for the scan's inputs/outputs (x_main, B, C, y_scan) — halves the
513	  576 B/channel traffic → the direct multiplier on the memory-bound scan.
514	- **TC the projection GEMMs around the scan** (in_proj 128→512, out_proj 256→128,
515	  x_proj 256→40) — these ARE GEMMs (§3.3), M-rows=T=37,632, and tiling them with
516	  wgmma + Fork-B dW is the real mamba compute win. The scan sits between them as a
517	  register-resident barrier-free stage.
518	- **conv1d** (depthwise k=3, `mb_conv1d_fwd:420`) is also memory-bound (3 MACs/elem)
519	  → bf16 storage, kept scalar.
520	
521	Net mamba story: **Q5 (bf16) + Q2 (split-K dW) + tiled proj GEMMs**; the scan itself
522	is left as the proven register recurrence, only its operands go bf16.
523	
524	---
525	
526	## 9. Autotuner dims (new `-DSG_TUNED_*`, per-TU defaults)
527	
528	These ride the **existing kernel-autotuner mechanism** (`AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md`:
529	`compile.py` → `_kernel_tuned.json` → `setup.py TunedBuildExtension` injects per-TU
530	nvcc flags onto `launch_<opt>.cu` and `mega_<model>_<opt>.cu`). The current four
531	SAFE dims are block/vec/unroll/async_depth + maxrregcount (`AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md:21`).
532	The doc's note that "TMA/WGMMA/cluster macros are component-scoped, riskier, phase-2,
533	NOT emitted by the current pass" (`:30-31`) means these **new dims must be added to
534	`MACROS` in `_tuned_inject.py`** and to the per-TU pass (lockstep with the header
535	`#ifndef` guards — the unit test `tuning/test_build_injection` fails on drift,
536	`AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md:223-227`).
537	
538	| new macro | meaning | per-TU default (`#ifndef`) | search range |
539	|---|---|---|---|
540	| `SG_TUNED_TILE_M` | token-tile rows per CTA (the M_tile of §3) | **128** | {64,128,256} |
541	| `SG_TUNED_TILE_N` | wgmma N (output tile width) | **128** | {64,128,256} |
542	| `SG_TUNED_PIPE_DEPTH` | producer/consumer ring stages (§4.2) | **2** | {2,3,4} (smem-capped) |
543	| `SG_TUNED_WG_COUNT` | warpgroups/CTA (producer+consumer split) | **2** | {2} fixed phase-1; {2,4} phase-2 cooperative |
544	| `SG_TUNED_K_SAMPLES` | samples-per-CTA in the R1 scalar path (§6) | **4** | {1,2,4,8} |
545	| `SG_TUNED_CLUSTER_DIM` | cluster size for TMA-multicast weights (phase-2) | **1** | {1,2} (≤2 in persistent grid, `primitives.cuh:594`) |
546	| `SG_TUNED_SG2_SEQPART_MIN` | min tensor N for SG2 sequence-space partition (§7.2) | **8192** | {4096,8192,16384} |
547	
548	**Absent definitions yield a correct untuned kernel** (contract rule 3,
549	`COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md:28-31`): default M_tile=128, depth=2, etc. all compose into
550	a valid cell. **Do not touch the Optuna optimizer-hyperparameter tuner in `tuning/`**
551	— that is a separate system (the briefing and `AUTOTUNE_LINKAGE.md` both stress this;
552	this is the **kernel** autotuner).
553	
554	---
555	
556	## 10. Validation + measurement plan
557	
558	### 10.1 Per-phase gates
559	
560	| phase | gate |
561	|---|---|
562	| R1 split-K dW (scalar) | grad parity vs current cell **bit-identical** (same fp32 math, just output-stationary; ascending-t order matches the old ascending-CTA reduce *only if* both sum T in the same order — verify, the order changed from CTA-major to t-major so it is fp32-rel ≤ 1e-5, **not** bit-exact) 🟡 |
563	| R1 bf16 storage | grad parity vs eager-bf16, rel ≤ 2e-2 (§5.2); grok-floor 3 seeds |
564	| R2 wgmma per GEMM | **SASS audit** (§10.3) + single-step grad parity vs eager-bf16 |
565	| R2 full cell | determinism A/B/A bit-exact; grok-floor 3 seeds; occupancy-refuse test (force a too-large smem config, assert `cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources`, **no hang**) |
566	| recomposition (every phase) | all 33 cells regenerate from `megakernel_codegen.py`; `git diff` generator-consistent (`COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md:5,37`); out-of-tree portability TU compiles (rule 4) |
567	
568	### 10.2 Roofline protocol per cell (the owner's metric)
569	
570	Reuse `tuning/roofline.py`'s **timed-FLOPs methodology** (ncu blocked —
571	ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM, `roofline.py:5`): achieved = FLOPs_per_step / wall_per_step;
572	wall = CUDA-synced over 100 steps after 25 warmup, **quiet-GPU window** (no other
573	process — the 3 grok-smoke + tuner fleet must be idle for the measurement window).
574	Ceiling = min(bf16_tc_peak, AI·HBM_BW); fraction = achieved/ceiling. **Per-pipeline
575	precision = bf16** now (the cells compute bf16), so the ceiling is the **989.4 TF/s
576	BF16 line** (`roofline.py:287`, `_PRECISION_PEAK['bf16']`), not tf32.
577	
578	### 10.3 SASS audit checklist (per cell .so)
579	
580	`cuobjdump -sass <mega_model_opt>.o | grep -E ...`:
581	- ✔ `WGMMA` present (the in-kernel tensor-core MMA — absence = scalar fallback shipped).
582	- ✔ `wgmma.wait_group` / `wgmma.commit_group` present (pipeline correctness).
583	- ✔ cp.async (`LDGSTS`) present (phase-1 staging) / `UTMALDG` (phase-2 TMA).
584	- ✔ `setmaxnreg` (`R2UR`/the warpgroup reg ops) present (producer/consumer split).
585	- ✔ **no `STL`/`LDL` spills** in the consumer wgmma loop (register pressure check;
586	  the `--maxrregcount` tuned dim exists to fix this if it appears).
587	
588	### 10.4 Step-time budget table (projection; decoder, bf16)
589	
590	| component | µs (projected) | basis |
591	|---|---|---|
592	| fwd+bwd GEMMs (TC) | ~60–90 µs 🟡 | 45 µs bf16 floor ÷ ~0.5–0.75 achievable roof (§3 per-GEMM classes, occ=1) |
593	| acts HBM round-trip (Fork B) | ~11.5 µs | 39 MB / 3.35 TB/s (computed §1.3) |
594	| grid barriers (2, Fork B) | ~2–4 µs 🟡 | 2 × ~1–2 µs (`__nanosleep` backoff rendezvous, no co-residency stall at occ=1) |
595	| elementwise (LN/GELU/softmax/CE, fp32) | ~10–20 µs 🟡 | small S; dominated by the 99-wide CE logsumexp × B |
596	| optimizer tail (fused, adamw) | ~5–8 µs 🟡 | 422,755 elems × (read g + r/w m,v + w param) ≈ 8.5 MB / 3.35 TB/s ≈ 2.5 µs + overhead |
597	| **total / step** | **~90–135 µs** 🟡 | → **~7,500–11,000 steps/s** |
598	| **roofline fraction** | **~35–50%** 🟡 | achieved (45 GFLOP / ~110 µs ≈ 410 GF/s) / 989 TF/s — memory-bound, so read against AI·BW: at AI≈45GFLOP/50MB≈900 FLOP/B the cell is **compute-bound** and the fraction is GEMM-roof-limited ~0.5 |
599	
600	> 🟡 The whole budget is a **no-silicon projection** (no GPU runs permitted here; the
601	> 3 grok-smoke + tuner processes are live). The achievable-roof column is the honest
602	> uncertainty: short-K GEMMs at occ=1 will not hit peak. The build agent measures
603	> the real numbers via §10.2 and the SASS audit confirms the instructions are
604	> present.
605	
606	---
607	
608	## 11. Effort / sequencing (day-level; substrate vs per-header)
609	
610	| phase | work | substrate vs header | recompose+validate | days 🟡 |
611	|---|---|---|---|---|
612	| **R1.1** | k-samples-per-CTA in `dec_/vit_/mb_linear` + dW loops | per-header (3 model headers) | regen 33 cells, parity + grok-floor | 1–2 |
613	| **R1.2** | split-K output-stationary dW (kills partials) + embedding owner-map | per-header (3) + phase struct in 3 `fused_*_megakernel.cuh` | bit/rel grad parity, drop B1 phase | 2 |
614	| **R1.3** | bf16 scalar storage (§5 dtype table) | per-header (3 SampleSmem structs) | eager-bf16 parity (calibrate tol), re-check smem budgets | 1–2 |
615	| **R2.1** | new `wgmma.cuh` substrate (ss-wgmma PTX + smem descriptors) + SASS verify on a microbench | **substrate** (1 new header) | SASS audit (WGMMA present) | 3–5 (the hard part) |
616	| **R2.2** | producer/consumer pipeline (mbarrier ring + cp.async staging) in a shared GEMM helper | **substrate** (extend `wgs::`) | per-GEMM grad parity | 2–3 |
617	| **R2.3** | wire wgmma GEMMs into the 3 model headers (replace scalar dots; keep scores/ctx/scan scalar) | per-header (3) | full-cell parity + determinism A/B/A + roofline | 2–3 |
618	| **R2.4** | TMA (host descriptors + `cp.async.bulk.tensor`) — phase-2 optional | substrate + autotuner dims | SASS (UTMALDG), roofline delta | 2–3 |
619	| **R2.5** | SG2 in-CTA bitonic sort (STAGE -1) + sequence-space partition driver | per-header (`opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh` driver) | SG2 parity (1e-5) + determinism | 2–3 |
620	| **autotuner** | add 7 `SG_TUNED_*` to `_tuned_inject.py` MACROS + pass | tooling | `tuning/test_build_injection` | 1 |
621	
622	**Substrate work** (inherited by all 33 cells): `wgmma.cuh`, the `wgs::` pipeline
623	extension, the TMA descriptors, the new autotuner macros. **Per-header work** (lands
624	once per model, recomposed across all 11 optimizers): the k-samples / split-K / bf16
625	edits and the wgmma wiring in the 3 `model_stage_*.cuh` + 3 `fused_*_megakernel.cuh`.
626	**Optimizer headers** are largely untouched except §4's epilogue-fusion (§ below).
627	
628	**Recomposition cost per phase** is one `megakernel_codegen.py` run + the parity
629	suite + a quiet-window roofline pass; it is dominated by the **per-cell CUTLASS-free
630	nvcc compile** (the cells are header-only; no CUTLASS in the L3 path, so the heavy
631	`mma.cuh` TUs are NOT rebuilt). Heavy-TU serial-compile OOM (`mma.cuh:384-396`) does
632	**not** apply to the L3 cells — another reason the in-kernel wgmma path is preferred
633	over dragging CUTLASS device-side.
634	
635	---
636	
637	## Appendix A — Optimizer epilogue-fusion verdict table (Q3)
638	
639	The dW tile is **register-resident** at the end of P1's dW GEMM (the fp32
640	accumulator fragment). An optimizer whose apply is **element-local** can run **in
641	that epilogue**, before the fragment is stored — eliminating B1+P2 (the grad never
642	leaves registers for those tails). Verdict per the 11 (apply math is
643	`opt_components.cuh:184-254`):
644	
645	| optimizer | element-local apply? | epilogue-fusable? | what it needs before apply | fallback if not fused |
646	|---|---|---|---|---|
647	| **AdamW** | yes (m,v,param all element-local, `adamw_step`) | **✔ FUSE** | bc1/bc2 (host scalars) | — |
648	| **Lion** | yes (`lion_step`, m only) | **✔ FUSE** | — | — |
649	| **Grokfast** | yes (EMA fused in apply, `opt_stages_precompute.cuh:52`) | **✔ FUSE** | — | — |
650	| **GrokAdamW** | yes (EMA fused, `:53`) | **✔ FUSE** | — | — |
651	| **NeuralGrok** | yes (psi MLP inline, `opt_components.cuh:222-229`) | **✔ FUSE** | psi-net weights (per-tensor, in `extra`) | — |
652	| **Prodigy** | apply is element-local BUT needs **global d** first | **✗ stage** | `d_factor` = cross-ALL-tensors r/s reduce (`opt_stages_precompute.cuh:58`) | precompute-d phase (B) **before** P2; order: P1 dW → B → d-reduce → B → apply |
653	| **Muon** | NO — needs Newton–Schulz on the **full matrix** | **✗ NOT fusable** | NS orth direction (5 matmul iters, `:59`) | keep staged: P1 dW → B → NS phase → B → apply (`muon_update_step`) |
654	| **SuperGrok11** | apply element-local; needs **per-tensor gate** | **✗ stage (light)** | one per-tensor cosine reduction (`:60`, single-drain, no grid barrier) | per-tensor mu+gate stage before apply (CTA-local, barrier-free) |
655	| **SuperGrok15** | apply element-local; gate is a **host scalar** | **partial** — mu is element-local, gate host-set | mu meta-MLP forward (`:62`); gate via `FusedScalars.gate` | mu stage before apply (gate already a scalar → no reduce) |
656	| **SuperGrok2** | apply is Adam on `smart_grad` | **✗ separate tail** | the whole CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net (§7) produces `smart_grad` | the SG2 in-kernel meta stages (own phase), then Adam apply |
657	
658	**Summary:** **5 of 11 fully epilogue-fusable** (adamw/lion/grokfast/grokadamw/
659	neuralgrok → 2 phases / 1 barrier). Prodigy/SG11/SG15 need **one reduction phase
660	before apply** (3 phases / 2 barriers). **Muon and SG2 are NOT fusable** — they keep
661	their multi-phase staged structure (NS orthogonalization / meta-net), which is
662	correct and faithful to the per-op pipelines (`opt_components.cuh:19-27`). The
663	fusion is a per-optimizer codegen branch in the cell template — it lands in
664	`fused_megakernel.cuh`'s phase selection, inherited by all model×opt combos.
665	
666	## Appendix B — What is explicitly NOT done (road not taken)
667	
668	- **Host-CUTLASS GEMMs (`mma.cuh`) for the L3 cells: REJECTED.** CUTLASS collectives
669	  are not device-callable (own their TMA mainloop, `mma.cuh:145-153`), and ~15–30
670	  host launches/step **without CUDA graphs** is pure launch overhead that swamps the
671	  45 µs compute floor. The owner forbids graphs and mandates one persistent kernel.
672	  ∴ in-kernel wgmma is the only consistent path. (`mma.cuh` stays for the L1 per-op
673	  Muon/SG2 paths it already serves.)
674	- **Global per-layer grid barrier (the briefing's literal Q1 phrasing): REJECTED** —
675	  it serializes the grid L×#GEMMs/step. Fork B keeps fwd→bwd CTA-local.
676	- **DSMEM cluster reduce for dW: NOT USED** — Fork B has no dW reduce.
677	- **TF32 path: NOT the race precision** — bf16 is (owner decision); TF32 stays only
678	  as the `mma.cuh` fp32-accuracy fallback for L1.
679	- **FP8: out of scope** — not in the owner's precision decision; the roofline tracks
680	  it only as a drawn ceiling (`roofline.py:51`).
681

content.content:
1	# Mamba-3 (SISO) Reference — Reversible Foundation
2	
3	Reference implementation of the **full Llama-style Mamba-3** model for the
4	`mamba` model. Source paper: **arXiv 2603.15569** (ICLR 2026), *"Mamba-3:
5	Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles"* (Lahoti, Li, Chen,
6	Wang, Bick, Kolter, Dao, Gu). Full text read at `/tmp/mamba3_paper.txt`.
7	
8	- Code: `grokking_optimizers/mamba3_block.py` (`Mamba3Layer` mixer, `SwiGLU_MLP`,
9	  `Mamba3Block`, `Mamba3Model`, `RMSNorm`)
10	- Oracle: `tests/hw/mamba3_oracle.py` (fp64; forward + VERIFIED hand-derived
11	  manual backward that matches autograd to **≤4e-15** per param + input — §4, §6, §7)
12	
13	The SSM mixer is the **SISO base** Mamba-3 (the MIMO variant of §3.3 is a
14	documented later option, §5). The **architecture is now the complete Llama-style
15	stack** of Section 3.4: each layer alternates a **Mamba-3 mixer** sub-block and a
16	**SwiGLU MLP** sub-block, both pre-norm + residual (`h = h + Mixer(RMSNorm(h))`,
17	then `h = h + SwiGLU(RMSNorm(h))`). With the SwiGLU blocks added, the canonical
18	`d=2048 / nl=24 / MLP-inner-4096` config reaches the paper's **~1.5B** (the
19	previous mixer-only reference was 0.661B). It is NOT wired into production, the
20	CUDA megakernel is untouched, and nothing is committed. The CUDA megakernel
21	transcribes its forward + backward line-for-line from this reference and the
22	verified manual backward in §6 (mixer) and §7 (SwiGLU + pre-norm/residual).
23	
24	---
25	
26	## 1. Exact forward equations implemented
27	
28	Per token. Quantity layout (RESOLVED against paper Sec 3.3 line 501-504 +
29	App C line 1661-1663 — the P=`head_dim` channels in a head **share** `alpha,dt,
30	B,C`; B,C,θ are shared across **all** heads via multi-value attention):
31	
32	| Quantity | scope | shape per token |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| `dt`, `A_real`, `lambda` | **per head** | `[n_heads]` |
35	| `theta`, `B`, `Bhat`, `C`, `Chat` | **head-shared** (all heads) | `[N_c]` |
36	| `x` (SSM input), `D` skip, `z` gate | **per channel** | `[d_inner]` |
37	
38	State is **real**, size `N = state_dim`, viewed as `N_c = N/2` complex
39	coordinates (a 2-vector `(real, imag)` each); the full SSM state is
40	`[n_heads, head_dim, N_c, 2]` — within a head all `head_dim` channels evolve with
41	the SAME `alpha_t`, `R_t` and head-shared `Bbar_t`, differing only through `x`.
42	
43	### 1.1 Exponential-trapezoidal discretization (Section 3.1, Prop 1, Eq 5–6; Table 1 last row)
44	
45	The continuous LTV SSM `h'(t) = A(t)h(t) + B(t)x(t)`, `y = C(t)^T h(t)` is
46	discretized with the **exponential-trapezoidal** rule to the **3-term** recurrence:
47	
48	```
49	h_t = alpha_t * h_{t-1}  +  beta_t * B_{t-1} x_{t-1}  +  gamma_t * B_t x_t      (Eq 6)
50	```
51	
52	with coefficients (Eq 5 / Table 1):
53	
54	```
55	alpha_t = exp(dt_t * A_t)                                  # decay
56	beta_t  = (1 - lambda_t) * dt_t * exp(dt_t * A_t)          # = (1-lambda_t)*dt_t*alpha_t
57	gamma_t = lambda_t * dt_t
58	```
59	
60	`lambda_t ∈ [0,1]` is a **data-dependent** convex-combination gate.
61	`lambda_t = 1` → Mamba-2 exponential-Euler; `lambda_t = 1/2` → classical
62	trapezoid (Remark 2). **Default parameterization** (Appendix A.3, Table 8 — best
63	ppl): `lambda_t = sigmoid(u_t)` with `u_t` a learned linear projection of the
64	token; the `lambda_t = 1/2 + O(dt)` constraint is intentionally **not** enforced.
65	
66	### 1.2 Complex state via the "RoPE trick" (Section 3.2; Prop 2, Prop 4; Eq 8, 9, 25)
67	
68	The SSM is complex (Eq 8): transition `Diag(A(t) + i*theta(t))`, complex
69	projections `(B + i*Bhat)`, `(C + i*Chat)`. Proposition 2 (Eq 9) shows the
70	discretized complex SSM of complex-dim `N_c` equals a **real** SSM of state dim
71	`N = 2*N_c` whose transition is a scalar decay × block-diagonal of 2×2 rotations:
72	
73	```
74	R(phi) = [[cos phi, -sin phi],
75	          [sin phi,  cos phi]]
76	R_t    = blockdiag_{i=1..N_c} R(dt_t * theta_t[i])
77	Bbar_t = [ B_t ; Bhat_t ]   in R^N        # real/imag stacked per complex coord
78	Cbar_t = [ C_t ; -Chat_t ]  in R^N
79	```
80	
81	Combined with exponential-trapezoidal (Proposition 4, **Eq 25**, the
82	direct-rotation real form), the recurrence we run is:
83	
84	```
85	h_t = alpha_t * (R_t @ h_{t-1})
86	      + beta_t  * (R_t @ (Bbar_{t-1} * x_{t-1}))
87	      + gamma_t *        (Bbar_t     * x_t)                 (Eq 25)
88	y_t = Cbar_t^T @ h_t
89	```
90	
91	For complex coord `i`, the 2-vector `h_t[i]` is rotated by `R(dt_t*theta_t[i])`;
92	`B,C` act as scalars on `x_t`; `y_t` is the **real part** of the complex inner
93	product (`Cbar = [C, -Chat]` encodes the `Re(...)` of Eq 8's output). With `dt`
94	per-head and `theta` head-shared, the angle is `phi[h,i] = dt[h]*theta[i]`
95	(**per-head per-coord** `[n_heads, N_c]` — exact, no mean-over-channels approx).
96	
97	> **Why Eq 25 and not Eq 11/24 (cumulative-product RoPE form)?** They are
98	> algebraically identical (Prop 4 proof, Appendix B.3). Eq 25 applies `R_t`
99	> **per step** inside the recurrence — the cleanest *sequential* form for a CUDA
100	> kernel to transcribe line-for-line. The cumulative-product `prod R^T` form is
101	> the optimization for the *parallel/chunked matmul* path; the kernel phase can
102	> switch to it if it implements the chunked SSD algorithm.
103	
104	### 1.3 Data-dependent A (Remark 1)
105	
106	All SSM params are data-dependent. Real part `A_t < 0` is a **scalar per head**
107	(Eq 8/9/17: "`A_t ∈ R` is a scalar so that `exp(dt·A_t)` commutes with rotations",
108	paper proof line ~1431; Mamba-2's scalar-identity transition), from a base
109	**per-head** rate `A_log` (Mamba-2 init `log(arange(1..n_heads))`) plus a
110	data-dependent **per-head** log-rate `A_mod`, mapped through
111	`A_t = -softplus(A_mod + exp(A_log))` so `alpha_t = exp(dt_t*A_t) ∈ (0,1]`, with
112	`dt_t = softplus(dt_proj(.)) > 0` (also per head). The rotation `R_t` (built from
113	`theta`) carries the per-coordinate structure; the real part stays scalar.
114	Imaginary part `theta_t` is a free head-shared data-dependent linear projection
115	(rotation frequency); per-step angle `phi_t[h,i] = dt_t[h] * theta_t[i]`.
116	
117	### 1.4 BCNorm + B,C biases (Section 3.4; Appendix F, Table 10)
118	
119	After the `B`,`C` projections: **RMSNorm** (BCNorm / QKNorm) over the state dim,
120	then add learnable, **data-independent, channel-wise** biases to **both** `B` and
121	`C` (added *after* the norm), **initialized to all-ones** (Appendix F default,
122	Table 10a). These biases inject the convolution-like data-independent component
123	that (with the trapezoidal implicit conv) replaces the short conv.
124	
125	### 1.5 Mixer-block scaffold (Section 3.4 / Fig. 2; Appendix C)
126	
127	```
128	residual = x
129	xz = in_proj(x);  x_main, z = xz.chunk(2)        # no bias
130	x_in = x_main                                     # NO conv1d AND NO SiLU (see §5)
131	(dt, A_real, theta, lambda, B, C) = x_proj(x_in)  # all data-dependent
132	y = mamba3_scan(x_in, dt, A_real, phi, lambda, Bbar, Cbar)   # Eq 25
133	y = y + x_in * D                                  # per-channel D skip
134	y = y * SiLU(z)                                   # gate: phi(Y,Z)=Y(.)SiLU(Z)  (App C, Eq C)
135	out = out_proj(y)                                 # no bias
136	return out (+ residual if self.residual)          # see §1.6 — OFF in Mamba3Block
137	```
138	
139	The output gate `· SiLU(z)` is RETAINED (App C: `φ(Y,Z) := Y ⊙ SiLU(Z)`); only
140	the SSM-input SiLU is dropped. `Mamba3Layer` has a `residual` flag: `True`
141	(default) keeps the Mamba-1/-2 drop-in contract (`out + x`); the Llama-style
142	`Mamba3Model` constructs the mixer with `residual=False` and adds the residual
143	around the pre-norm at the **block** level (§1.6).
144	
145	### 1.6 Llama-style architecture: alternating Mamba-3 mixer + SwiGLU (Section 3.4)
146	
147	> Section 3.4: *"The overall architecture follows Llama (Grattafiori et al.
148	> 2024), **alternating Mamba-3 and SwiGLU blocks with pre-norm**."*
149	
150	Each `Mamba3Block` is **one Llama layer** = a Mamba-3 mixer sub-block then a
151	SwiGLU MLP sub-block, each pre-norm + residual:
152	
153	```
154	h = h + Mamba3Mixer( RMSNorm_mix(h) )      # mixer residual=False (added here)
155	h = h + SwiGLU_MLP ( RMSNorm_mlp(h) )      # SwiGLU feed-forward
156	```
157	
158	`Mamba3Model`: `tok+pos` embeddings → `nl` × `Mamba3Block` → final `RMSNorm` →
159	`Linear(d, p)` head on the **last** token; CE loss. The Mamba-2 **post-gate
160	RMSNorm is removed** (BCNorm stabilizes; Section 3.4) — only the single final
161	RMSNorm before the head remains.
162	
163	**Alternation convention (RESOLVED — Convention A, "n of each"):** `nl` counts
164	the **mixer** blocks; **each is paired with a SwiGLU MLP**, so the canonical
165	config has **24 Mamba-3 mixers + 24 SwiGLU blocks**. This is the Mamba-2
166	convention the paper explicitly follows (Appendix D: *"pretraining procedures
167	follow those of Dao and Gu (2024)"*), and it is the convention that makes the
168	canonical config (`d_model=2048`, `nl=24`, MLP inner 4096, Llama-3.1 vocab
169	128256, **tied** embeddings) land at **~1.5B** (measured 1.5277B; §3). The
170	alternative "24 total = 12 mixer + 12 SwiGLU" gives only 0.895B and is rejected.
171	
172	**SwiGLU MLP** (`SwiGLU_MLP`, the standard Llama feed-forward, **no biases**):
173	
174	```
175	SwiGLU(x) = down_proj( SiLU(gate_proj(x)) ⊙ up_proj(x) )
176	```
177	
178	with three bias-free `Linear`s, inner ("MLP"/"hidden") dim `d_ff`. At the 1.5B
179	scale `d_ff = 4096 = 2·d_model` (Appendix C Table: *"SISO MLP dim … 1.5B:
180	4,096"*; Appendix D fixes the expand factor at 2). The default `mlp_ratio=2`
181	reproduces 4096 at d=2048. The paper states **4096 directly**, so we use it as-is
182	and do **not** re-apply the classic Llama `2/3` factor (it is already folded into
183	the stated 4096). The MIMO variant shrinks this to 3824 to parameter-match SISO
184	(Appendix C); SISO uses the full 4096. **Backward in §7.**

188	## 2. Key differences vs the current Mamba-1 `SelectiveSSMLayer`
189	
190	| Aspect | Mamba-1 (`SelectiveSSMLayer`, grokking_race_v2.py:412) | Mamba-3 (`Mamba3Layer`) |
191	|---|---|---|
192	| **Short conv1d** | depthwise `Conv1d(k=3)` on `x_main` (NON-causal) | **DROPPED** — trapezoidal implicit conv + B,C biases subsume it (Sec 3.1.2, 4.2) |
193	| **SSM-input SiLU** | `SiLU` after the conv on `x_main` | **DROPPED** — conv "and its accompanying activation function" obviated (Sec 3.4) |
194	| **`dt` / `A` / `lambda` scope** | per-channel `dt`; `A=-exp(A_log)` per `[d_inner,N]` | **per head** (`P` channels in a head share `alpha,dt,B`; Sec 3.3, App C) |
195	| **Discretization** | exponential-**Euler**, 2-term: `h = exp(dt·A)h + dt·B·x` | exponential-**trapezoidal**, 3-term: `+ beta·B_{t-1}x_{t-1}` (Eq 6) |
196	| **State** | **real** diagonal, `A = -exp(A_log)` (real eigenvalues) | **complex**, `A = A_real + i·theta`; real form = decay × 2×2 rotations (Prop 2) |
197	| **State tracking** | cannot (real eigenvalues) — fails parity | can (rotations) — solves parity / modular arithmetic (Table 5b) |
198	| **`lambda` (trapezoid gate)** | n/a | `lambda_t = sigmoid(u_t)`, data-dependent (App A.3) |
199	| **B,C normalization** | none | **BCNorm** (RMSNorm) on B,C (Sec 3.4) |
200	| **B,C biases** | none | learnable all-ones-init channel-wise biases on B,C (App F) |
201	| **Per-layer norm** | post-`LayerNorm` inside the block | **Llama pre-norm**: RMSNorm before the mixer AND before the SwiGLU MLP; model-level final RMSNorm; post-gate norm removed (Sec 3.4) |
202	| **Norm type** | LayerNorm | RMSNorm |
203	| **Gate** | `(y + D·x)·SiLU(z)` | same scaffold: `(y + D·x)·SiLU(z)` (App C `phi`) |
204	| **MLP / feed-forward** | none (mixer-only stack) | **SwiGLU MLP** alternating with the mixer, Llama-style (Sec 3.4); `down(SiLU(gate)⊙up)`, inner 4096 at 1.5B (§1.6, §7) |
205	| **Model architecture** | embed → `nl` mixers → norm → head | embed → `nl`×(mixer + SwiGLU) blocks, pre-norm → norm → head (Llama, Sec 3.4) |

293	- **RESOLVED — SiLU on the SSM input is DROPPED.** Paper Sec 3.4 (line 678):
294	  exponential-trapezoidal discretization + B,C biases "obviate the short causal
295	  convolution **and its accompanying activation function** present in Mamba-2".
296	  So `x_main` feeds the projections and the scan **directly** (`x_in = x_main`,
297	  no `SiLU`, no conv). The **output gate** `· SiLU(z)` is a *different*, retained
298	  activation (App C, `φ(Y,Z) := Y ⊙ SiLU(Z)`) and stays.
299	
300	- **RESOLVED — `dt` (and `A_real`, `lambda`) are PER HEAD.** Paper Sec 3.3
301	  (line 501-504): the SISO recurrence is stacked over the `P = head_dim` channels
302	  of a head "with `P` copies **sharing the same `alpha_t`, `dt_t` and `B_t`**";
303	  App C (line 1661-1663) confirms B,C are `N·R` (head-shared) and the per-head
304	  input `x` is `P`-dim. So `dt`, the scalar `A_real`, and `lambda` are **per
305	  head** (`[n_heads]`), `theta/B/C` are **head-shared** (`[N_c]`), `x/D/z` are
306	  **per channel** (`[d_inner]`). The rotation angle `phi[h,i] = dt[h]·theta[i]`
307	  is therefore **per-head per-coord** and **EXACT** — the old per-channel-mean(dt)
308	  approximation is gone. `dt_proj` now emits `n_heads`; `x_proj` emits `n_heads`

312	  real **scalar** (`A(t) ∈ R`, paper line 365; "scalar so that `exp(dt·A_t)`
313	  commutes with rotations", line ~1431); the rotation `R_t` carries the
314	  per-coordinate structure (Mamba-2's scalar-identity transition). Base per-head
315	  rate `A_log = log(arange(1..n_heads))`, plus per-head `A_mod`, then
316	  `A_real = -softplus(A_mod + exp(A_log))`. (Previously this was an

373	## 6. The DERIVED backward (mixer — verified, transcribe the CUDA kernel from this)
374	
375	This is the hand-derived, NON-autograd backward implemented in
376	`tests/hw/mamba3_oracle.py` (`scan_backward`, `layer_backward`,
377	`model_backward`) and **verified to match `torch.autograd` to ≤7e-15 relative**
378	in fp64 for every parameter and the input (§4 (F)). The CUDA megakernel
379	transcribes the math below line-for-line. Notation matches §1: per-head scalars
380	`alpha_t[h], beta_t[h], gamma_t[h]`; head-shared `theta_t[c]`; head-shared
381	`Bbar_t[c]=(Br,Bi)`, `Cbar_t[c]=(Cr,-Ci)` (2-vectors); per-channel input
382	`x_t[h,p]`. State `h_t[b,h,p,c,:]` is a 2-vector per complex coord `c`.
383	
384	### 6.1 Forward (the exact recurrence the backward inverts)
385	
386	```
387	alpha_t[h] = exp(dt[t,h] * A_real[t,h])          # in (0,1]
388	gamma_t[h] = lambda[t,h] * dt[t,h]
389	beta_t[h]  = (1 - lambda[t,h]) * dt[t,h] * alpha_t[h]
390	phi_t[h,c] = dt[t,h] * theta[t,c]                # per-head per-coord angle
391	R(phi) @ (w0,w1) = (cos*w0 - sin*w1,  sin*w0 + cos*w1)
392	v_t[b,h,p,c] = Bbar_t[c] * x_t[b,h,p]            # 2-vector (Br*x, Bi*x)
393	
394	h_t = alpha_t * (R_t @ h_{t-1}) + beta_t * (R_t @ v_{t-1}) + gamma_t * v_t
395	y_t[b,h,p] = sum_{c,d} Cbar_t[c,d] * h_t[b,h,p,c,d]      # h_{-1}=v_{-1}=0
396	```
397	
398	### 6.2 Scan backward — reverse-time recurrence (`t = L-1 … 0`)
399	
400	Carry **TWO** adjoints (this is the key structure):
401	- `gh[b,h,p,c,:] = dL/dh_t` — flows back through `h_{t+1} = alpha R h_t + …`;
402	- `gv[b,h,p,c,:] = dL/dv_t` — accumulated from step `t+1`'s β-term
403	  `beta_{t+1} R_{t+1} v_t`. **This is the width-2 coupling** (`v_{t-1}` feeds both
404	  step `t-1`'s γ-term and step `t`'s β-term) — the #1 index-bug site. Both carries
405	  start at 0.
406	
407	At step `t`, given `gh` (carried from `t+1`, = grad through future `h`'s) and
408	`gv` (carried from `t+1`'s β-term):
409	
410	```
411	# (1) output: y_t = sum Cbar_t · h_t
412	gh          += Cbar_t * dy_t                               # now gh = full dL/dh_t
413	dCbar[t,c,d] = sum_{b,h,p}  h_t[b,h,p,c,d] * dy_t[b,h,p]   # Cbar head-shared
414	
415	# (2) v_t total grad = (gv from t+1 β-term) + (γ-term at t)
416	dv_t          = gv + gamma_t * gh
417	dx[t,h,p]    += sum_{c,d} dv_t[...,c,d] * Bbar_t[c,d]      # x per channel
418	dBbar[t,c,d] += sum_{b,h,p} dv_t[...,c,d] * x_t[b,h,p]     # Bbar head-shared
419	
420	# (3) coefficient + angle grads.  Rh = R_t @ h_{t-1},  Rv = R_t @ v_{t-1}
421	dalpha[b,t,h] += sum_{p,c,d} Rh * gh         # per head: sum over p,c,d
422	dbeta [b,t,h] += sum_{p,c,d} Rv * gh
423	dgamma[b,t,h] += sum_{p,c,d} v_t * gh
424	# phi via R'(phi) = [[-sin,-cos],[cos,-sin]].  For a term coef*R@w, adjoint g:
425	#   dphi += coef*( g0*(-sin*w0 - cos*w1) + g1*(cos*w0 - sin*w1) )
426	dphi[b,t,h,c] += sum_p [ alpha_t * R'term(h_{t-1}[..,c]) + beta_t * R'term(v_{t-1}[..,c]) ]
427	
428	# (4) propagate to the previous step.  R orthogonal -> adjoint = R^T = R(-phi):
429	#   R^T @ g = (cos*g0 + sin*g1,  -sin*g0 + cos*g1)
430	gv  = beta_t  * (R_t^T @ gh)      # becomes dL/dv_{t-1}  -> carried to step t-1
431	gh  = alpha_t * (R_t^T @ gh)      # becomes dL/dh_{t-1}
432	```
433	
434	At `t=0`, `h_{-1}=v_{-1}=0`, so `Rh=Rv=0` (their α/β/φ contributions vanish) and
435	the final `gh,gv` multiply into the zero initial state and are discarded.
436	
437	### 6.3 Fold the per-head coefficient Jacobians
438	
439	With `alpha = exp(dt·A_real)`, `beta = (1-lambda)·dt·alpha`, `gamma = lambda·dt`,
440	`phi = dt·theta`:
441	
442	```
443	ddt[t,h]     = dalpha*(A_real*alpha)
444	             + dbeta*((1-lambda)*alpha*(1 + dt*A_real))
445	             + dgamma*lambda
446	             + sum_c  dphi[t,h,c]*theta[t,c]          # (post-softplus dt)
447	dlambda[t,h] = dbeta*(-dt*alpha) + dgamma*dt          # (w.r.t. lambda)
448	dA_real[t,h] = dalpha*(dt*alpha) + dbeta*((1-lambda)*dt^2*alpha)
449	dtheta[t,c]  = sum_h  dphi[t,h,c]*dt[t,h]             # theta head-shared
450	```
451	
452	(`dalpha/d(dt)=A·alpha`, `dalpha/dA=dt·alpha`; `dbeta/d(dt)=(1-λ)·alpha·(1+dt·A)`,
453	`dbeta/dλ=-dt·alpha`, `dbeta/dA=(1-λ)·dt²·alpha`; `dgamma/d(dt)=λ`, `dgamma/dλ=dt`;
454	`dphi/d(dt)=theta`, `dphi/dtheta=dt`.)
455	
456	### 6.4 Through the projections (the rest of the layer)
457	
458	```
459	# softplus / sigmoid Jacobians (dt_pre = dt_proj output, u_lam pre-sigmoid):
460	ddt_pre  = ddt    * sigmoid(dt_pre)                  # dt = softplus(dt_pre)
461	du_lam   = dlambda * lambda*(1-lambda)               # lambda = sigmoid(u_lam)
462	# A_real = -softplus(A_arg), A_arg = A_mod + exp(A_log):
463	dA_arg   = dA_real * (-sigmoid(A_arg))
464	dA_mod   = dA_arg
465	dA_log[h]= sum_{b,t} dA_arg[b,t,h] * exp(A_log[h])   # d(exp(A_log))/dA_log = exp(A_log)
466	
467	# Cbar=(Cr2,-Ci2), Bbar=(Br2,Bi2):  dCr2=dCbar[..,0], dCi2=-dCbar[..,1],
468	#                                    dBr2=dBbar[..,0], dBi2= dBbar[..,1]
469	# each B/C stream: +bias then RMSNorm  (bias grad = sum over b,l; then RMSNorm bwd)
470	dB_bias = sum_{b,l} dBr2 ; ... ; (dBr, dB_norm.w) = rmsnorm_bwd(dBr2, …) ; etc.
471	
472	# ddt_pre -> dt_proj backward (weight+bias) -> ddt_lr
473	# reassemble x_proj output grad: cat[ddt_lr, dA_mod, dtheta, du_lam, dBr,dBi,dCr,dCi]
474	#   -> x_proj backward -> dx_in (3rd path)
475	# x_in fans into THREE: the scan (dx from 6.2 (2)), x_proj, and the D-skip
476	#   (dx_in += dy_skip * D ; dD = sum_{b,l} dy_skip * x_in)
477	dx_main = dx_scan + dx_xproj + dx_Dskip              # NO SiLU now: dx_in = dx_main
478	# xz = [x_main | z]; gate sz=silu(z): dz = (dy_gated*y_skip)*silu'(z)
479	#   -> in_proj backward -> dx_inproj
480	# in the Llama-style Mamba3Block the mixer's residual is OFF (§1.6), so the input
481	# grad is dx_inproj ONLY here; the residual path (dx_residual) is added at the
482	# BLOCK level in §7. (If self.residual: dx = dx_inproj + dx_residual as before.)
483	dx = dx_inproj  (+ dx_residual if self.residual)
484	```
485	
486	`RMSNorm` backward (no fp32 downcast, `y = x·rsqrt(mean(x²)+eps)·w`, `r=rsqrt(…)`,
487	`xhat=x·r`): `dw = Σ_rows dy·xhat`, `dxhat = dy·w`,
488	`dx = r·(dxhat - xhat·(Σ_lastdim dxhat·xhat)/D)`.
489	
490	---
491	
492	## 7. SwiGLU MLP + Llama-style block backward (verified — §4 (F))
493	
494	The new sub-blocks added around the mixer (§1.6). Implemented in
495	`tests/hw/mamba3_oracle.py` as `swiglu_forward`/`swiglu_backward` and
496	`block_forward`/`block_backward`, verified to match `torch.autograd` to **≤4e-15**
497	for every SwiGLU/pre-norm parameter + the input (§4 (F)). All standard; the CUDA
498	megakernel transcribes them line-for-line alongside §6.
499	
500	### 7.1 SwiGLU MLP (no biases)
501	
502	```
503	# forward
504	g_pre = x @ W_gate^T ;  u = x @ W_up^T
505	s     = SiLU(g_pre)  ;  prod = s ⊙ u
506	out   = prod @ W_down^T
507	
508	# backward (upstream dout)
509	(dprod, dW_down) = linear_bwd(dout, prod, W_down)
510	ds = dprod ⊙ u ;  du = dprod ⊙ s
511	dg_pre = ds ⊙ SiLU'(g_pre)                  # SiLU'(x)=σ(x)(1+x(1-σ(x)))
512	(dx_gate, dW_gate) = linear_bwd(dg_pre, x, W_gate)
513	(dx_up,   dW_up)   = linear_bwd(du,     x, W_up)
514	dx = dx_gate + dx_up                        # x fans into gate AND up
515	```
516	
517	### 7.2 Llama block (two pre-norm residuals)
518	
519	```
520	# forward (residual=False mixer; RMSNorm_mix/mlp are the per-block pre-norms)
521	h1 = x  + Mixer ( RMSNorm_mix(x)  )
522	h2 = h1 + SwiGLU( RMSNorm_mlp(h1) )
523	
524	# backward (upstream dh2)
525	# h2 = h1 + SwiGLU(RMSNorm_mlp(h1)):
526	dh1   = dh2.clone()                                  # residual path
527	dh1n  = swiglu_bwd(dh2, …)                            # through the MLP
528	(dh1_mlpnorm, dW_mlpnorm) = rmsnorm_bwd(dh1n, …)
529	dh1  += dh1_mlpnorm                                   # h1 fans: residual + mlp_norm
530	# h1 = x + Mixer(RMSNorm_mix(x)):
531	dx    = dh1.clone()                                   # residual path
532	dxn   = layer_bwd(mixer, dh1)                          # mixer with residual OFF
533	(dx_mixnorm, dW_mixnorm) = rmsnorm_bwd(dxn, …)
534	dx   += dx_mixnorm                                    # x fans: residual + mixer_norm
535	```
536	
537	Each pre-norm input therefore fans into **two** paths (its residual + its
538	sub-block); the residual `.clone()` and the additive accumulation onto `dx`/`dh1`
539	are the bug-prone spots (mirrors how the mixer input fans into in_proj + the
540	mixer residual when `residual=True`).
541	
542	The model wrapper adds: cross-entropy (`dlogits=(softmax-onehot)/B`), the head
543	`Linear`, the final `RMSNorm`, last-token gather (only `t=L-1` carries grad into
544	the block stack), and the embedding `index_add_`. All verified in §4 (F).

1	# Superoptimizer Scoping — go/no-go for a full GPU-kernel superoptimizer on SuperGrok1.5
2	
3	**Author:** kernel-perf analysis pass, 2026-06-16. CPU/analysis only (no GPU, no builds).
4	**Status:** decision document. Uncommitted by design (the main loop commits).
5	**Audience:** the owner, for a go/no-go on building the *full* superoptimizer vs. continuing the
6	incremental **#24** path (widening `compile.py`'s joint search over hand-authored structural
7	variants).
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 0. TL;DR — the recommendation
12	
13	**No-go on the full, general GPU-kernel superoptimizer. Continue #24 + hand-author the handful of
14	named structural levers.** The break-even for a general correctness-gated search engine is *kernel
15	and architecture breadth*; we have **3 fixed models × 11 optimizers on one arch (sm_90a)**, the
16	known wins are a *small, already-enumerated set of structural levers* (P0/P1/M0/M1, dW staging), and
17	**we already own ~80% of a practical superoptimizer** in `compile.py`: a self-configuring
18	Optuna-TPE search over structure-macros × PTX-hints × ptxas-flags, fp64-gated, scored by real
19	d=2048 timing, with a *wired* XGBoost/ridge learned cost model and *real-but-off-by-default*
20	generative back-ends (OpGraph synth-codegen, libclang+islpy polyhedral, CUTLASS/CK emitters).
21	
22	The thing a full superoptimizer would add — *automatic discovery of structural rewrites of a fused
23	training megakernel* — is exactly the thing every surveyed autoscheduler **cannot express** (they
24	target inference / single ops, not a persistent fwd+bwd+optimizer megakernel behind a hand-built
25	grid barrier), and the thing our concrete bottleneck **does not need** (the dW lever is a known
26	gmem-layout change a human already designed and partially wired: `SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1`).
27	
28	**If you want to spend anything here, spend it on the one cheap, measurable probe in §6** (re-express
29	ONE decoder GEMM in CuTe-DSL/Triton and race its autoscheduled result against our hand-tuned engine
30	on the *isolated* GEMM). That probe costs ~3–5 person-days and either (a) reveals a real
31	auto-scheduling gap worth more investment, or (b) confirms hand-authoring + #24 captures the value —
32	without a multi-month blind commit. **A STOKE pilot on the inner loop is a no-go** (§4): the win is
33	structurally above the instruction window, and NVIDIA has no assembler to search at the SASS level.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 1. Where we actually are (grounded)
38	
39	The numbers and structure below are read directly from the codebase; citations are `file:line`.
40	
41	### 1.1 The system
42	- **ONE persistent CUDA megakernel per (model × optimizer) cell** fuses the entire training step
43	  (P0 zero → P1 fwd+bwd → P2 deterministic grad reduce → P3 optimizer tail), separated only by a
44	  **hand-built sense-reversing `GridBarrier`** (`csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh:120-153`). The
45	  barrier **needs no cooperative launch** so it scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap
46	  (`megakernel_common.cuh:28-29`); the host launches exactly `gridDim.x == #SMs` persistent CTAs
47	  (`:59`). **This is the single most important structural fact for IR selection** (§2): a
48	  *host-launched* collective (CUTLASS device::Gemm, the CuTe device GEMM API, an MLIR/Linalg-lowered
49	  op) cannot be invoked device-side *inside* this persistent grid.
50	- **33 cells** = 3 models (`transformer_decoder`, `vit`, `mamba3`) × 11 optimizers
51	  (`fused_dispatch_table.inc`), generated from ONE structural template
52	  `l3_megakernel<Model, Optimizer>` by `grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py` (you do **not**
53	  hand-write 33 kernels — the demo TU is the template, re-instantiated per cell).
54	- The GEMM engine is **hand-rolled in-kernel ss-wgmma** (`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/wgmma.cuh`),
55	  consumed via thin orientation wrappers (`model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:717+`) and an unpipelined /
56	  cp.async-ring tile loop (`tc_gemm_block_unpipelined`, `:508-715`).
57	
58	### 1.2 Current performance and *why* it's capped
59	- decoder d=2048 = **2.0%** of the 989 TF/s bf16 roofline; ViT = **0.19%**; Mamba-3 can't place at
60	  d=2048 (smem-bound) (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md:9`).
61	- **Structurally capped, not knob-bound:** decoder is the same 2% at d=1024 and d=2048
62	  (scale-invariant cap, `PERF_ANALYSIS.md:11`); the kernel-knob track hit a 3-consecutive-not-positive
63	  STOP and is **knob-converged** at TILE 128×128/IL=2/STAGES=2/cp.async-ring
64	  (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:44`).
65	- Root cause: (1) the **dW GEMM is staging-bound** — ~97% of each dW K-step is the transposed-strided
66	  scalar operand gather, ~3% is the wgmma (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:52`, `PERF_ANALYSIS.md:19`);
67	  (2) the fused step is mostly **non-GEMM fp32 CUDA-core work** the roofline numerator ignores.
68	- **The P0 pipelining lever was tried and reverted** (`OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:52`): fp64 gate passed
69	  (11/11) but perf regressed −11.6% — pipelining the MMA is the wrong lever when the bottleneck is
70	  staging. The redirect (documented, not yet landed): faster *staging* via contiguous K-major
71	  pre-transpose (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1`, `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:114-150`) or
72	  TMA-with-transpose.
73	
74	### 1.3 What `compile.py` already is (this is decisive for ROI)
75	`compile.py` is **already a practical superoptimizer over its macro/flag space** — not a stub. Verified:
76	
77	| Capability | Status | Evidence |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| Self-configuring search space | **REAL, used** | `_discover_kernel_knobs` scans committed kernels for `#ifndef SG_TUNED_X`/`#define` guards → a new knob enters the space with zero edits; producer→consumer liveness audit drops dead macros. Cartesian ~10⁶–10¹³/arch. |
80	| Joint structure × PTX-hint × ptxas-flag | **REAL, used** | `TILE_M/N`, `*_DW_SPLITK`, `async_depth`, `cluster_shape`, `swizzle`, `wgmma_shape`, `prod_regs/cons_regs`, warp-spec → `-DSG_TUNED_*`; plus real `--maxrregcount`, `-Xptxas --opt-level`, `--allow-expensive-optimizations`. |
81	| Search algorithm | **REAL, used** | Optuna **TPE Bayesian** (`run_bayesian`, `TPESampler(multivariate=True)`) + **top-K ±2-step local refine** (`topk_refine`) + multi-criterion `BayesianEarlyStopper`. Opt-in exhaustive/Cartesian mode also exists. |
82	| Learned cost model (Ansor-style surrogate) | **REAL, wired, default-ON** | `class CostModel`: XGBoost → sklearn-GBR → numpy-ridge fallback; **vetoes candidates inside the TPE loop** (`ms_pred > threshold and high_confidence` → `cost_model_pruned` → Optuna `PRUNED`); cold-start floor of 100 real timings; online-fit + warm-start + persisted; multi-fidelity 2nd prune stage. |
83	| Correctness gate (in-loop) | **REAL** but **NOT fp64** | strict-math (`-DSG_STRICT_MATH=1`, fast-math-OFF) AOT build's own fp32 output is the oracle; `np.allclose` per-dtype tol + a `np.array_equal` 3× determinism check. Generated/transformed origins are **ineligible to win unless they recorded an oracle PASS** (`_VALIDATION_REQUIRED_ORIGINS`). |
84	| Correctness gate (fp64 ground truth) | **REAL, separate layer** | `tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py` (+ `*_oracle.py`, `*_kernel_mirror.py`): bf16-TC kernel vs pure-**fp64** canonical refs (`ref_<opt>_step`), rel-tol 1e-4 (SAM surfaces 2.5e-2/3e-2), + A/A/A bit-identical determinism via `torch.equal`. **This does NOT call the autotuner — it gates the production step directly.** |
85	| Measurement | **REAL, used** | `TimingWorker` persistent CUDA-context subprocess + watchdog + multi-GPU pool; CUDA-graph median at `--size 2048`; `.so` reuse keyed on sources+flags hash (skips ~125s recompiles, `compile.py:7589`); sqlite `compiled_cache.db`; resumable Optuna study. |
86	| Generative codegen (the "real superoptimizer") | **REAL but OFF by default** | OpGraph synth-codegen (fused AdamW/flash-attn/Newton-Schulz patterns → real CUDA elementwise/reduce/GEMM emitters), polyhedral (libclang AST + islpy deps, honest conservative fallback), CUTLASS/CK GEMM emitters. Gated `enable_*=false`; exercised by self-tests; **not proven on the production megakernels**; origin-tagged only when a transformed source actually compiles. |
87	| Objective | **roofline-aware** | optimization target is *distance-to-roofline* (`tuning/roofline.py`: achieved FLOP/s = FLOPs/wall), tracked at 10-step granularity; the surrogate predicts `median_ms`. |
88	
89	**Honest gaps in `compile.py` a "full superoptimizer" would need to close:** (1) the in-loop oracle is
90	strict-AOT-fp32 self-consistency, not fp64 — fp64 ground truth lives only in the hardware test layer;
91	(2) there is **no e-graph / equality-saturation / true program-synthesis search over semantics** — the
92	"generative" layer is a *fixed pattern library* + polyhedral reschedule, not search over rewrites;
93	(3) the generative back-ends are unproven at scale and off; (4) `compiled_cache.db` is empty in this
94	checkout (no GPU builds persisted).
95	
96	### 1.4 What IRs are already vendored
97	- **CUTLASS v3.6.0 + CuTe** — PRESENT and **used**, but only on the **host-launched** path:
98	  `csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/mma.cuh` (`#ifdef WITH_CUTLASS`) builds a Sm90 `GemmUniversalAdapter`
99	  (TMA+WGMMA) for Muon Newton-Schulz and SuperGrok2 `dt_proj`. The header itself states the boundary:
100	  "The CUTLASS GEMM is a self-contained kernel that OWNS its TMA mainloop … Pairing the elect/mbarrier
101	  primitives with TMA belongs to the … hand-written TMA path, NOT here" (`mma.cuh:148-160`). It is
102	  **explicitly rejected for the persistent-megakernel path** (`wgmma.cuh:14-18`).
103	- **Triton** — ABSENT (no `@triton.jit`/`tl.`; not a dependency).
104	- **MLIR / Linalg / IREE / TVM / Ansor / OpenXLA** — ABSENT for kernel gen (only an XLA/Pallas
105	  scaffold for the TPU path).
106	- **Polyhedral (islpy / libclang)** — PRESENT but only as `compile.py`'s opt-in, off-by-default
107	  scaffold; soft deps, not in `install_requires`; not wired into the sm_90 megakernels.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## 2. IR options for Level-2 structural auto-scheduling
112	
113	The question that dominates every row: **can it express our FUSED TRAINING megakernel** — one
114	persistent kernel that does fwd + bwd + dW + the optimizer step, with a deterministic cross-CTA grad
115	reduce, behind a hand-built grid barrier? This is *not* the workload any of these tools is built for.
116	Autoschedulers target **inference / single ops / forward graphs**; a fused fwd+bwd+optimizer
117	persistent megakernel with cross-CTA reductions and an in-kernel optimizer is **out of distribution
118	for all of them**. Treat this as the central obstacle, not a footnote.
119	
120	### 2.1 CuTe-DSL (CUTLASS-native, Python)
121	- **Substrate match:** *best of the four* — CuTe is the native abstraction over exactly our wgmma/TMA
122	  substrate, and we already vendor CUTLASS 3.6 + CuTe and use it (host-side) in `mma.cuh`. Layouts,
123	  swizzles, TMA descriptors, warp-specialized mainloops are first-class.
124	- **Can it express the fused training megakernel?** **No, not as one persistent device kernel.** The
125	  CuTe-DSL / CUTLASS programming model is *collective-kernel-shaped*: you author a GEMM (or a fused
126	  epilogue) that CUTLASS launches and that owns its own mainloop/epilogue. Our megakernel is the
127	  *inverse*: a persistent grid we own, into which GEMMs are *embedded* as device-side tile loops
128	  between grid barriers, with a cross-CTA reduce and an optimizer phase living in the same launch.
129	  There is no CuTe construct for "persistent grid that runs a backward pass and an Adam step between
130	  two grid barriers." You could express the *individual GEMMs* in CuTe and the *epilogue fusion* in a
131	  CUTLASS collective epilogue — but not the whole step, and not without re-introducing the
132	  host-launch boundary the persistent design exists to avoid.
133	- **Autoscheduler maturity on Hopper/wgmma/TMA:** CuTe gives you the *vocabulary* and CUTLASS ships
134	  expert-tuned Hopper kernels, but CuTe-DSL is **not an autoscheduler** — there is no Ansor-style cost
135	  model or search; you (or CUTLASS's `CollectiveBuilder` heuristics) pick the schedule. So "adopt
136	  CuTe-DSL" buys *expression*, not *automatic search* — and we already have the search (`compile.py`).
137	- **Rewrite cost:** to get value inside the megakernel you'd re-express the in-kernel GEMM tile loop
138	  in CuTe device code and prove it composes with our grid barrier / persistent loop / smem budget —
139	  **weeks per GEMM family**, and the persistent-launch composition is unproven (likely the hardest
140	  part). To get value *outside* (host-launched per-GEMM), you abandon fusion.
141	- **fp64 gate integration:** clean — a CuTe GEMM has a well-defined I/O contract; run it through the
142	  same `test_l3tc_tail_gate` fp64 oracle. But bit-exact A/A/A requires the same ascending-k reduction
143	  order; CuTe's split-K/stream-K reorders the sum and would fail the determinism gate as-is.
144	- **Verdict:** highest-leverage IR for a *probe* (it matches our substrate and is already vendored),
145	  but it **cannot express the fused training megakernel** and is not itself a search engine.
146	
147	### 2.2 Triton
148	- **Substrate match:** good for elementwise/attention/forward GEMMs; Hopper wgmma/TMA support exists
149	  but lags hand-tuned CUTLASS for the last 2× on big GEMMs.
150	- **Can it express the fused training megakernel?** **No.** Triton's model is grid-of-independent-tiles
151	  per `@triton.jit` kernel; it has no persistent-grid-barrier / cross-CTA-reduce-in-one-launch /
152	  in-kernel-optimizer construct. You'd write *many* Triton kernels (one per phase) and launch them
153	  separately — i.e. **un-fuse** the megakernel, which is the opposite of the design.
154	- **Autoscheduler maturity:** Triton's autotuner is a **config grid search** (`@triton.autotune` over
155	  `num_warps`/`num_stages`/block sizes) — *less* capable than what `compile.py` already does (TPE +
156	  learned surrogate + multi-fidelity). No structural search.
157	- **Rewrite cost:** ABSENT today (new dependency); per-kernel rewrites are days each but the
158	  *fusion-breaking* is architectural.
159	- **fp64 gate:** same story as CuTe — clean per-kernel contract; reduction-order determinism is the
160	  catch.
161	- **Verdict:** viable only as a *forward-GEMM / attention probe*; structurally cannot host the fused
162	  training step; its search is weaker than ours.
163	
164	### 2.3 MLIR-Linalg (IREE / custom pipeline)
165	- **Substrate match:** Linalg can represent GEMM/conv/elementwise and there are Hopper lowerings, but
166	  driving wgmma/TMA well end-to-end is research-grade and brittle.
167	- **Can it express the fused training megakernel?** **No, and worst rewrite cost of the four.** Linalg
168	  models tensor algebra (a *forward* dataflow graph); backward + the optimizer update + a deterministic
169	  cross-CTA reduction + a persistent grid barrier are not Linalg ops. You would be authoring a custom
170	  dialect + lowering pipeline for a one-of-a-kind kernel shape — a multi-quarter compiler project with
171	  no guarantee the Hopper codegen beats our hand-tuned engine.
172	- **Autoscheduler maturity on Hopper/wgmma/TMA:** the least mature for *persistent fused* shapes;
173	  IREE/Linalg autoscheduling targets inference graphs.
174	- **fp64 gate:** the gate would sit at the whole-kernel boundary (same fp64 oracle), but you'd first
175	  have to *build* the kernel through the pipeline before you could gate it.
176	- **Verdict:** not worth it for 3 fixed models. This is the option whose break-even most clearly
177	  requires breadth we don't have.
178	
179	### 2.4 Polyhedral (Pluto-style; islpy/libclang already scaffolded in `compile.py`)
180	- **Substrate match:** polyhedral excels at *affine loop-nest reschedule* (tiling, fusion, skewing,
181	  interchange) of static-control loops — and `compile.py` already has the libclang+islpy plumbing
182	  (off by default).
183	- **Can it express the fused training megakernel?** It does not *replace* the kernel; it *reschedules
184	  loops within* it. The hot loops are wgmma tile loops whose schedule is constrained by (a) the wgmma
185	  `.aligned` collective requirement (all 128 warpgroup threads issue uniformly, `wgmma.cuh:423`),
186	  (b) the ascending-k determinism contract, and (c) smem capacity. Polyhedral reschedule that respects
187	  all three reduces to choices our macro space already covers (STAGES, INTERLEAVE, split-K).
188	- **Autoscheduler maturity on Hopper/wgmma/TMA:** polyhedral tools have **no model of wgmma/TMA**;
189	  they schedule scalar affine loops, then you still hand-map to the tensor-core substrate. The match
190	  to our substrate is weak precisely where the perf lives.
191	- **fp64 gate:** any reschedule that reorders the fp32 accumulation breaks bit-exact A/A/A; only
192	  order-preserving reschedules pass — a narrow set.
193	- **Verdict:** the scaffold is fine to keep as an *experiment* on the non-GEMM fp32 epilogue passes
194	  (P1 fusion candidates), but it cannot reach the GEMM bottleneck and isn't a general win.
195	
196	### 2.5 IR summary
197	None of the four can express the fused training megakernel as one persistent kernel; **CuTe is the
198	only one whose substrate matches ours and that we already own**, and even it is collective-shaped,
199	not persistent-megakernel-shaped, and is not itself a search engine. The honest conclusion: the
200	*expression layer* is not our gap — our gap is structural rewrites, and no surveyed autoscheduler
201	discovers those for this kernel shape.
202	
203	---
204	
205	## 3. Search method
206	
207	The space is **structure × realization × flags**:
208	- *structure*: tile shapes, split-K, interleave, pipeline depth, staging method, warp-spec, fusion of
209	  the fp32 epilogue passes, the dW operand layout;
210	- *realization*: how each structural choice is lowered (cp.async ring vs synchronous stager vs
211	  TMA-with-transpose);
212	- *flags*: PTX hints + ptxas (`--maxrregcount`, opt-level, expensive-opts).
213	
214	Methods, judged against what we already have:
215	
216	| Method | What it is | Status here | Verdict for us |
217	|---|---|---|---|
218	| **Measured search (Optuna-TPE + local refine)** | Bayesian global + ±2-step neighbor refine, every candidate timed | **Already built & default** (`run_bayesian`/`topk_refine`) | The right backbone; keep it. |
219	| **Learned cost model (Ansor-style)** | surrogate predicts runtime, prunes candidates before building | **Already built, wired, default-ON** (`CostModel`, XGBoost/ridge, cold-floor 100, multi-fidelity) | Already have it; the value is *fewer ~125s builds*, not new wins. |
220	| **Stochastic / MCMC over programs (STOKE)** | MCMC over instruction sequences with correctness+perf cost | **ABSENT** | No-go for our bottleneck (§4): win is above the instruction window; no SASS assembler. |
221	| **Exhaustive** | enumerate the Cartesian space | opt-in mode exists | Intractable for the full megakernel; fine for tiny pinned sub-spaces. |
222	
223	**How correctness-equivalence is enforced (the fp64 oracle):** today, two-tier — the in-loop
224	strict-AOT-fp32 self-consistency + 3× determinism gate inside `compile.py`, and the authoritative
225	**fp64** parity + A/A/A gate in `tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py` driving the production step. **A
226	full superoptimizer that generates novel structure would need the fp64 oracle wired *into the search
227	loop*** (not just the post-hoc hardware gate), because in-loop strict-fp32 self-consistency does not
228	prove fp64 correctness of a *newly synthesized* variant — it only proves it matches the strict build
229	of the *same source*. That wiring is a real, bounded piece of work and a prerequisite for trusting any
230	generative back-end's winners.
231	
232	**The decisive constraint across every method:** bit-exact A/A/A determinism requires preserving the
233	**ascending-k fp32 reduction order**. fp32 add is non-associative, so *any* search that reassociates
234	the sum (a faster reduction tree, stream-K, a different split-K reduce order) changes bits and fails
235	the determinism gate. This collapses the *legal* realization space to **transport-only** rewrites
236	(move the same operands to the same smem in the same k-order). Relaxing the oracle to ULP-tolerance
237	to unlock reassociation would re-litigate the determinism contract the whole project rests on — and
238	would *still* not help the dW, whose bottleneck is the load pattern, not the sum.
239	
240	---
241	
242	## 4. Component-level STOKE on the hot K-step inner loop
243	
244	The full megakernel is far too big for STOKE; the hot **dW K-step inner loop** (staging + wgmma, ~tens
245	of instructions) is the only plausibly-STOKE-able unit. **Verdict: no-go.** Grounded reasons:
246	
247	1. **The win is structurally above the instruction window.** The dW is staging-bound (~97% staging /
248	   ~3% wgmma, `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md:52`) and the documented lever is to **stop doing the strided
249	   gather at all** — pre-transpose dY/X into a contiguous K-major gmem scratch so rows become
250	   K-contiguous + 16B-aligned, flipping `DecTileSrcIsGmem` true and letting the *already-validated*
251	   cp.async ring stream them (`SG_TUNED_DEC_DW_STAGE=1`, `model_stage_decoder_tc.cuh:114-150`,
252	   transpose pass `:1660-1692`), or TMA-with-transpose. Both are **changes to the *input* side of the
253	   I/O contract** (a different gmem layout + a separate pre-transpose pass). STOKE optimizes a fixed
254	   instruction sequence *for a fixed I/O contract*; it cannot say "first run a different kernel to
255	   rewrite memory, then a different sequence becomes optimal." The lever is out of its search space by
256	   construction — and a human already found it and partially wired it.
257	2. **No SASS substrate.** NVIDIA SASS is **not officially assemblable** (no public assembler, no
258	   documented `ptxas` round-trip; the toolchain here references only ptxas flags, no
259	   `nvdisasm`/`cuobjdump`-edit path). STOKE's premise (mutate assembly → reassemble → measure) has no
260	   substrate on NVIDIA. The realistic levels are **PTX** (assemblable, but ptxas re-schedules /
261	   re-allocates so you don't control final SASS — and the body is already near-minimal PTX: single
262	   inline-asm wgmma, single-op barriers/fences, `LDG.U16`/`STS.U16` with no instruction-count fat) or
263	   **CUDA-C/intrinsic source** (real leverage — but the leverage is *choosing a staging strategy*,
264	   which is exactly the discrete macro space `compile.py` already sweeps: `STAGES`, `INTERLEAVE`,
265	   `SPLITK`, `DW_STAGE`, `kRingAsync`).
266	3. **The exact oracle the project requires forbids the interesting rewrites.** A unit oracle is cheap
267	   and would be *bit-exact* (feed a known dY/X tile, compare the fp32 accumulator) — but exactness +
268	   ascending-k means only **transport-only** rewrites are legal; STOKE can't touch the arithmetic, and
269	   the arithmetic isn't the bottleneck.
270	4. **The one local coalescing micro-rewrite STOKE would plausibly find was already tried and reverted**
271	   (m-major HBM coalescing introduced a compensating smem bank conflict → neutral-to-worse). The fix
272	   has to be holistic (layout + transport together), i.e. structural, not peephole.
273	
274	STOKE could only pay off if pointed at a **compute-bound / instruction-count-bound** inner loop. We
275	don't have one on the critical path — our hot loop is latency-bound on an uncoalesced gather.
276	
277	---
278	
279	## 5. Effort / ROI
280	
281	Person-time is rough order-of-magnitude (one experienced GPU+compiler engineer). "Gain vs #24" is the
282	*expected marginal* gain over continuing the incremental path, **given the bottleneck is a known
283	structural lever and `compile.py` already searches the flag/macro space**.
284	
285	| Option | Person-time | Expected gain vs #24 | Risk | Notes |
286	|---|---|---:|---|---|
287	| **#24 (baseline): widen `compile.py` joint search over hand-authored structural variants** | ongoing (in flight) | — (the reference) | low | Author each lever as a `SG_TUNED_*` variant; the autotuner searches it; fp64-gated ratchet. Captures P0-redirect (dW staging), P1 epilogue fusion, M0/M1, swizzle, TMA-transpose **as they're authored**. |
288	| Hand-author the named levers (dW `STAGE=1`, M0 wgmma-projections, P1 fusion, ViT B1) | ~1–3 wk each | **High** — these are the measured 5–15× headroom (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md`) | med (per-lever eng + parity) | This is where the real perf is. Each is bounded, fp64-gated, revertible. |
289	| **CuTe-DSL probe** (re-express ONE decoder GEMM, race vs hand engine, *isolated*) | ~3–5 days | Diagnostic (info, not perf) | low | The recommended probe (§6). Tells us if an autoscheduler beats our hand-tuned GEMM *at all* before any big bet. |
290	| Triton probe (forward GEMM / attention only) | ~1 wk | Diagnostic, lower relevance | low | Only touches forward ops; can't host fusion; search weaker than ours. |
291	| Wire fp64 oracle *into* the search loop + turn on `compile.py` generative back-ends (synth-codegen / polyhedral) on the megakernel | ~3–6 wk | **Low-to-uncertain** | high | Back-ends are real but unproven at scale; the pattern library doesn't contain our bottleneck's fix; e-graph/equality-sat search over semantics doesn't exist here and would be a research build. |
292	| Full MLIR-Linalg / custom-dialect auto-scheduling of the megakernel | **multi-quarter** | **Speculative** | very high | Cannot express the fused training kernel without a bespoke dialect+pipeline; no guarantee of beating the hand engine. |
293	| Component STOKE on the dW inner loop | ~2–4 wk | **~0** (likely negative ROI) | high | §4: win is above instruction window; no SASS; oracle forbids the useful rewrites; the local rewrite it'd find was reverted. |
294	
295	### 5.1 The break-even
296	A general correctness-gated superoptimizer amortizes its build cost across **kernel/architecture
297	breadth** — many distinct kernels, multiple GPUs/arches, evolving ops, where re-deriving schedules by
298	hand is the bottleneck. **Our situation is the opposite of the break-even case:**
299	- **3 fixed models, 11 optimizers, ONE arch (sm_90a).** The 33 cells already share ONE structural
300	  template and ONE GEMM engine — a lever fixed once (P0-redirect, M0) propagates to all relevant cells
301	  by construction (`PERF_ANALYSIS.md:22` "shared engine ⇒ one change fixes both models").
302	- The headroom lives in a **small, already-enumerated set of structural levers** (P0/P1/P2, M0/M1/M2,
303	  S1–S3 in `PERF_ANALYSIS.md`), not in an open-ended schedule space a human can't enumerate.
304	- We **already own the search engine** for the flag/macro/structural-variant space. The full
305	  superoptimizer's *only* novel capability — automatic discovery of structural rewrites of a fused
306	  training megakernel — is precisely what no autoscheduler can express for this kernel shape (§2).
307	
308	So the marginal value of the full superoptimizer over #24-plus-hand-authoring is **low and high-risk**,
309	while its cost is **high**. #24 + hand-authoring the handful of levers captures most of the value.
310	
311	---
312	
313	## 6. Phased plan IF go (start with a cheap probe, not a blind commit)
314	
315	If the owner wants to *de-risk* the auto-scheduling question before committing, do the **minimal
316	measurable probe first** and gate expansion on its result.
317	
318	### Phase 0 — the probe (~3–5 person-days, low risk) [RECOMMENDED if spending anything]
319	**Re-express ONE isolated decoder GEMM in CuTe-DSL and race its autoscheduled result against our
320	hand-tuned engine.** Pick the **fwd in_proj GEMM** (clean shape: M = token tile, N = 3d, K = d; *not*
321	the dW — the dW's lever is layout, not scheduling, so it would mislead the probe). Concretely:
322	1. Author the GEMM as a standalone CuTe/CUTLASS Sm90 collective (we already vendor CUTLASS 3.6 + use
323	   it host-side in `mma.cuh`, so the toolchain is in place).
324	2. Feed it the *same* bf16 operands the in-kernel engine sees; compare the fp32 output against the
325	   existing `test_decoder_tc.py` micro-gate (bit-match where ascending-k is preserved; ULP-bounded
326	   otherwise, recorded honestly).
327	3. Time both *in isolation* at d=2048 with the existing `TimingWorker` harness.
328	
329	**Decision rule:**
330	- If CuTe's autoscheduled GEMM is **meaningfully faster** than our hand-tuned engine *on the isolated
331	  GEMM* → there is a real auto-scheduling gap. Proceed to Phase 1, but scoped to **host-launchable
332	  GEMM families only** (the fusion question is still unsolved — see §2.1).
333	- If it is **within noise or slower** (the likely outcome given the bottleneck is staging/layout and
334	  non-GEMM fp32 work, not GEMM scheduling) → **stop**; the value is in hand-authoring the structural
335	  levers + #24. Record the result in `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md` as a measured dry-well.
336	
337	(Optional cheaper sub-probe: a Triton version of the same GEMM, ~1 day, as a second data point. Skip if
338	Phase 0 already answers the question.)
339	
340	### Phase 1 — only if Phase 0 shows a real gap (~3–6 wk)
341	Wire the **fp64 oracle into the search loop** (prerequisite to trust any generated variant), then turn
342	on **one** `compile.py` generative back-end (start with the CUTLASS emitter, since the probe validated
343	CuTe) on the **host-launchable GEMM families**, gated by the fp64 oracle + A/A/A. Measure against the
344	hand engine on 3 seeds at d=2048. Keep only on a measured win (the existing ratchet). **Do not** attempt
345	the persistent-megakernel-internal auto-scheduling until/unless a host-launched GEMM win is demonstrated
346	*and* a persistent-launch composition story exists — that remains the hardest, least-proven part.
347	
348	### Phase 2 — only if Phase 1 wins compound (re-evaluate)
349	Revisit polyhedral reschedule on the **non-GEMM fp32 epilogue passes** (the P1 fusion candidates), where
350	affine-loop transforms are actually applicable, and the broader generative search. Re-run the
351	break-even (§5.1) with real Phase-1 numbers before any multi-month commit.
352	
353	**Throughout:** every step lands in `OPTIMIZATION_LEDGER.md` with its measured numbers and the
354	mechanistic why (the existing protocol), so the "big bet" only ever advances on evidence.
355	
356	---
357	
358	## 7. The honest one-paragraph answer
359	
360	For *our* situation — 3 fixed models, 11 optimizers, one arch, a structurally-capped megakernel whose
361	known wins are a short list of human-identifiable structural levers, and an existing `compile.py` that
362	is already a fp64-gated, roofline-scored, learned-cost-model-pruned Bayesian superoptimizer over the
363	flag/macro/structural-variant space — **a full general GPU-kernel superoptimizer is not worth
364	building.** No surveyed IR (CuTe, Triton, MLIR-Linalg, polyhedral) can even express the fused training
365	megakernel as one persistent kernel, and the only one matching our substrate (CuTe) is collective-shaped
366	and not itself a search engine. Component-level STOKE can't reach our bottleneck (the lever is a gmem
367	layout change above the instruction window, and NVIDIA has no SASS assembler to search). **#24 +
368	hand-authoring the handful of levers (dW staging redirect, M0, P1 fusion) captures most of the value at
369	a fraction of the cost and risk.** If you want to spend anything to *confirm* this, run the Phase-0 CuTe
370	probe (~3–5 days) and let the measurement decide.
371
