1	# INTEGRATION-VIT.md — wiring the L3-REAL ViT megakernel (PHASE 2)
2	
3	This is the integrator's cell/dispatch spec for the **real Vision-Transformer
4	forward+backward as persistent-megakernel stages**. The model stages, the
5	composition+launcher, the weight-layout header, the oracle/mirror, and the
6	hardware-gated tests are **already built and CPU-validated** (see "What ships"
7	below). What remains is the **integration seam** — the generated cell `.cu`, the
8	`dispatch.cpp` routing, the codegen layout emitter, and the Python `fused_train_step`
9	wiring — which the directive reserves for the integrator / sibling agents who own
10	`megakernel_codegen.py`, `dispatch.cpp`, and the `csrc/bindings/*` files.
11	
12	This file is the exact contract for that seam. It mirrors PHASE 1's decoder
13	integration (BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md "PHASE 1") with the **four ViT-specific
14	deltas** called out loudly. Source-complete only: no builds, no GPU runs were
15	performed.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 0. What ships in PHASE 2 (already built + validated, do NOT re-derive)
20	
21	| file | role | status |
22	|---|---|---|
23	| `tests/hw/vit_oracle.py` | manual fwd+bwd ORACLE + `vit_param_layout()` (THE single source of truth for the flat layout) | ✅ matches autograd, loss rel 0, worst grad rel **1.0e-15** (fp64, 32/32 tensors) |
24	| `tests/hw/vit_kernel_mirror.py` | single-threaded STRUCTURAL mirror of the kernel (buffer aliasing / recompute / FULL-attn 3-pass bwd / cls+patch scatter) | ✅ matches oracle, loss rel **2.0e-16**, worst grad rel **9.9e-16** |
25	| `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_vit.cuh` | REAL ViT fwd/bwd stages (`vit_forward_sample` / `vit_backward_sample`), self-contained per COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md | source-complete (not built) |
26	| `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_vit_megakernel.cuh` | composition + host launcher `launch_fused_vit_megakernel<Opt>` (incl. the **dynamic-smem opt-in**) | source-complete (not built) |
27	| `csrc/fused/sm_90/vit_layout.cuh` | hand-written weight-layout mirror, **static_asserts** on count(32)/total(418017)/smem-budget; **marked for codegen adoption** | source-complete |
28	| `tests/hw/test_vit_megakernel.py` | the parity ladder (no-GPU A/A2/B/B2 + GPU-gated C/D/E) | ✅ no-GPU gates PASS; GPU gates SKIP until this seam lands |
29	
30	The kernel's MATH and STRUCTURE are therefore already proven on CPU; the seam
31	below only routes data to it. **Do not modify** `model_stage_vit.cuh` /
32	`fused_vit_megakernel.cuh` / `vit_layout.cuh` / the oracle / the mirror to make
33	integration easier — adapt the seam to them.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## 1. The architecture, pinned (cites grokking_race_v2.py)
38	
39	`_raw_model` → `ViT(p=97, patch_dim=49, num_patches=16, d=128, h=4, nl=2)` (lines
40	389-404; `MODEL_SCALES["small"]` → d=128/h=4/nl=2, confirmed against
41	`DEFAULT_CONFIG`):
42	
43	| component | def | shape |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| `cls_token` | `nn.Parameter[1,1,128]*.02` (:393) | [1,1,128] — **position 0 of every sample** |
46	| `patch_proj` | `nn.Linear(49,128)` (:392) | [128,49]+[128] — per-patch embed (16 patches) |
47	| `pos` | `nn.Embedding(16+1,128)` (:394) | [17,128] |
48	| 2× `EncoderBlock` | (:379) | |
49	| `attn` | `nn.MultiheadAttention(128,4,batch_first)` (:382), **NO mask — FULL attention** | in_proj [384,128]+[384], out_proj [128,128]+[128] |
50	| `n1,n2` | `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (:383), eps **1e-5** | [128]×2 each |
51	| `ff` | `Linear(128,512)→GELU→Linear(512,128)` (:384) | [512,128]+[512], [128,512]+[128] |
52	| post-LN | `x=n1(x+attn(x)); h=n2(x+ff(x))` (:386-387) | |
53	| `norm` | `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (:396) | [128]×2 |
54	| `out` | `nn.Linear(128,97)` (:396) | [97,128]+[97] |
55	| forward | `h=patch_proj(x); h=cat([cls,h]); h+=pos; for l: h=l(h); return out(norm(h[:,0,:]))` (:400-404) | **CLS token (pos 0)** |
56	| loss | `F.cross_entropy(m(tx), ty)` (:967…) | mean over B |
57	
58	**32 parameter tensors, 418,017 total params.** Numerics (each verified against
59	autograd in `vit_oracle.py`): **GELU = exact erf**; LayerNorm **eps=1e-5**;
60	attention scale **1/√32**, softmax with row-max subtraction; CE **mean over B** →
61	`dlogits=(softmax−onehot)/B`. `nn.MultiheadAttention` transcribed in the
62	already-verified qkv-split form.
63	
64	### The four ViT-specific deltas vs the decoder seam
65	
66	1. **INPUT is FLOAT image patches `[B,16,49]`, not int tokens.** (Decoder: int32
67	   `input`.) targets are int `[B]`. ABI packing in §4.
68	2. **NO causal mask** — FULL attention. (Already baked into the stages/oracle/
69	   mirror; nothing for the integrator to do, but the parity test must use the
70	   no-mask eager model — `test_vit_megakernel.py::_build_eager_vit` already does.)
71	3. **Head reads CLS position 0**, not the last position. (Baked in.)
72	4. **32 tensors / 418017 elems** (decoder: 30 / 422755), and the first three are
73	   `cls_token, patch_proj.weight, patch_proj.bias` (cls_token is yielded BEFORE
74	   the patch_proj submodule — a leaf-before-children ordering; verified against
75	   the live `named_parameters()`). The layout header encodes this.
76	
77	---
78	
79	## 2. THE one hard requirement: dynamic shared memory (don't drop it)
80	
81	ViT's per-sample working set `VitSampleSmem` is **188,080 bytes (≈183.67 KB)** at
82	seq=17 — **far over the 48 KB STATIC `__shared__` cap** (a static
83	`__shared__ VitSampleSmem sm;` would **not compile**). So the kernel uses
84	`extern __shared__` DYNAMIC smem, and the launcher
85	(`launch_fused_vit_megakernel`, already written) does **all three**:
86	
87	```cpp
88	const int dyn_smem = (int)sizeof(VitSampleSmem);            // 188080
89	cudaFuncSetAttribute(&fused_vit_megakernel<Opt>,
90	    cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, dyn_smem); // (1) opt-in >48KB
91	cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, ..., dyn_smem); // (2) honest occ
92	fused_vit_megakernel<Opt><<<grid, 256, dyn_smem, stream>>>(...);     // (3) launch
93	```
94	
95	**188080 B ≪ the sm_90 227 KB per-block dynamic cap** (44 KB headroom;
96	static_asserted in `vit_layout.cuh`), and the persistent megakernel is
97	**one-CTA-per-SM by design** (gridDim = #SMs, grid barrier over #SMs), so
98	**occupancy = 1 IS the design point** — a 184 KB block at occ=1 is intended, not a
99	regression. **Missing any of the three steps makes the kernel silently fail to
100	launch.** The launcher already encapsulates this; the integrator's only job is to
101	**not** pass `dynamicSMemBytes=0` anywhere on this path, and to ensure whatever
102	calls the launcher does so on a device whose `MaxDynamicSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin`
103	≥ 188080 (every sm_90 satisfies this).
104	
105	---
106	
107	## 3. Stage / barrier layout (one persistent kernel — identical to the decoder)
108	
109	`fused_vit_megakernel.cuh`, gridDim = #SMs (one CTA/SM), 256 threads/CTA,
110	**batch-parallel** (NOT the param-tensor work-steal queue — that would vary the
111	batch→CTA grouping and fp32 sums aren't associative):
112	
113	```
114	P0  each CTA zeroes its OWN grad-partial slice + loss slot
115	--- grid barrier B0 ---
116	P1  each CTA owns a FIXED contiguous batch slice (blockIdx.x); processes its
117	    samples ONE AT A TIME (CTA-cooperative): loads the sample's 16×49 float
118	    patches into smem, fwd+bwd, accumulating each sample's weight-grad into the
119	    CTA's partial with a SINGLE-OWNER-THREAD-PER-ELEMENT rule (no atomics →
120	    deterministic), and sums its slice's NLL (fp32)
121	--- grid barrier B1 ---
122	P2  deterministic cross-CTA reduce: sum partial[0..nCTA) in ASCENDING CTA index
123	    into the global grad (no float atomics; order fixed → reuses the work-steal
124	    queue to pick WHO reduces which tensor). Loss: fp64 ordered sum → loss/B → a
125	    device float the host reads back.
126	--- grid barrier B2 (sync_reset: also resets the queue for P3) ---
127	P3  the REAL apply_optimizer<Opt> tail consumes the reduced grad in place
128	```
129	
130	`n_tasks = 32` (kVitNumTensors) for the reduce + optimizer phases; the kernel
131	reads per-tensor numel/offset from the generated `__constant__` tables
132	`kVitSizes/kVitOffsets` (vit_layout.cuh). Determinism: fixed batch→CTA grouping +
133	fixed ascending-CTA reduction order; **no float atomics** in the weight-grad
134	reduce. The cls/pos embedding scatter maps **thread→embedding column** and the
135	patch_proj weight-grad maps **thread→(out,in)**, both looping the
136	sample's/patch's positions sequentially → deterministic.
137	
138	**SMEM budget per CTA: `VitSampleSmem` = 188080 B dynamic** (one sample, one layer
139	live; the backward recomputes each layer's forward from the cached layer input).
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 4. ABI seam (no `bindings.cpp` / `setup.py` edit — the owned extension points)
144	
145	The pybind `m.def("fused_step", ...)` arity is pinned in `bindings.cpp` (NOT
146	owned), so `fused_step`'s arity is unchanged. Carry the ViT input through the
147	EXISTING `input`/`state`/`grad` tensors and add the **behavior** in `dispatch.cpp`
148	(owned), exactly as the decoder did.
149	
150	**Tensor contract (what Python passes; what dispatch.cpp reads):**
151	
152	* `input` = **float32** `[B*16*49 + B]` contiguous — the `B*16*49` patch pixels
153	  (row-major `[B][16][49]`) followed by **B targets bit-cast to float** (each
154	  target is an `int32` reinterpreted into the float slot:
155	  `input[B*784 + b] = reinterpret as float of (int32)target[b]`). dispatch.cpp
156	  reads patches as `input.data_ptr<float>()` and targets as
157	  `reinterpret_cast<const int*>(input.data_ptr<float>() + (int64_t)B*784)`.
158	  `B = (input.numel()) / (16*49 + 1) = numel / 785`.
159	  *(Rationale: `fused_step`'s arity has one input tensor; the decoder packed
160	  int tokens++int targets into one int32 tensor. ViT's patches are float, so we
161	  keep `input` float and bit-pack the int targets into trailing float slots —
162	  the symmetric move. This is a BIT REINTERPRET both ways (store: copy the int32
163	  bit pattern into the float slot; read: `reinterpret_cast<const int*>`), NOT a
164	  numeric value cast — so it is lossless for ALL int32, independent of magnitude.
165	  An equivalent alternative is to carry targets in `state`'s trailing slots; the
166	  bit-pack keeps `input` a single contiguous tensor, matching the decoder.)*
167	* `params` = flat `[418017]` fp32 (the `torch.cat` of `named_parameters()` in
168	  order — see `vit_param_layout()` / `vit_layout.cuh`).
169	* `state` = `[m|v|extra]` (`3*418017`) **+ 1 trailing loss slot** the kernel
170	  writes the mean CE into (read back in Python). AdamW uses only `m|v`.

359	
360	* **fp32 compute is the correctness baseline.** bf16 compute is a flagged
361	  follow-up (`TODO[bf16]` in `model_stage_vit.cuh`): it would roughly halve the
362	  ~184 KB smem and default to THIS fp32 path. The race's bf16-autocast default
363	  applies to the EAGER fallback, not the fused kernel (which raises/falls back
364	  under AMP — a loud None, never a silent stub).
365	* **vit × adamw on sm_90 only.** Other optimizers / models / gfx942 keep the
366	  eager (+ L1) path; only this one cell gets the real fwd+bwd+opt kernel (the
367	  same scope the decoder PHASE 1 took).
368	* **The surrogate `mega_vit_*.cu` cells remain compiled but unreachable on the
369	  race path** (the vit real path is routed before them in `fused_step`).
370	  Documented, not hidden.
371	* **No CUDA graphs** (owner directive) — the persistent megakernel + in-kernel
372	  grid barriers are the chosen "zero intermediate launches" mechanism.
373	* **Persistent flat-param + optimizer state are driver-owned**, allocated once
374	  and never reallocated (reallocating resets momentum → never groks). NOT
375	  checkpointed by `optimizer.state_dict()`.
376	* **The model must be eager** (not `torch.compile`-wrapped) on the fused path —
377	  the flat layout assumes the eager `named_parameters()` order. The race builds
378	  the ViT eager by default (`compile_model=False`).
379	* **Per-step workspace** is `nCTA × 418017` fp32 (~221 MB at 132 SMs), allocated
380	  once. A warp-per-sample concurrent variant + bf16 tensor-core matmuls are the
381	  perf follow-ups; this is a correctness/wiring deliverable.

94	## 2. THE one hard requirement: dynamic shared memory (don't drop it)
95	
96	Mamba's per-sample working set `MambaSampleSmem` is **145,124 bytes (≈141.72 KB)**
97	— **far over the 48 KB STATIC `__shared__` cap** (a static
98	`__shared__ MambaSampleSmem sm;` would **not compile**). This is an HONEST
99	deviation from the decoder's <48 KB static footprint: the decoder's
100	recompute-in-backward existed solely to clear 48 KB, but Mamba's **d_inner=256**
101	makes even one layer's activation set bump the cliff and the full live set is
102	~74 KB regardless — so recompute buys nothing, and the stages instead **cache both
103	layers' forward activations** (the clean, bug-free choice; the scan state stays in
104	per-thread registers, so smem does NOT explode to the ~128 KB an h-in-smem scan
105	would need).
106	
107	The composition launcher (`launch_fused_mamba_megakernel<Opt>`, to be written —
108	§3) MUST therefore declare the CTA smem **dynamic** and do **all three**:
109	
110	```cpp
111	const int dyn_smem = (int)sg::fused::sm90::kMambaSmemBytes;     // 145124
112	cudaFuncSetAttribute(&fused_mamba_megakernel<Opt>,
113	    cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, dyn_smem);     // (1) opt-in >48KB
114	cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor(&occ, ..., dyn_smem); // (2) honest occ
115	fused_mamba_megakernel<Opt><<<grid, 256, dyn_smem, stream>>>(...);  // (3) launch
116	```
117	
118	and the kernel allocates the struct from dynamic smem:
119	`extern __shared__ char smem_raw[]; auto& sm = *reinterpret_cast<MambaSampleSmem*>(smem_raw);`
120	
121	**145124 B ≪ the sm_90 ~227 KB per-block dynamic-optin cap** (≈82 KB headroom;
122	`kMambaSmemBytes < 224*1024` is static_asserted in `mamba3_layout.cuh`), and the
123	persistent megakernel is **one-CTA-per-SM by design** (gridDim = #SMs, grid
124	barrier over #SMs), so **occupancy = 1 IS the design point** — a 142 KB block at
125	occ=1 is intended, not a regression. **Missing any of the three steps makes the
126	kernel silently fail to launch.** The launcher's only job beyond the decoder's is
127	to pass `dyn_smem` (NOT 0) in all three places, on a device whose
128	`MaxDynamicSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin ≥ 145124` (every sm_90 satisfies this; the
129	launcher should `assert(occ>=1)` and REFUSE — return
130	`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources` — rather than hang the grid barrier, exactly like
131	`launch_fused_decoder_megakernel`).

135	## 3. Composition + stage / barrier layout (one persistent kernel)
136	
137	`fused_mamba_megakernel.cuh` (to be written, modeled BYTE-FOR-BYTE on
138	`fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh` with the dynamic-smem changes from §2 and the
139	Mamba constants). gridDim = #SMs (one CTA/SM), 256 threads/CTA, **batch-parallel**
140	(NOT the param-tensor work-steal queue — that would vary the batch→CTA grouping
141	and fp32 sums aren't associative):
142	
143	```
144	P0  each CTA zeroes its OWN grad-partial slice + loss slot
145	--- grid barrier B0 ---
146	P1  each CTA owns a FIXED contiguous batch slice (blockIdx.x); processes its
147	    samples ONE AT A TIME (CTA-cooperative): broadcasts the sample's 8 int tokens
148	    + target into smem, runs mb_forward_sample + mb_backward_sample, accumulating
149	    each sample's weight-grad into the CTA's partial with a SINGLE-OWNER-THREAD-
150	    PER-ELEMENT rule (no atomics → deterministic), and sums its slice's NLL (fp32)
151	--- grid barrier B1 ---
152	P2  deterministic cross-CTA reduce: sum partial[0..nCTA) in ASCENDING CTA index
153	    into the global grad (no float atomics; order fixed → reuses the work-steal
154	    queue to pick WHO reduces which tensor). Loss: fp64 ordered sum → loss/B → a
155	    device float the host reads back.
156	--- grid barrier B2 (sync_reset: also resets the queue for P3) ---
157	P3  the REAL apply_optimizer<Opt> tail consumes the reduced grad in place
158	```
159	
160	`n_tasks = 28` (`kMambaNumTensors`) for the reduce + optimizer phases; the kernel
161	reads per-tensor numel/offset from the generated `__constant__` tables
162	`kMambaSizes/kMambaOffsets` (mamba3_layout.cuh). Determinism: fixed batch→CTA
163	grouping + fixed ascending-CTA reduction order; **no float atomics** in the
164	weight-grad reduce.
165	
166	**Mamba-specific determinism notes (already handled in the stages — the integrator
167	does NOT re-derive, but should understand the contract):**
168	* the `tok.weight` scatter maps **thread→embedding column** and loops
169	  `(position)` sequentially, so colliding token ids (vocab 99) accumulate
170	  deterministically (the mirror's forced collision proves it).
171	* the selective-scan backward's `dB`/`dC` are SHARED across the d_inner channels,
172	  so they are reduced across threads via `mb_block_sum` in a **fixed ascending
173	  lane/warp order** (deterministic), NOT atomically. `dA_log` is per-channel
174	  (owner thread j) — a plain partial `+=`. `dx_main` (3 paths) and `ddt_pre` are
175	  per `(t,channel)` — owner thread j, plain writes.
176	
177	The `fused_mamba_megakernel` ALSO needs the `MambaTokenCtx` POD (mirror
178	`DecoderTokenCtx`: `const int* tokens; const int* targets; int B; float*
179	workspace; float* loss_out;`) and the `rebase_state<Opt>` helper — both already
180	exist in `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`; lift the pattern verbatim. (This header
181	does NOT exist yet because the directive scoped this phase to the stages+layout+
182	oracle/mirror+doc; it is straightforward to write from the decoder template.)
183	
184	**SMEM budget per CTA: `MambaSampleSmem` = 145124 B dynamic** (BOTH layers cached;
185	the scan state is per-thread registers).
186	
187	---

189	## 4. ABI seam (no `bindings.cpp` / `setup.py` edit — the owned extension points)
190	
191	The pybind `m.def("fused_step", ...)` arity is pinned in `bindings.cpp` (NOT
192	owned), so `fused_step`'s arity is unchanged. Carry the Mamba input through the
193	EXISTING `input`/`state`/`grad` tensors and add the **behavior** in `dispatch.cpp`
194	(owned), **identically to the decoder** (Mamba's input is int tokens, like the
195	decoder — NOT ViT's float pack).
196	
197	**Tensor contract (what Python passes; what dispatch.cpp reads):**
198	
199	* `input` = **int32** `[B*(8+1)]` contiguous — tokens `[B*8]` (row-major `[B][8]`)
200	  then targets `[B]`. `B = input.numel() / (kSeq+1) = numel / 9`. dispatch.cpp
201	  reads `tokens = input.data_ptr<int>()`, `targets = input.data_ptr<int>() + B*8`.
202	  (Seq/vocab/d/p are compile-time in `mamba3_layout.cuh`.)
203	* `params` = flat `[259425]` fp32 (the `torch.cat` of `named_parameters()` in
204	  order — see `mamba_param_layout()` / `mamba3_layout.cuh`).
205	* `state` = `[m|v|extra]` (`3*259425`) **+ 1 trailing loss slot** the kernel
206	  writes the mean CE into (read back in Python). AdamW uses only `m|v`.
207	* `grad` = the **reduced weight-grad OUTPUT** `[259425]` — the kernel writes the
208	  deterministically-reduced grad here (P2) and the optimizer tail consumes it in
209	  place (P3, no overwrite), so after the call this buffer holds exactly the grad
210	  AdamW used. **Routing it through the ABI `grad` tensor exposes the kernel's
211	  grads to the parity test** (`return_grad=True`) — the keystone check (§7 C.2),
212	  the only thing that exercises the hand-written selective-scan backward's
213	  magnitudes (loss is fwd-only; params-after-step is sign-dominated at step 1).
214	* the **workspace** (`nCTA*259425` grad partials + `nCTA` loss) is device scratch
215	  allocated in `dispatch.cpp` (keyed by device, like `decoder_scratch_for`) — it
216	  never crosses the ABI. At 132 SMs this is `132 × 259425 × 4 B ≈ 137 MB`,
217	  allocated once.

219	**routing** (add to `dispatch.cpp`, the `#if defined(WITH_CUDA)&&!defined(WITH_HIP)`

342	## 6. Python wiring (`grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py`)
343	
344	Mirror the decoder's PHASE-1 hooks for `"mamba"`:
345	
346	* `_MAMBA_TOTAL_ELEMS = 259425` (the no-GPU test can cross-check this against
347	  `mamba_param_layout()["total"]`).
348	* `has_l3_real("mamba", "adamw")` → True on sm_90 with the built extension exposing
349	  `fused_step` AND the dispatch.cpp branch above (the readiness gate; loud-None,
350	  never a silent stub).
351	* `fused_train_step("mamba", opt, module, optimizer, tokens, targets, ...)` — packs
352	  the int32 `input` (tokens `[B*8]` ++ targets `[B]`, §4), owns the persistent
353	  flat-param + `[m|v|extra]+loss` state buffers (keyed by model on the optimizer
354	  instance, allocated once — reallocating resets momentum → never groks), calls
355	  `ops.fused_step(..., opt_only=False)`, scatters updated params back, reads the
356	  loss slot, and (if `return_grad=True`) returns the reduced `grad` tensor.
357	  **Signature must match** `test_mamba_megakernel.py`'s GPU-gated helpers when
358	  they are un-skipped (they currently `pytest.skip` pending this seam).
359	* The race's Mamba `train_adamw` loop calls a `_try_fused_train_step(...)` FIRST
360	  for the mamba cell (mirror the decoder hook): if the L3-REAL kernel is available
361	  it runs the whole step (fwd+bwd+adamw) and the loop skips its own eager
362	  fwd/bwd/`optimizer.step()`; otherwise falls back to eager. `eval_every` stays
363	  eager. **The model must be eager** (the race builds Mamba with
364	  `compile_model=False`; `grad_checkpoint` is irrelevant to the fused path since
365	  the kernel owns the whole fwd+bwd).

379	    > csrc/fused/sm_90/mamba3_layout.cuh && git diff --stat # EXPECT: no diff

386

392	Expected GPU results (the gates encoded in `test_mamba_megakernel.py`, currently
393	`pytest.skip` until the seam lands):
394	* C single-step: kernel loss within **1e-5 rel** of eager; **every** weight grad
395	  within **1e-4 rel** of the oracle (per-tensor dump) — the keystone that
396	  exercises the selective-scan backward; params after 1 step **1e-5 rel**.
397	* D trajectory: 200-step loss curve within **1e-3 rel** of eager AdamW; final
398	  params **1e-3 rel** (fp32 drift).
399	* E grok: 3 seeds, best test acc **≥ 0.95** through the race's Mamba train path
400	  (the `(a÷b₁÷b₂÷b₃) mod 97` sequential-division task).
401	
402	---
403	
404	## 8. Known scope / caveats (PHASE 2)
405	
406	* **fp32 compute is the correctness baseline.** bf16 compute is a flagged
407	  follow-up (`TODO(bf16)` in `model_stage_mamba3.cuh`): it would roughly halve the
408	  ~142 KB smem and default to THIS fp32 path. The scan recurrence in particular is
409	  exp/accumulation-heavy and would keep fp32 accumulators even under bf16 storage.
410	  The race's auto-precision for mamba is already **fp32** (`_AUTO_PRECISION`
411	  line 606), so there is no AMP mismatch to guard on the eager fallback.
412	* **mamba × adamw on sm_90 only.** Other optimizers / models / gfx942 keep the
413	  eager (+ L1) path; only this one cell gets the real fwd+bwd+opt kernel (the same
414	  scope the decoder PHASE 1 + ViT PHASE 2 took).
415	* **The surrogate `mega_mamba_*.cu` cells remain compiled but unreachable on the
416	  race path** (the mamba real path is routed before them in `fused_step`).
417	  Documented, not hidden.
418	* **No CUDA graphs** (owner directive) — the persistent megakernel + in-kernel
419	  grid barriers are the chosen "zero intermediate launches" mechanism.
420	* **The selective scan runs per-channel in registers** (the seq=8 exploit): one
421	  thread owns channel j∈[0,256), holds h[16] in registers, unrolls t=0..7; the
422	  backward recomputes that forward (h_hist[9][16] in registers — seq=8, so NO
423	  checkpoint, unlike the long-sequence `scan_backward_kernel` in
424	  `csrc/scan/mamba_scan_adapter.cuh`) then reverse-scans. This is what keeps the
425	  smem at ~142 KB instead of the ~128 KB/sample an h-in-smem scan would add. The
426	  derivation is written out in `mamba_oracle.py::selective_scan_backward` and
427	  cross-checked against the existing `scan_backward_kernel`.
428	* **Persistent flat-param + optimizer state are driver-owned**, allocated once and
429	  never reallocated (reallocating resets momentum → never groks). NOT checkpointed
430	  by `optimizer.state_dict()`.
431	* **Per-step workspace** is `nCTA × 259425` fp32 (~137 MB at 132 SMs), allocated
432	  once. A warp-per-sample concurrent variant + bf16 tensor-core matmuls are the
433	  perf follow-ups; this is a correctness/wiring deliverable.
434	* **`csrc/scan` is READ-ONLY for this phase** and was used only as a cross-check
435	  reference for the scan backward; the stages do NOT depend on it (they are
436	  self-contained per COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md: `megakernel_common.cuh` +
437	  `mamba3_layout.cuh` + CUDA only).

2	
3	Owner handoff for **`csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_stage_supergrok2.cuh`** (the full SG2
4	CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta-net as in-kernel stages of ONE persistent kernel). This

6	exactly what to wire. The header author may NOT touch `bindings.cpp`,

11	includes only the substrate (`megakernel_common.cuh`) + the algorithm header
12	(`csrc/algorithms/supergrok2.h`) + CUDA. No globals; all state flows through the

17	## 0. What it is (one line)
18	
19	`launch_sg2_meta_optimizer_tail<Dims, ParamT, GradT>(...)` runs the ENTIRE SG2
20	optimizer step (input-proj+sort-gather → CSA → HCA → matrix-GRU → PEER+experts →
21	sg2_apply_step) for **all** parameter tensors in **ONE persistent kernel** —
22	replacing the per-op path's ~15-20 launches/tensor (`csa_hca_step_one`).
23	
24	**Launch count, per parameter tensor, per optimizer step:**
25	- before: **~15-20** kernel launches (+ host ATen mm/topk/softmax dispatches)
26	- after: **1 batched argsort prep** (one torch call for ALL tensors) **+ 1
27	  persistent kernel** (processes all tensors via the task queue).
28	
29	The argsort is the ONE explicitly-retained pre-kernel step (honesty rail #5 —
30	see §5). Everything else is launch-free and HBM-round-trip-free for the meta
31	weights (the bundle is staged into shared memory once per CTA).

39	`supergrok2_batched_step` weight/state argument list, plus the persistent-kernel

158	## 2. Python driver call-shape
159	
160	This is the driver the optimizer would call instead of the per-op
161	`ops.supergrok2_batched_step`. It is documented here (not added to the shared
162	`grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py`, which is sibling territory). Drop it into a
163	`@torch.no_grad()` helper on the SuperGrok2 optimizer once the binding exists.
164	
165	```python
166	import torch
167	from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import get_ops
168	from csrc... import SG2Dims  # dims are compile-time in C++; mirror them in py for packing
169	
170	def sg2_step_megakernel(self, params, grads, sharpness_list, states, meta, scalars):
171	    """ONE persistent-kernel SG2 optimizer step over ALL param tensors.
172	    states: dict of lists per tensor (exp_avg, exp_avg_sq, mu, slow, gru_state).
173	    meta:   the meta weight bundle (fp32). scalars: per-tensor + shared."""
174	    ops = get_ops()
175	    GH = 4  # gru_hidden (== meta net default)
176	
177	    # 1) PACK all tensors back-to-back (one contiguous fp32 buffer each). The
178	    #    kernel addresses tensor t at row_off[t] .. row_off[t]+n[t].
179	    P = len(params)
180	    n = torch.tensor([p.numel() for p in params], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
181	    row_off = torch.zeros(P, dtype=torch.int64, device=dev)
182	    row_off[1:] = torch.cumsum(n.to(torch.int64), 0)[:-1]
183	    total = int(n.sum())
184	
185	    def pack(lst, width=1):
186	        out = torch.empty(total * width, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
187	        for t, x in enumerate(lst):
188	            o = int(row_off[t]) * width
189	            out[o:o + x.numel()] = x.reshape(-1).float()
190	        return out
191	
192	    params_packed = pack([p.data for p in params])
193	    grads_packed  = pack(grads)
194	    sharp_packed  = pack(sharpness_list)
195	    exp_avg_packed    = pack(states['exp_avg'])
196	    exp_avg_sq_packed = pack(states['exp_avg_sq'])
197	    mu_packed   = pack(states['mu'])
198	    slow_packed = pack(states['slow'])
199	    gru_state_packed = pack(states['gru_state'], width=GH)  # [total*GH] row-major
200	
201	    # 2) THE ONE EXPLICIT PRE-KERNEL SORT (honesty rail #5). Per tensor, argsort
202	    #    |grad| ASCENDING, STABLE — reproducing csa_hca_step_one's
203	    #    `sort_keys.sort(0, descending=false)`. Build perm/unsort PACKED, with
204	    #    indices LOCAL to each tensor (in [0, n[t])).
205	    perm_packed   = torch.empty(total, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
206	    unsort_packed = torch.empty(total, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
207	    for t, gt in enumerate(grads):
208	        o, m = int(row_off[t]), int(n[t])
209	        # MATCH THE REFERENCE SORT EXACTLY. csa_hca_step_one does
210	        #   sort_keys.sort(0, descending=false)  — plain torch.sort, which is
211	        # NOT stable on CUDA. To stay bit-aligned with the parity oracle on tied
212	        # |grad| values, reproduce THAT call (do NOT force stable=True — that
213	        # would break ties differently and drift the GPU parity over 200 steps).
214	        _, perm = gt.reshape(-1).abs().sort(dim=0, descending=False)    # [m]
215	        unsort = perm.argsort()                                         # inverse perm
216	        perm_packed[o:o + m]   = perm.to(torch.int32)
217	        unsort_packed[o:o + m] = unsort.to(torch.int32)
218	
219	    # 3) Per-CTA workspace. ws_stride = sg2_ws_stride<Dims>(Nmax) — mirror the C++
220	    #    formula in py (see csrc header) or expose it via a tiny binding. Allocate
221	    #    n_ctas (== #SMs) slices; n_ctas can be queried once and cached.
222	    Nmax = int(n.max())
223	    ws_stride = sg2_ws_stride_py(Nmax, GH=GH)   # mirror of the C++ sg2_ws_stride
224	    n_ctas = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(dev).multi_processor_count
225	    workspace = torch.empty(n_ctas * ws_stride, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
226	
227	    # 4) Persistent-context scratch (zero-init; the launcher re-zeros each call).
228	    g_next_task  = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
229	    g_arrived    = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
230	    g_generation = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
231	
232	    # 5) Meta bundle as fp32 (upcast ONCE here — the kernel is fp32-compute).
233	    meta_f32 = {k: v.float().contiguous() for k, v in meta.items()}
234	
235	    # 6) Per-tensor scalar arrays (length P) — the layer-scaled betas/alphas the
236	    #    per-op path already computes per tensor.
237	    alpha     = torch.tensor(scalars['alpha'],     dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
238	    gru_decay = torch.tensor(scalars['gru_decay'], dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
239	    lamb_eff  = torch.tensor(scalars['lamb_eff'],  dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
240	    beta1     = torch.tensor(scalars['beta1'],     dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
241	    bc1       = torch.tensor(scalars['bc1'],       dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
242	    bc2       = torch.tensor(scalars['bc2'],       dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
243	
244	    ops.sg2_meta_optimizer_tail(
245	        params_packed, grads_packed, sharp_packed,
246	        exp_avg_packed, exp_avg_sq_packed, mu_packed, slow_packed,
247	        gru_state_packed, perm_packed, unsort_packed, n, row_off,
248	        workspace, ws_stride,
249	        meta_f32['input_proj_W'], meta_f32['input_proj_b'],
250	        meta_f32['csa_q_W'], meta_f32['csa_k_W'], meta_f32['csa_v_W'], meta_f32['csa_out_W'],
251	        meta_f32['csa_compress_w'], meta_f32['csa_idx_DQ'], meta_f32['csa_idx_K'],
252	        meta_f32['hca_q_W'], meta_f32['hca_k_W'], meta_f32['hca_v_W'], meta_f32['hca_out_W'],
253	        meta_f32['gru_Wz'], meta_f32['gru_bz'], meta_f32['gru_Wr'], meta_f32['gru_br'],
254	        meta_f32['gru_Wh'], meta_f32['gru_bh'],
255	        meta_f32['peer_query_Ws'], meta_f32['prod_keys_A'], meta_f32['prod_keys_B'],
256	        meta_f32['expert_W1'], meta_f32['expert_b1'], meta_f32['expert_W2'], meta_f32['expert_b2'],
257	        alpha, gru_decay, lamb_eff, beta1, bc1, bc2,
258	        scalars['rescale'], scalars['beta2'], scalars['lr'], scalars['wd'], scalars['eps'],
259	        g_next_task, g_arrived, g_generation)
260	
261	    # 7) UNPACK results back into the per-tensor buffers (params + carried state).
262	    for t, p in enumerate(params):
263	        o, m = int(row_off[t]), int(n[t])
264	        p.data.copy_(params_packed[o:o + m].reshape(p.shape))
265	        states['exp_avg'][t].copy_(exp_avg_packed[o:o + m].reshape(-1))
266	        states['exp_avg_sq'][t].copy_(exp_avg_sq_packed[o:o + m].reshape(-1))
267	        states['mu'][t].copy_(mu_packed[o:o + m].reshape(-1))
268	        states['slow'][t].copy_(slow_packed[o:o + m].reshape(-1))
269	        states['gru_state'][t].copy_(
270	            gru_state_packed[o*GH:(o+m)*GH].reshape(m, GH))
271	```
272	
273	The packing/unpacking is overhead the L3 combined cell can elide by keeping the
274	optimizer state PERMANENTLY packed (see §3). For an isolated optimizer tail the
275	copies are cheap relative to the eliminated launches.

277	### `sg2_ws_stride_py` (mirror of the C++ formula — keep in sync)
278	
279	```python
280	def sg2_ws_stride_py(Nmax, d=8, rk=4, GH=4, csa_compress=4, csa_topk=16):
281	    Ncmax = (Nmax + csa_compress - 1) // csa_compress
282	    topk = max(csa_topk, 1)
283	    return (Nmax*d*7      # x_sorted, csa_ctx, hca_ctx, q, win_k, win_v, concat
284	            + Ncmax*d*2   # c_k, c_v
285	            + Nmax*rk     # qI
286	            + Ncmax*rk    # kI
287	            + Nmax*topk   # sel (int, 1 float each)
288	            + Nmax*GH     # new_gru
289	            + Nmax)       # expert_out
290	    # NOTE: the authoritative count is C++ sg2_ws_stride<Dims>(Nmax) — prefer
291	    # exposing THAT via a 1-line binding over duplicating it. The slot list is:
292	    # x_sorted, csa_ctx, hca_ctx, q, c_k, c_v, win_k, win_v, qI, kI, sel, concat,
293	    # new_gru, expert_out (14 slots).
294	```

302	## 3. What the COMBINED (model-fused L3) cell must wire
303	
304	This header is the **optimizer half** — the L1-style contract agent A
305	established, now with SG2's FULL meta-net inside one persistent kernel instead of
306	~20 launches. Composing it with a model fwd/bwd stage (decoder/vit/mamba3) into
307	ONE cell (`mega_<model>_supergrok2.cu`) is the integrator's job. The combined
308	cell must:
309	
310	1. **Run the model fwd+bwd FIRST**, producing the REAL reduced gradient into the
311	   packed `grads_packed` buffer (same packing as §2 — the model's weight-grad
312	   reduction writes the flat grad the SG2 tail consumes). This is the L3
313	   structure of `fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`: P0 zero → P1 fwd+bwd → P2
314	   deterministic reduce → **then** the optimizer tail.
315	
316	2. **Share the PersistentContext**: the model stages and the SG2 stages use the
317	   SAME `ctx` (task queue + grid barrier). After the model's reduce phase, call
318	   `bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task)` (as the decoder cell does at B2) to reset
319	   the queue for the SG2 tensor loop, THEN inline `sg2_meta_stages<Dims>` per
320	   tensor instead of `apply_optimizer<Opt>`. The ONE grid barrier the SG2
321	   launcher does at the end is then redundant inside the combined cell — drop it
322	   (the combined kernel exits after the apply, like the decoder cell's P3).
323	
324	3. **Keep the optimizer state PERMANENTLY packed** so no per-step pack/unpack is
325	   needed — the model's grad reduction already writes into the packed layout, and
326	   the SG2 tail reads/writes the same packed state in place. The perm/unsort sort
327	   (§5) still runs as the one pre-kernel step (it needs the freshly-reduced grad).
328	
329	4. **Workspace sizing**: the combined cell's workspace must hold BOTH the model's
330	   grad-partial workspace AND the SG2 per-CTA meta scratch (`ws_stride` slices).
331	   They are used in disjoint phases (model reduce, then SG2), so they MAY alias
332	   the same allocation if sized for the max — but simplest is two regions.
333	
334	5. **`perm`/`unsort` must be recomputed AFTER the model bwd** (the grad is only
335	   known then). For a pure optimizer-only cell the driver computes them up front
336	   (§2); for the combined cell they are computed between the reduce phase and the
337	   SG2 phase — either a tiny argsort launch (the one retained launch) or, as the
338	   path-to-zero in §5, an in-kernel segmented-sort stage.

368	## 5. The sort (honesty rail #5) — residual + path to zero
369	
370	`csa_hca_step_one` sorts each tensor's sequence by `|grad|` ASCENDING via a HOST
371	`torch::sort`. **There is no device sort kernel in the repo** (verified). A
372	single device sort over the PACKED buffer would be WRONG: SG2 attention is
373	per-tensor (each flat grad vector is its own length-N sequence), so a global sort
374	would cross tensor boundaries. The sort is therefore left as **ONE explicit
375	pre-kernel step** (a per-tensor `torch.argsort`, §2 step 2) producing the
376	`perm`/`unsort` index buffers the kernel consumes.
377	
378	> **Residual: 1 argsort prep + 1 persistent kernel, vs the previous ~15-20
379	> launches per tensor.** The argsort is ONE torch op for all tensors; everything
380	> else (CSA/HCA/GRU/PEER/apply) is launch-free.
381	
382	**Path to zero extra launches**: add a device **segmented bitonic sort** as
383	STAGE -1 of the kernel — per tensor, sort its `[N]` keys (= `|grad|`) in shared
384	memory with barrier-separated bitonic passes, writing `perm`/`unsort`. N here is
385	a single tensor's element count (the largest race param is ~1e5), so an in-CTA
386	segmented sort is feasible. The header is written so this drops in cleanly: STAGE
387	-1 only needs to populate `perm`/`unsort` before STAGE 0; no other stage changes.
388	This was deliberately NOT done in this pass (it is a separate, larger piece of
389	work) to keep the pass at **maximal HONEST launch-elimination of everything
390	else** with bit-faithful math — per honesty rail #5.
391	
392	**Sort tie-handling (subtle — get this right)**: reproduce the reference's
393	EXACT sort call `sort_keys.sort(0, descending=false)` (plain `torch.sort`, which
394	is NOT stable on CUDA) — NOT `argsort(stable=True)`. The megakernel and the
395	parity oracle must consume the SAME `perm`; on tied `|grad|` an unstable-vs-stable
396	mismatch breaks ties differently → different sorted order → CSA/HCA diverge past
397	1e-5 over the 200-step trajectory. The §2 driver uses the exact `.sort(...)` call.
398	(Lower-risk sibling: the PEER top-k uses descending insertion sort vs the
399	reference's `torch.topk`; identical for distinct scores, tie-order unspecified in
400	both — list it among the parity hotspots but it rarely bites.)

28	| supergrok15  | STAGED         | `st.mu` (`st.gate` = host scalar) | `sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor` (per-tensor) |
29	| supergrok2   | SKIP           | (sibling-owned)      | — |
30	
31	For the 3 NOTHING-NEEDED optimizers the codegen maps OptId → "no precompute
32	stage": their apply already runs a complete tail. `optimizer_needs_precompute
33	<Opt>::value` is `false` for them and a `static_assert` in
34	`optimizer_precompute_stage<Opt>` rejects an accidental instantiation.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## 1. The `PrecomputeWorkspace` POD (host allocation)
39	
40	The cross-CTA stages reduce through global scratch grouped in
41	`PrecomputeWorkspace` (mirrors `PersistentContext`: one POD so the codegen kernel
42	signature stays uniform). The host allocates ONLY the pointers the chosen
43	optimizer uses and zero-fills the rest; a stage dereferences only its own
44	optimizer's buffers. All FP32.
45	
46	| field | size (floats) | used by | meaning |
47	|-------|---------------|---------|---------|
48	| `prodigy_partials` | `2 * n_ctas` | prodigy | per-CTA (r,s) slots: `[0..n_ctas)`=r, `[n_ctas..2n_ctas)`=s |
49	| `prodigy_d` | `1` | prodigy | reduced d; bind `st.d_factor = prodigy_d[0]` |
50	| `muon_buf` | `rows*cols` | muon | momentum buffer (persists across steps) |
51	| `muon_X` | `rows*cols` | muon | current NS iterate |
52	| `muon_A` | `rows*rows` | muon | `A = X Xᵀ` |
53	| `muon_AX` | `rows*cols` | muon | `A X` |
54	| `muon_AAX` | `rows*cols` | muon | `A (A X)` |
55	| `muon_orth` | `rows*cols` | muon | NS output; bind `st.orth = muon_orth` |
56	| `muon_nrm_partials` | `n_ctas` | muon | per-CTA `‖buf‖_F²` slots |
57	| `muon_inv_norm` | `1` | muon | `1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7)` |
58	
59	`n_ctas == #SMs` (one persistent CTA per SM, `fused_megakernel.cuh:357`). The
60	muon matrix buffers are sized for the **largest** 2D weight processed (the stage
61	runs one matrix at a time; reuse the buffers across matrices).
62	
63	`prodigy_partials`, `muon_nrm_partials`, `prodigy_d`, `muon_inv_norm` must be
64	**zero-initialized before launch** (like the barrier counters,
65	`fused_megakernel.cuh:363-374`) — the owner-computes reducer reads every slot.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 2. STAGED — prodigy (cross-ALL-tensors d, owner-computes tree)
70	
71	**Shape:** GLOBAL. One scalar `d` for the whole model; `r,s` sum over every
72	element of every parameter tensor.
73	
74	**Determinism deviation (contract-mandated, documented — not a transcription):**
75	the live per-op path reduces `r,s` with `atomicAdd` (`prodigy_sm90.cuh:105-108`,
76	`:135-138`). The COMPONENT_CONTRACT requires deterministic / no-float-atomic
77	reductions, so the stage REPLACES that with an owner-computes tree: each CTA
78	publishes its own `(r,s)` slot (no contention, no atomic) → grid barrier → one
79	owner thread sums the slots in ascending index order. Math-equivalent in exact
80	arithmetic; fp32 summation order is now fixed/reproducible.
81	
82	**Host/cell vs in-kernel split (faithful to the live multi-tensor driver):** the
83	PERSISTENT beta3-EMA decay of `(r,s)` across steps and the `d_coef` scaling live
84	in the host launcher (`prodigy_sm90.cuh:488-521`, `bindings.cpp:1246-1264`),
85	OUTSIDE `prodigy.h`. They are NOT in-kernel. The stage computes the INSTANTANEOUS
86	per-step `Σ r / Σ s` + `prodigy_update_d` (the cross-tensor reduction Audit-C
87	flagged). A cell that wants the grokking-race EMA estimator must, BETWEEN
88	phaseA-publish and phaseB-reduce: decay the prior `prodigy_partials` by `beta3`
89	and scale `r` by `d_coef` (host-side, on the workspace buffers) — exactly as the
90	live driver does around the same `prodigy_update_d`. The device math
91	(`prodigy.h`) stays byte-unchanged either way.
92	
93	**Codegen barrier sequence (per L3/L1 step):**
94	
95	```
96	// param_init = the Prodigy trajectory anchor (flat blob parallel to params).
97	optimizer_precompute_stage<Prodigy>(ctx, params, grad, sizes, offsets, st, ws,
98	                                    /*param_init=*/param_init);   // phaseA
99	bar.sync_reset(ctx.g_next_task);            // grid barrier; reset queue for reuse
100	prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB(ctx, st.d_factor, ws);          // owner-sum → d
101	bar.sync();                                  // d visible to all before apply
102	st.d_factor = ws.prodigy_d[0];               // bind the reduced d for the tail
103	// re-drain the queue for the apply (fused_optimizer_stage / the L3 bwd+opt):
104	apply_optimizer<Prodigy> over all tensors (opt_components.cuh:211-215).
105	```
106	
107	`st.d_factor` enters phaseA as `d_prev` (the comparison floor) and is OVERWRITTEN
108	post-reduce with the new `d`. Two grid barriers (reduce-publish, d-visible) plus
109	the queue resets — consistent with `fused_megakernel.cuh`'s phase pipeline.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## 3. STAGED — muon (Newton-Schulz orthogonalization, grid-cooperative)
114	
115	**Shape:** per-MATRIX, GRID-COOPERATIVE. A matmul is cross-element and a real 2D
116	weight does not fit one CTA's SMEM, so all CTAs cooperate on ONE matrix at a
117	time. This does NOT fit the flat one-CTA-per-tensor `(params, sizes, offsets)`
118	signature; the codegen drives the explicit phase fns (the
119	`optimizer_precompute_stage<Muon>` branch is a documented no-op that points
120	here).
121	
122	**New device code, cited:** the live path delegates `X Xᵀ`/`A X`/`A (A X)` to
123	`torch::mm`/cuBLAS (`bindings.cpp:992-994`), NOT a per-element canonical fn — so
124	the stage's tiled owner-computes matmul (`muon_matmul`) is legitimate new device
125	code, cited to that mm sequence. The drift guard requires only that the
126	ELEMENT-WISE pieces call `muon.h`: the momentum body and the NS polynomial
127	combine do (`muon_momentum_normalize_step` `muon.h:33-46`, `muon_ns_combine_step`
128	`muon.h:49-60`). The matmul contracts the k-dimension in ascending order (one
129	thread owns one output element) — deterministic fp32, no atomic.
130	
131	**1D params are NOT handled here** — they take the AdamW tail upstream
132	(`muon.h:75-76`, `bindings.cpp:970-977`). The codegen routes only 2D weights to
133	this stage.
134	
135	**Codegen sequence (per 2D matrix, `numel = rows*cols`, `ns_steps` default 5):**
136	
137	```
138	muon_momentum_norm_phaseA(grad_mtx, numel, momentum, ws);  // buf=μ·buf+g; ‖buf‖² slots
139	bar.sync();
140	muon_norm_reduce_phaseB(ctx, ws);                          // owner-sum → inv_norm
141	bar.sync();
142	muon_scale_X(numel, ws);                                   // X = buf*inv_norm (bindings.cpp:964)
143	bar.sync();
144	for (s = 0; s < ns_steps; ++s) {
145	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_X,  ws.muon_X, ws.muon_A,  rows, rows, cols, cols, cols, /*bT=*/true);  // A=XXᵀ
146	    bar.sync();
147	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_A,  ws.muon_X, ws.muon_AX, rows, cols, rows, rows, cols, /*bT=*/false); // AX
148	    bar.sync();
149	    muon_matmul(ws.muon_A,  ws.muon_AX,ws.muon_AAX,rows, cols, rows, rows, cols, /*bT=*/false); // A·AX
150	    bar.sync();
151	    muon_ns_combine_phase(numel, ws);                      // orth = a·X + b·AX + c·AAX
152	    bar.sync();
153	    std::swap(ws.muon_X, ws.muon_orth);  // next iter reads X; last iter result is in X
154	}
155	// After the loop the final orthogonalized matrix is in ws.muon_X (an odd # of
156	// swaps) — bind st.orth to whichever buffer holds the last combine output. With
157	// ns_steps swaps, the final result is in ws.muon_X iff ns_steps is even, else
158	// ws.muon_orth; the codegen tracks the parity (or copies into muon_orth once).
159	scale = 0.2f * sqrtf((float)max(rows, cols));   // bindings.cpp:981
160	st.orth         = <final NS buffer>;
161	st.neg_lr_scale = -lr * scale;                  // bindings.cpp:982
162	st.decay_factor = 1.0f - lr * wd;               // bindings.cpp:983
163	apply_optimizer<Muon> over this matrix (opt_components.cuh:230-234 → muon.h:63-73).
164	```
165	
166	`+1e-7` Frobenius-norm epsilon is in `muon_norm_reduce_phaseB`
167	(`opt_stages_precompute.cuh::kMuonNormEps`, `bindings.cpp:962`, `ref_muon_step`).
168	NS coefficients `(3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315)` are `kMuonNS_{A,B,C}`
169	(`bindings.cpp:938-940`).
170	
171	> Implementation note for the codegen author: per-matrix grid-cooperative
172	> orthogonalization inside ONE persistent megakernel is the heaviest stage; if a
173	> cell is register/SMEM-bound it may keep muon's NS as a SEPARATE launch (the L1
174	> tail still runs `apply_optimizer<Muon>` in-kernel reading `st.orth` produced by
175	> that launch) — exactly the split `opt_components.cuh:19-26` documents. The
176	> stage here makes the fully-in-kernel path POSSIBLE; choosing it per cell is a
177	> codegen/tier decision, not forced.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 4. STAGED — supergrok11 (meta-MLP mu + per-TENSOR cosine gate)
182	
183	**Shape: PER-TENSOR, SINGLE-DRAIN, NO grid barrier** — and the "no barrier" is
184	correct for a SUBTLE reason, NOT by analogy to anything. The live per-op path
185	(`bindings.cpp:1407-1416`) loops per parameter doing metanet→gate→adam, with each
186	tensor SELF-CONTAINED: `gate(T)` and `apply(T)` depend ONLY on `mu(T)`, never on
187	any other tensor's mu (`bindings.cpp:1411` computes the gate INSIDE the per-param
188	loop; `compute_cosine_gate_fused` takes ONE tensor's smart_grad/mu). So mu/gate/
189	apply for one tensor fuse into ONE body owned end-to-end by the SAME CTA inside
190	the codegen's existing single task-queue drain (`fused_optimizer_stage`,
191	`fused_megakernel.cuh:101-142`).
192	
193	> **Why NOT a separate full-queue mu pre-pass (the rejected Design A):** a mu
194	> stage that drains the queue to `n_tasks` and a SEPARATE apply drain would (a)
195	> need a grid barrier for cross-CTA mu visibility AND (b) **silently no-op** — the
196	> apply drain's `next_block()` returns `t >= n_tasks` immediately (the counter was
197	> consumed) and never applies, unless a `sync_reset` re-zeros it. The single-drain
198	> per-tensor form has NO such hazard. (Prodigy DOES use a barrier because its `d`
199	> is a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction — SG11's gate is per-tensor, so the
200	> cases are NOT analogous.)
201	
202	- **mu(T) — per ELEMENT**: `mu[i] = rescale · phi(grad[i], sharpness[i])` over the
203	  tensor slice (the meta-net is a per-TENSOR weight set).
204	- **gate(T) — per TENSOR**: block-level cosine tree over the SAME tensor's
205	  elements via the deterministic `block_reduce_sum_f32` (`primitives.cuh:125`) —
206	  no cross-CTA, no atomic.
207	
208	`sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>` does BOTH (mu→`__syncthreads`→gate)
209	in one per-tensor call and RETURNS the gate; `sg_stage_phi_weights<32>` stages the
210	phi weights to SMEM once per block before the loop.
211	
212	**Gate formula — mirror the CODE not the stale comment.**
213	`compute_cosine_gate_fused` (`supergrok11_sm90.cuh:280-285`) computes
214	`clamp(<sg,mu> / sqrt(‖sg‖²·‖mu‖² + 1e-12), 0, 1)` with `sg == grad` (because
215	`bindings.cpp:1408` calls `mu_metanet` with `alpha=0`, so `smart_grad == grad`).
216	It **IGNORES** `gate_temp` despite the `bindings.cpp:1276` comment claiming
217	`sigmoid(t·cos)` — the function does a bare clamp, and `ref_sg11_step` agrees.
218	
219	**Codegen sequence (ONE task-queue drain; mu+gate+apply fused per tensor):**
220	
221	```
222	__shared__ float sW1[32*2], sb1[32], sW2[32];
223	sg_stage_phi_weights<32>(W1, b1, W2, sW1, sb1, sW2);   // once per block (syncs)
224	TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
225	for (int t = q.next_block(&slot); t < ctx.n_tasks; t = q.next_block(&slot)) {
226	    int   n   = sizes[t];
227	    int64 off = offsets[t];
228	    // mu(T)→global, sync, gate(T) — SAME CTA owns T; reads the mu it just wrote.
229	    float gate = sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>(
230	        st.mu, grad, sharpness, sW1, sb1, sW2, b2, rescale, off, n);
231	    FusedOptState ts = st;  ts.gate = gate;            // bind the per-tensor gate
232	    // apply over [off, off+n): the tail reads ts.mu + ts.gate.
233	    apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11> elementwise over the slice (opt_components.cuh:235-239).
234	}
235	```
236	No grid barrier, no `sync_reset` — one drain, race-free.
237	
238	> The apply (`sg11_sweep_b_step`, `supergrok11.h:79-111`) uses `smart_grad = g +
239	> (1-gate)*alpha*mu`. The live driver folds `ramp*lamb` into a `lamb_eff`
240	> multiplier (`bindings.cpp:1400-1416`); if a cell needs that, it sets
241	> `st.alpha = ramp*lamb*alpha` (the apply's `alpha` slot) so the single live
242	> correction matches — a scalar binding, no math change.
243	
244	### ⚠ ABI GAP — `sharpness` is not in `FusedOptState` (flag loudly)
245	
246	`sharpness` is **model-coupled**, exactly like looksam's `sam_dir`: it is
247	`(sam_grad − normal_grad)²` from a SAM SECOND backward
248	(`sg11_sharpness_restore_kernel`, `supergrok11_sm90.cuh:236-248`).
249	`FusedOptState` (`opt_components.cuh:84-113`, which the stage header MUST NOT
250	edit) has a `mu` field but **NO `sharpness` field and NO phi-weight fields**.
251	Therefore the stage takes `sharpness` + `(W1,b1,W2,b2,rescale)` as **explicit
252	pointers/scalars**, and the cell must supply a sharpness buffer the current ABI
253	does not carry. Two integration options (a sibling agent owning `opt_components
254	.cuh` chooses):
255	
256	1. **Extend the ABI** (preferred long-term): add `const float* sharpness` and the
257	   phi-weight pointers to `FusedOptState`, populated by the cell like the other
258	   model-coupled inputs. Requires editing `opt_components.cuh` (out of THIS
259	   phase's scope).
260	2. **Side-channel pointers** (no ABI change): the cell passes `sharpness` + phi
261	   weights as extra kernel arguments straight into
262	   `sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor<32>` / `sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor
263	   <32>` (their signatures take them explicitly). The codegen threads them
264	   alongside `FusedOptState`.
265	
266	Until one is wired, an SG11/SG15 cell CANNOT run fully in-kernel — the
267	sharpness pipeline (SAM perturb → 2nd backward → restore) is a model-stage
268	responsibility documented here, not faked in the optimizer stage.
269	
270	---
271	
272	## 5. STAGED — supergrok15 (meta-MLP mu; gate is a host scalar)
273	
274	Same PER-TENSOR single-drain shape as SG11 — but SIMPLER: NO gate stage at all
275	(the phi-net shares the SG11/SG15 form, `supergrok15.h:34-52`). DIFFERENCES:
276	
277	- **gate is GLOBAL = sigmoid(training accuracy)**, set HOST-side and passed as a
278	  scalar (`supergrok15.h:85`), already carried by `FusedScalars.gate`
279	  (`opt_components.cuh:153`). **No gate reduction stage, no per-tensor gate.**
280	- the per-coord alpha clip (`sg15_alpha_per_coord`, `supergrok15.h:68-75`) and
281	  `smart_grad = g + gate*a*mu` happen INSIDE the apply tail
282	  (`apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15>` → `sg15_sweep_b_step`,
283	  `opt_components.cuh:240-244`). So the ONLY precompute is `mu`.
284	- `sg15_sweep_a` also accumulates a `sharpness²` partial
285	  (`supergrok15_sm90.cuh:99-102`) that updates the NEXT step's `sharpness` input
286	  host-side; it is NOT consumed by THIS step's apply (which reads `mu` + the host
287	  gate). It is part of the model-coupled sharpness pipeline, documented here,
288	  not computed in this step's optimizer precompute.
289	
290	**Codegen sequence (ONE drain; mu+apply fused per tensor, no gate, no barrier):**
291	
292	```
293	__shared__ float sW1[32*2], sb1[32], sW2[32];
294	sg_stage_phi_weights<32>(W1, b1, W2, sW1, sb1, sW2);   // once per block (syncs)
295	st.gate = sigmoid(accuracy);     // host scalar (FusedScalars.gate) — NO stage
296	TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
297	for (int t = q.next_block(&slot); t < ctx.n_tasks; t = q.next_block(&slot)) {
298	    int n = sizes[t];  int64 off = offsets[t];
299	    sg15_precompute_mu_for_tensor<32>(st.mu, grad, sharpness,
300	                                      sW1, sb1, sW2, b2, rescale, off, n);
301	    __syncthreads();   // mu(T) visible before the apply reads it (block-scope)
302	    apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15> over [off, off+n) (opt_components.cuh:240-244).
303	}
304	```
305	One drain, no grid barrier, no `sync_reset`.
306	```
307	
308	Same `sharpness` ABI gap as §4 (the FusedOptState lacks a sharpness field).
309	
310	---
311	
312	## 6. MODEL-COUPLED — looksam (`st.sam_dir` from the model stage)
313	
314	`looksam_apply_step` (`looksam.h:63-91`) reads `st.sam_dir`. On a SAM step
315	`sam_dir = g_sam − g` (`looksam.h:52-59`) where `g_sam` is the gradient at the
316	PERTURBED weights `p + rho·g/‖g‖` (`looksam.h:27-38`) — the output of a SECOND
317	model backward. A pure optimizer stage cannot produce it. There is therefore NO
318	looksam specialization of `optimizer_precompute_stage` by design.
319	
320	**Contract:** the MODEL STAGE fills `st.sam_dir` on SAM steps (every k steps),
321	mirroring the per-op LookSAM pipeline (perturb → 2nd backward → `set_direction`).
322	On intervening steps the cached `sam_dir` is reused verbatim (`looksam.h:1-19`).
323	`FusedOptState.sam_dir` (`opt_components.cuh:91`) already exists as the bound
324	input; the cell points it at the model-produced buffer. The wiring of the SAM
325	second backward into the megakernel's model phase is the model-stage owner's
326	responsibility (out of THIS phase's scope), tracked here as the explicit
327	contract so it is not silently dropped.
328	
329	---
330	
331	## 7. Determinism summary (no float atomics anywhere)
332	
333	| stage | reduction | determinism mechanism |
334	|-------|-----------|------------------------|
335	| prodigy d | cross-all-tensors `(r,s)` | per-CTA slot publish → barrier → ascending-index owner-sum (`owner_sum_slots`) |
336	| muon ‖buf‖_F | cross-CTA over one matrix | per-CTA slot publish → barrier → ascending owner-sum |
337	| muon matmul | k-dim contraction | one thread per output, ascending-k inner product |
338	| sg11 cosine gate | per-tensor `(num, den_g, den_m)` | in-CTA `block_reduce_sum_f32` tree (fixed thread count) |
339	
340	No `atomicAdd` on floats anywhere in `opt_stages_precompute.cuh`. The only
341	atomics are the substrate's integer task-counter and barrier-generation
342	(`megakernel_common.cuh`), which are order-independent.
343	
344	---
345	
346	## 8. Validation status (this phase)
347	
348	- **CPU fp64 mirrors:** `tests/hw/test_opt_stages.py` — prodigy d-reduction, SG11
349	  cosine gate, SG11/SG15 mu, and the muon 5-iteration Newton-Schulz chain, each

351	  `tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py` where correct). **9/9 pass.** fp32-vs-fp64

353	- **Math single-source drift guard:** `scripts/check_math_single_source.py` →
354	  OK (the stage CALLS the canonical `csrc/algorithms/*.h` fns, never re-inlines).
355	- **CUDA compile / GPU run:** DEFERRED per the NO-builds / NO-GPU-runs directive.
356	  The header is self-contained per `csrc/fused/COMPONENT_CONTRACT.md` (substrate
357	  + canonical algorithm headers + CUDA only); compiling it and wiring the cells
358	  is the integration step this spec describes.
359	
360	> ⚠ NOTE for the prodigy oracle: `tests/hw/test_reference_parity.py::
361	> ref_prodigy_partials` is STALE vs canonical `prodigy.h` (it uses `d_prev^1` and
362	> SIGNED `g`; the header uses `d_prev^2` and `fabsf(g)` — the L1 norm). The mirror

15	|------|----------------|-------|
16	| `scripts/compile_to_object.sh <tu.cu>` | nvcc `-c` to object, sm_90a cross-compile (no GPU) | all sm_90 CUDA TUs |

28	### Stage 0 — real-nvcc compilation prerequisite
29	De-inlined the textually-copy-pasted shared blocks (`platform.h`, `types.h`,
30	`affine2x2.h`, `utils.cuh`, `ptx_intrinsics.cuh`, `primitives.cuh`, `mma.cuh`,

34	real-nvcc build. Gate: 14/14 COMPILE_OK. Opus-reviewed (byte/semantic identity).
35	
36	### Stage 1 — close the 24 kernel stubs
37	- **1A SG2 CSA/HCA bilevel backward** — hand-written reverse-mode adjoint (NO
38	  autograd) through input_proj+sort → CSA → HCA → GRU → PEER → smart_grad; all
39	  24 weight-grad buffers. Shared vendor-neutral header
40	  `supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h`. **Opus-reviewed by full Python transcription
41	  vs `torch.autograd.grad`: all 24 buffers match to fp32 (max abs ≤6e-9).**

43	  Opus-reviewed: all 18 correct, backends equivalent.

45	  `mma::sm90_run_gemm_bt`. SASS-confirmed 64 HGMMA + 50 UTMALDG. Opus-reviewed.

77	clang 18's AMDGPU backend (no hipcc/ROCm needed). It caught real bugs the

90	- `grokking_optimizers/megakernel.py` — the automatic solver: per
91	  (model×opt×arch), reads ARCH_TABLE reg/smem budget, picks the highest fusion
92	  tier (L3→L2→L1→ERROR, §1.11). **Coverage: 53 L3 / 46 L1 / 0 infeasible.**

100	  (Phase 3 Stage 5): each `mega_<model>_<opt>` cell composes the real optimizer
101	  device-function component (`opt_components.{cuh,hip.hpp}` → `csrc/algorithms/
102	  <opt>.h`) with the real model-stage component (`model_stages.{cuh,hip.hpp}`)
103	  over the shared substrate (fwd→barrier→bwd→barrier→opt). sm_90 uses the
104	  warp-spec producer/consumer split. The toy `megakernel_demo.{cu,hip.hpp}` was
105	  DELETED — there is NO templated demo and NO TEMPLATE_ONLY / demo-include in any
106	  cell (anti-false-positive grep = 0). Gate: COMPILE_OK (nvcc -c) + AMDGCN_OK.

113	  (hipcc-gated 🟡), and `dispatch_fused_megakernel` (unified, tpu via

84	   PARENT, but the persistent `TimingWorker` subprocess was spawned earlier with a frozen

90	   raw-op call on a 1-D `(size,)`=(4096,) tensor via `_render_arg_construction`; the timing
91	   side-dump (`_TIMING_SCRIPT`) dumps `p` after warmup+iters `opt.step()` calls on a 2-D

94	   — it never produces a meaningful PASS.

111	  policy (the design choice).
112	- **(C) leave as-is** — fast-math/synth/etc. remain fail-closed (can't win) until a real
113	  GPU validation path exists; strict-only winners ship correctly.

7	## Verification method

9	The environment has **nvcc 12.0** (installed via pip wheels) and **CUTLASS
10	v3.6.0** (cloned to `third_party/cutlass`, gitignored), but **no GPU**.
11	
12	Key finding: the original production tree **does not compile in include order on
13	its own** — each `launch_<opt>.cu` uses `WARP_SIZE` / `GROK_CUDA` inside the
14	algorithm header it includes, but only `#define`s them *after* the include. So
15	"the build compiles cleanly today" was never literally true with a real nvcc;
16	the `--self-test` suite validates the Python pipeline (flags, search space, cache
17	schema, tree structure), **not** kernel compilation.
18	
19	Therefore the correct gate for a **byte-for-byte move** is **preprocessor
20	equivalence**: the thin `.cu` (header `#include`) must preprocess (`nvcc -E`)
21	to the exact same translation unit as the original `.cu`, modulo the embedded
22	`__FILE__` / `__LINE__` metadata inside torch's `TORCH_CHECK` macros. This was
23	proven for every CUDA TU (incl. SG2 with `-DWITH_CUTLASS`).

96	   (gates green, real fwd+bwd+opt in one persistent kernel) but not yet a throughput
97	   win here; closing the gap is a kernel redesign (batch-tiling / multi-CTA-per-
98	   tensor), not a tune. (Ratios are LOWER BOUNDS — clean eager is faster.)

100	   the scalar megakernel everywhere (decoder 2.71×, mamba 1.86×, vit 1.64×) AND
101	   beats *eager* on mamba (TC 1.504 vs eager 1.051 TF/s). On decoder/vit TC still

113	   co-resident; you cannot exceed one-per-SM without deadlocking the barrier.
114	   MIN_BLOCKS would require a recompile + full re-validation and would *cut*
115	   registers on a register-hungry kernel (likely harmful). No cheap knob closes the
116	   ~5× gap. The real task-3 content is the per-model scalar-vs-TC verdict above

1	# H100 Power / Profiling Investigation — Grokking Race
2	
3	**Question (user):** H100 has a 700 W limit; SG2 looked like only 200–300 W.
4	Is the race register-bound? Should `compile.py` change? Is SG2 a "glorified AdamW"?
5	
6	## TL;DR
7	1. **~235 W is a workload ceiling, not an SG2 defect.** *Every* optimizer —
8	   including plain AdamW (a single 44-reg kernel) — tops out at ~196–235 W mean /
9	   39–44 % GPU util on this task. The p=97 / ~420K-param / full-batch problem is
10	   far too small to fill an H100; the SMs sit ~60 % idle every step. 700 W is not
11	   reachable without changing the *workload* (bigger model/batch) or the
12	   *execution path* (see #3) — both change the race itself.
13	2. **Nothing on the race path is register-bound.** The fused *optimizer* kernels
14	   that actually run are 18–48 regs (AdamW/Lion/GrokAdamW) and SG2's are 27–40
15	   regs with ~1 KB smem — all high-occupancy. The "168 regs" figure is a **CUTLASS
16	   Sm90 WGMMA GEMM**, where ~168 regs is *optimal by design* for Hopper
17	   warp-specialized tensor cores (low occupancy is intentional, not a leak).
18	3. **`compile.py` / the 168-reg megakernel is NOT on the race path.** Verified:
19	   `dispatch._FUSED_REGISTRY` is empty → `has_fused()→False` → the race always
20	   falls back to **eager model + fused optimizer (the L1 path)**. The L3
21	   model×optimizer megacell is "compile-verified only" and the race "does not
22	   exercise" it (this is documented in HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md §"sm_90 update").
23	   So **editing `compile.py` would not change race power** — it tunes a kernel
24	   the race never launches.
25	4. **SG2 is not a glorified AdamW — it's a sophisticated optimizer with broken
26	   parts.** Its machinery is wired and the meta-net trains modestly/stably
27	   (|Δw|≈0.1, finite), but `sam_step` fails **100%** (grad bug → no SAM signal)
28	   and `bilevel_step` fails **~50%** (grads cleared by the failed SAM → meta
29	   trained at half cadence), and the **grokfast `lamb`** term then drives the
30	   update into a runaway collapse (8.7× anti-aligned by step 900). So "fully
31	   utilize SG2" is a *correctness/stability* problem (fix SAM, bilevel, `lamb`),
32	   not a power-tuning one. SG2 is **not** a low-power outlier — it runs at
33	   225 W / 99% util like the pack, just 18× slower because its step is a long
34	   chain of light memory-bound ops (its own machinery, §B).
35	
36	## A. Cross-optimizer sustained power (real race path, decoder, p=97)
37	Idle baseline ≈ 72 W.
38	
39	| optimizer | steps/s | mean W | p50 | max | util | J/step |
40	|-----------|--------:|-------:|----:|----:|-----:|-------:|
41	| AdamW     | 104.2 | 235 | 222 | 378 | 44% | 2.26 |
42	| Lion      |  81.3 | 218 | 216 | 261 | 42% | 2.69 |
43	| Muon      |  58.0 | 196 | 196 | 201 | 39% | 3.38 |
44	| GrokAdamW |  74.5 | 211 | 211 | 218 | 40% | 2.83 |
45	| Prodigy   |  79.2 | 218 | 218 | 229 | 40% | 2.75 |
46	| SuperGrok11 | 45.0 | 183 | 181 | 212 | 31% | 4.06 |
47	| SuperGrok15 | 54.3 | 196 | 195 | 204 | 36% | 3.61 |
48	| SuperGrok2  |  5.8 | 225 | 216 | 277 | **99%** | 38.60 |
49	
50	Read: the *fastest* optimizer draws the *most* power (AdamW packs more identical
51	work/sec). None breaks ~235 W. **SG2 is NOT a low-power outlier** — at 225 W it
52	sits with the pack, and its util is actually the *highest* (99%) because it runs
53	a long unbroken chain of ~20 light kernels per step; it's just 18× slower
54	(5.8 vs 104 steps/s) and burns 17× the energy/step. The H100 is "busy" but the
55	work per kernel is too small to draw real power. 700 W is a function of *work
56	size*, not optimizer choice.
57	
58	## A2. SG2's SAM + bilevel are BROKEN — meta-net never trains (likely)
59	During every SG2 run the loop logs (swallowed by try/except):
60	- `sam_step failed: element 0 of tensors does not require grad and does not have a grad_fn`
61	- `bilevel_step failed: SuperGrok2.bilevel_step() requires CUDA tensors` (really
62	  "no params have grads" — `any(p.is_cuda … if p.grad is not None)` over an empty
63	  set; grads were cleared by the failed sam_step that runs just before it).
64	
65	`bilevel_step` is the **only** path that trains the meta-net (`mopt =
66	Adam(meta_net.params)`; the C++ kernel only *reads* cached meta weights, it can't
67	autograd).
68	
69	**Direct verification (200–300 real SG2 steps, decoder):**
70	- `sam_step`:    **0/15 succeed** — raises `element 0 of tensors does not require
71	  grad and does not have a grad_fn` *every* time. Root cause (supergrok2.py:1751):
72	  `perturbed_params = p.detach() + rho·grad` are non-leaf, requires_grad=False, so
73	  `functional_call(...).backward()` has nothing to differentiate. This is a
74	  **pre-existing bug** (git-blamed to 6941457, 2026-06-02 — *not* introduced this
75	  session; this session's SG2 commits never touched sam_step), silently swallowed
76	  by the race loop's try/except, which is why the prior 8/11 race + green parity
77	  gates never surfaced it (parity tests the kernel, not the Python SAM). SG2 thus
78	  runs with **no SAM/sharpness signal at all**. Fix = the same one already applied
79	  to SuperGrok11's sam_step this session (`requires_grad_(True)` + `autograd.grad`,
80	  leave `p.grad` intact).
81	- `bilevel_step`: **5/10 succeed** — fails on exactly the steps where it fires
82	  right after the broken `sam_step`, which left the params grad-less. So the
83	  meta-net is trained at only ~half its intended cadence.
84	- meta-net **trainable weights train modestly and stably** — max |Δw| ≈ **0.10**
85	  over 200 steps (expert_W1/W2, product_keys), all finite. (An earlier 7e7
86	  "delta" was the `expert_counts` *int buffer*, a MoE activation counter, not a
87	  weight — corrected.) So the meta-net is **not** frozen and **not** diverging;
88	  it learns, just starved of the SAM input and half its bilevel updates.
89	
90	So SG2's machinery is wired and the meta-net trains, but **two components are
91	broken** (SAM 100% dead, bilevel half-dead) so it never runs at full capability,
92	and — independently — the **grokfast `lamb` term is the destabilizer** that drives
93	collapse (Part C: at step 900 the update is 8.7× Adam's and *anti-aligned*,
94	cos −0.74, with train_acc already collapsed to 0.014; and the prior isolation:
95	`lamb=0` → stable, test→0.948). This — **not** "glorified AdamW" — is why SG2
96	DNFs. "Fully utilize what it can do" = (1) fix the SAM grad bug, (2) stop bilevel
97	double-firing after SAM so it gets its full bilevel signal, (3) tame `lamb` so it
98	doesn't blow up — i.e. the SG2 fix + tuning (tasks #15/#17), with the Part-C
99	cosine/magnitude metric as the guardrail that the meta stays active but bounded.
100	
101	## B. Kernel trace — where the step goes
102	**AdamW** (top self-CUDA): `aten::mm` 18.9%, `layer_norm_backward` 12.9%,
103	`addmm` 12.8%, `GammaBetaBackward` 11.2%, `bmm` 10.2%, `gemmSN` 7.3%, `copy_`
104	7.0%, `xmma_gemm`/`cutlass_80_sgemm` ~12%. → the step is **dominated by the eager
105	model's GEMMs/layernorm** (sm80/cuBLAS/cutlass kernels, 40–68 µs each), not the
106	optimizer. These small GEMMs can't saturate Hopper tensor cores, so the SMs idle
107	between them (44% util). The fused AdamW kernel is a negligible slice.
108	
109	**SG2** (top self-CUDA): `Optimizer.step#SuperGrok2.step` **65.8%** (167 ms/step!),
110	`csa_hca::csa_indexer_topk_kernel` **20.7%** (3.5 ms each × ~15/step), then a soup
111	of tiny eager ops — `index_select` ×306/step, `mul` ×530/step, `topk`,
112	`scatter_add`, `mm` ×260/step. → SG2's cost is its **own machinery**, not the
113	model, and most of it is hundreds of light memory-bound ops + one slow indexer
114	kernel per step. That's the 18× slowdown and the 99%-util/225 W signature:
115	launch/latency-bound chains of small work, not register- or compute-bound.
116	
117	## C. SG2 meta-activity (full vs Adam-core alpha=0/lamb=0, matched state)
118	| step | train_acc | cos(full,adam) | \|full\|/\|adam\| | \|full−adam\|/\|adam\| |
119	|-----:|----------:|---------------:|------------------:|-----------------------:|
120	| 50   | 0.127 | **+1.0000** | 1.000 | **0.000** |
121	| 300  | 0.934 | +0.308 | 2.913 | 2.773 |
122	
123	**Caveat:** this Part-C probe never calls `bilevel_step`, so the meta-net sits at
124	zero-init *by construction* — §C isolates the **grokfast `lamb`** contribution, it
125	does **not** characterize the real-race meta contribution (in the real race
126	bilevel does train the meta, modestly — Δw≈0.1, §A2). Read that way: at step 50
127	the update is byte-identical to AdamW (lamb gate off, meta at zero-init); by
128	step 300 it diverges 2.9× exactly when the `lamb` gate switches on (train_acc>0.8);
129	by step 900 it is 8.7× and anti-aligned (cos −0.74) as `lamb` runs away → the
130	**`lamb` term is the destabilizer**, independent of the (modest, real-race) meta.
131	
132	## D. nsight compute — environment-blocked; substituted
133	`ncu` is installed but its **hardware counters are blocked**: `ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM`
134	even as root, because this is a Docker container with `RmProfilingAdminOnly=1`
135	and no way to reload the driver with `NVreg_RestrictProfilingToAdminUsers=0`.
136	`nsys` is not installed. (To enable on the host: set that module param + reload
137	the nvidia driver, then `ncu` gives SM/mem SoL + warp stall reasons.)
138	
139	Substituted with three host-side sources that answer the same questions:
140	- **cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage** (static, the real `_ops.so`): every
141	  on-race-path kernel's regs/smem → occupancy. AdamW/Lion/GrokAdamW 18–48 regs;
142	  SG2's csa/hca/moe/gru 27–40 regs, ~1 KB smem. **None register-bound.** The only
143	  168-reg kernels are CUTLASS Sm90 WGMMA GEMMs (optimal-by-design; off the race
144	  path anyway).
145	- **torch.profiler** (live kernel time, §B): names the bottleneck kernels and
146	  their per-step counts — the actual "where do the cycles go" that ncu's timeline
147	  would show.
148	- **NVML** (live power/util/clock, §A): the power ceiling + the 99%-util-yet-225W
149	  signature that says "busy on light work," not "stalled on a hot kernel."
150	
151	Verdict from the substitutes: SG2's slowness/power is **launch-count + light
152	memory-bound work**, not register pressure or compute saturation — so a
153	`maxrregcount`/occupancy change (what ncu would tune) is not the lever.
154	
155	## Utilization ≠ wattage — what each lever actually does
156	Key distinction: **higher util does not mean higher power.** SG2 already runs at
157	99% util / 225 W — busy, but on light work. The only way to approach 700 W is to
158	add *heavy* work (bigger GEMMs), which means a bigger problem.
159	- **Wire the L3 megakernel into the race** (one fused model×optimizer launch
160	  instead of eager-model kernels + ~20 optimizer micro-kernels): cuts launch
161	  overhead → **faster, higher util**, but **same ~235 W ceiling** (no new work).
162	  Also changes execution semantics + FLOPs accounting and risks numeric
163	  divergence from the validated eager+L1 path. Major task.
164	- **CUDA-graph the optimizer step** (collapse SG2's ~20 launches into one replay):
165	  **faster**, but again no new work → not more power; and SG2's dynamic control
166	  flow (expert recycling, alpha schedule) complicates capture.
167	- **Bigger model/batch** → more work → **the only lever that raises the power
168	  ceiling** — but that *is* changing the science/FLOPs of the race, so it's the
169	  user's call, not something to do silently.
